eyebrow: How Computers Work · 電腦概論
lead_en: We use computers every day, but how do they really do it? This series starts with a single switch and climbs, one question at a time, to programs, the internet, and AI.
lead_zh: 電腦天天在用，可是它到底怎麼做到的？這個系列從一個開關講起，一次回答一個問題，一路講到程式、網路和 AI。

intro.en: The whole series is one building that goes up floor by floor: bits, then logic, then the machine, then programs, then networks and AI. Each lesson stands on the one before it and explains a single idea, with a 3D model you can play with and a short English reading, with Chinese a tap away.
intro.zh: 整個系列像一棟一層一層往上蓋的樓：位元、邏輯、機器、程式，再到網路與 AI。每一課都站在上一課上面，只講清楚一件事：有一個可以動手玩的 3D 模型，再讀一篇英文短文把它說明白，中文翻譯隨點隨看。

intro.en: Every lesson also has one thing you can check on your own computer, so you can see that what the lesson says is real. Names, dates, and numbers are checked against the sources listed at the bottom of each lesson, and the models say plainly where a real computer is different.
intro.zh: 每一課還有一件可以在自己電腦上動手驗證的事，親眼看到課文講的是真的。人名、年代和數字都依每課最下方列出的資料查證；模型和真的電腦哪裡不一樣，也會說清楚。

units.blurb_en: Why a computer uses only two digits, how those digits turn into words, pictures, and sound, and how a few simple switches can make decisions and add numbers.
units.blurb_zh: 電腦為什麼只用兩個數字、這兩個數字怎麼變成文字、圖片和聲音，以及幾個簡單的開關怎麼做決定、做加法。

lessons.title: Why Do Computers Use Only 0 and 1?
lessons.title_zh: 電腦為什麼只用 0 和 1？
lessons.blurb_en: Flip eight switches in 3D and watch a row of light bulbs count from 0 to 255. Count to 31 on one hand, read numbers written in lights, and see why on and off are so hard to mix up.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡撥八個開關，看一排燈泡從 0 數到 255。用一隻手數到 31、讀出用燈寫的數字，再看看為什麼「開」和「關」最不容易弄錯。
lessons.big_idea_en: A computer is built from switches that are either off (0) or on (1). Two states are the hardest to mix up, and a row of switches can still count to very large numbers, because each switch is worth twice the one to its right.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電腦是用開關做成的，每個開關不是關（0）就是開（1）。兩種狀態最不容易弄錯；而一排開關照樣能數到很大的數，因為每個開關代表的數都是右邊那一個的兩倍。

lab.how_en: Tap any switch to flip it, and its light turns on or off. The switch on the far right is worth 1, and each one to the left is worth double: 2, 4, 8, and on up to 128. The panel adds up the lights that are on. Press +1 to add one, or Count up to keep adding, and watch the carry jump from right to left like falling dominoes.
lab.how_zh: 點任何一個開關把它撥過去，它的燈就亮或滅。最右邊的開關代表 1，往左每一個加倍：2、4、8，一直到 128。右邊會把亮著的燈加起來。按「+1」加一，或按「往上數」一直加，看進位像骨牌一樣從右往左跳過去。

legend.en: Light on: this place counts (1)
legend.zh: 燈亮：這一位算進去（1）

legend.en: Light off: this place does not count (0)
legend.zh: 燈滅：這一位不算（0）

legend.en: Switch lever: red knob toward you is off, green knob toward the bulb is on
legend.zh: 撥桿：紅色朝你這邊是關，綠色倒向燈泡是開

legend.en: Teal ball: a carry moving one place to the left
legend.zh: 青色小球：往左進一位

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. A real computer has no light bulbs and nobody flips its switches by hand: the switches are transistors on a chip, far too small to see, and they are turned on and off by electricity. The carry is slowed down here so that you can watch it. The numbers are exact: eight switches show every whole number from 0 to 255.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。真的電腦裡沒有燈泡，也沒有人用手去撥開關：那些開關是晶片上的電晶體，小到看不見，由電來控制開和關。這裡把進位放慢了，好讓你看得見。數字是精確的：八個開關可以表示 0 到 255 的每一個整數。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The counting rules are tested in tools/computers/test/bits.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；數數的規則有自動測試（tools/computers/test/bits.test.mjs）。

paras: Your phone or computer can show photos, play songs, and send messages around the world. But if you could look deep inside its chips, you would not find any pictures, sounds, or letters. You would find switches: billions of them on a single chip, each one far too small to see. Every switch can be in only one of two states, off or on. We write off as 0 and on as 1. Everything a computer does, from games to video calls, is built out of these two digits.

One switch holds the smallest piece of information there is: a single 0 or 1. It is called a bit, which is short for “binary digit.” Binary means “made of two parts.” The mathematician John Tukey suggested the word, and Claude Shannon used it in 1948 in a famous paper about sending messages. One bit cannot say much. It can answer only one yes-or-no question: Is the light on? Is the door open?

A row of bits can say much more. Think about how we normally count. We have ten digits, 0 to 9. When we run out, we carry into a new place, and each place is worth ten times the one to its right: ones, tens, hundreds. Binary works the same way with only two digits, so each place is worth two times the one to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and so on. To read a row of switches, add up the places that are on. The row 1101 means 8 + 4 + 1, which is 13.

Counting up is simple, too. To add one, flip the switch on the far right. If it was off, it turns on, and you are done. If it was already on, it turns off and passes a carry to the switch on its left, which does the same thing. The carry can run down the row like falling dominoes: 0111 is 7, and one more makes 1000, which is 8. With eight switches you can count from 0 to 255. Eight bits together are called a byte. Every switch you add doubles how far you can count.

Why two states and not ten? A computer could try to use ten levels of voltage, one for each digit. But electrical signals are never perfectly steady. There is always a little unwanted wobble, called noise. With ten levels packed close together, a small wobble could make a 6 look like a 7. With only two levels, far apart, the signal has to change a lot before off could be mistaken for on. Engineers have tried other ways: ENIAC, an early American computer, counted in tens, and a Soviet computer called Setun used three states. Nearly every computer today uses two.

The idea is much older than computers. The German thinker Gottfried Leibniz had worked out binary numbers by 1679, and in 1703 he wrote an article explaining how to do arithmetic with only 0 and 1. In it he also described something a French missionary in Beijing, Joachim Bouvet, had noticed: the six-line figures in the ancient Chinese Book of Changes match binary numbers, if a whole line is read as 1 and a broken line as 0. Much later, as a student at MIT, Claude Shannon showed that circuits made of switches could carry out logic. Today those switches are transistors on a chip. They are tiny and fast, but each one still does what the lights in the model do: off or on, 0 or 1.
paras_zh: 你的手機或電腦可以顯示照片、播放歌曲，還能把訊息傳到世界各地。可是如果你能看進晶片的最裡面，你不會找到任何圖片、聲音或文字。你會找到開關：一顆晶片上就有幾十億個，每一個都小到看不見。每個開關只有兩種狀態，不是關就是開。我們把關寫成 0，把開寫成 1。電腦做的每一件事，從遊戲到視訊通話，都是用這兩個數字搭起來的。
一個開關存的是最小的一份資訊：一個 0 或一個 1。它叫做「位元」（bit），是 binary digit（二進位數字）的縮寫。binary 的意思是「由兩個部分組成」。這個詞是數學家約翰・圖基（John Tukey）建議的，克勞德・夏農（Claude Shannon）1948 年在一篇談怎麼傳送訊息的著名論文裡用了它。一個位元說不了多少事，它只能回答一個「是或不是」的問題：燈亮著嗎？門開著嗎？
一排位元能說的就多得多了。想想我們平常怎麼數數。我們有十個數字，0 到 9；用完了就進到新的一位，每一位代表的數是右邊那一位的十倍：個位、十位、百位。二進位的道理一樣，只是數字只有兩個，所以每一位代表的數是右邊那一位的兩倍：1、2、4、8、16……要讀一排開關，把開著的那幾位加起來就好。1101 這一排是 8＋4＋1，也就是 13。
往上數也很簡單。要加一，就去撥最右邊的開關。它本來是關的，就打開，結束。它本來就開著，就關掉，並且向左邊的開關進一位，左邊的開關再照同樣的規則做。進位可以像骨牌一樣一路傳下去：0111 是 7，再加一變成 1000，就是 8。八個開關可以從 0 數到 255。八個位元合起來叫做一個「位元組」（byte）。每多一個開關，能數的範圍就加倍。

為什麼是兩種狀態，不是十種？電腦可以試著用十種高低不同的電壓，每一種代表一個數字。可是電的訊號從來不會完全平穩，總是有一點不想要的晃動，叫做「雜訊」。十種電壓擠在一起時，一點點晃動就可能讓 6 看起來像 7。只有兩種、而且離得很遠時，訊號要變很多，才可能把關看成開。工程師也試過別的做法：美國早期的電腦 ENIAC 用十進位計數，蘇聯有一台叫 Setun 的電腦用三種狀態。今天幾乎所有的電腦都用兩種。

這個想法比電腦老得多。德國學者萊布尼茲（Gottfried Leibniz）在 1679 年就已經把二進位弄清楚了，1703 年寫了一篇文章，說明怎麼只用 0 和 1 做算術。他在文章裡也提到在北京的法國傳教士白晉（Joachim Bouvet）注意到的一件事：中國古老的《易經》裡六條線組成的卦，和二進位的數對得起來：把完整的線讀成 1，斷開的線讀成 0。很久以後，克勞德・夏農在麻省理工學院當學生時證明，用開關接成的電路可以做邏輯運算。今天這些開關是晶片上的電晶體，又小又快，但每一個做的事還是和模型裡的燈一樣：關或開，0 或 1。
questions: What is a bit, and what two values can it have?
How do you find the number that a row of switches shows?
Why is it safer for a computer to use two levels of electricity than ten?
answers: A bit is the smallest piece of information, held by one switch. It is short for “binary digit,” and it can be only 0 (off) or 1 (on).
The place on the far right is worth 1, and each place to the left is worth double. Add up the places whose switches are on. For example, 1101 is 8 + 4 + 1 = 13.

Electrical signals always have a little noise. Ten levels are close together, so a small wobble can turn one digit into another. Two levels are far apart, so a small wobble does not change off into on.

vocab.ex: Flip the switch by the door to turn on the light.
vocab.exzh: 撥一下門邊的開關，把燈打開。

vocab.ex: In binary counting, there are only two digits: 0 and 1.
vocab.exzh: 二進位的數法只有兩個數字：0 和 1。

vocab.ex: The number 255 has three digits.
vocab.exzh: 255 這個數有三個數字。

vocab.ex: A bit is either 0 or 1, and nothing in between.
vocab.exzh: 一個位元不是 0 就是 1，沒有中間的。

vocab.ex: One byte is made of eight bits.
vocab.exzh: 一個位元組由八個位元組成。

vocab.ex: When you add 9 and 1, you carry a one into the tens place.
vocab.exzh: 9 加 1 的時候，要進一位到十位。

vocab.ex: The phone lost its signal inside the tunnel.
vocab.exzh: 手機在隧道裡收不到訊號。

vocab.ex: Electrical noise made the old radio hiss.
vocab.exzh: 電的雜訊讓那台舊收音機發出嘶嘶聲。

quiz.q: What is “bit” short for?
In a row of switches, the one on the far right is worth 1. What is the fourth switch from the right worth?
What number does the row 1101 show?
What is the largest number that eight switches can show?
According to the reading, why do computers use two states instead of ten?
options: Two states are harder to mix up when there is noise.
Ten states would use too many colors.
People can only count to two.
Light bulbs come in only two sizes.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the rightmost switch flip off, on, off, on. That is everything one bit can say.
parts.text_zh: 看最右邊的開關關、開、關、開。一個位元能說的就這麼多。

parts.text_en: One light at a time, from right to left. How much is each switch worth by itself?
parts.text_zh: 由右往左，一次只亮一盞。每個開關自己代表多少？

parts.text_en: Seven lights are on. Add one in slow motion and count how many switches have to move.
parts.text_zh: 七盞燈亮著。用慢動作加一，數數看有幾個開關要動。

parts.meta_en: 255 is the limit of eight switches
parts.text_en: All eight on makes 255. What happens when you add one more and there is no ninth switch?
parts.text_zh: 八個全開是 255。再加一，可是沒有第九個開關，會怎樣？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then press Count up and let the row run. Which light changes every single time, and which one almost never does?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 最後按「往上數」讓它自己跑。哪一盞燈每一次都在變？哪一盞幾乎不動？

fingers.lead_en: Counting the usual way, one hand gets you to 5. Counting in binary, each finger is a switch: the thumb is worth 1, then 2, 4, 8, and 16. Tap the fingers to raise or lower them. All five up is 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 31.
fingers.lead_zh: 照平常的數法，一隻手只能數到 5。用二進位來數，每根手指就是一個開關：拇指代表 1，接著是 2、4、8、16。點手指把它舉起來或放下。五根全舉起來是 16＋8＋4＋2＋1＝31。
fingers.hand_en: A right hand with the palm facing you: the thumb, worth 1, is on the right, just like the row of lights.
fingers.hand_zh: 右手，手心朝自己：代表 1 的拇指在右邊，和那一排燈一樣。

tips.en: Five fingers make 32 different patterns, from 0 (a fist) to 31.
tips.zh: 五根手指有 32 種比法，從 0（握拳）到 31。

tips.en: With both hands you have ten switches: 0 to 1,023.
tips.zh: 兩隻手就有十個開關：0 到 1,023。

tips.en: In class, lay your hand flat on the desk and lift fingers a little. It is easier, and nobody mistakes a number for a gesture.
tips.zh: 上課時把手平放在桌上，手指稍微翹起來就好：比較好比，也不會有人把數字看成手勢。

guess.lead_en: Eight rows of lights, from four lights up to eight. Choose the number each row shows. The game counts how many you get right on the first try.
guess.lead_zh: 八排燈，從四盞到八盞。選出每一排代表的數；遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾題。

levels.en: Why Not Ten Levels of Brightness?
levels.lead_en: Imagine sending the digits 0 to 9 as ten levels of brightness, and sending 0 and 1 as just off and on. Each dot is one signal after a little random noise has pushed it left or right. A signal is read as whichever level it lands closest to. Slide the noise up and compare.
levels.lead_zh: 想像用十段亮度來送 0 到 9，另一邊只用關和開來送 0 和 1。每個點是一個訊號，被一點隨機的雜訊往左或往右推了一下；它落在離哪一段最近，就被讀成哪一段。把雜訊往上拉，比比看。
levels.note_en: This is an illustration, not a measurement of a real circuit. The noise here is random and evenly spread, and both rows get exactly the same noise. With ten levels, each level sits 1/18 of the full range (about 5.6%) from its border; with two levels, each sits one half (50%) away, nine times as far.
levels.note_zh: 這是示意，不是真實電路的量測。這裡的雜訊是均勻的隨機數，兩排受到的雜訊完全相同。十段時，每一段離界線是全幅的 1/18（約 5.6%）；兩段時是一半（50%），是前者的九倍。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind 0 and 1 · 0 和 1 的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A new word, an old book, eight bits, and two exceptions
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個新詞、一本古書、八個位元、兩個例外
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about where binary came from.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於二進位從哪裡來的四個小故事。

cards.k: A New Word · 一個新詞
cards.en: Who named the bit?
cards.body_en: In 1948 Claude Shannon, an engineer at Bell Labs, published “A Mathematical Theory of Communication.” In it he wrote that units of information measured in base 2 “may be called binary digits, or more briefly bits, a word suggested by J. W. Tukey.” Tukey was a statistician who worked with him. The next sentence of the paper could describe the model on this page: a device with two stable positions can store one bit.
cards.body_zh: 1948 年，貝爾實驗室的工程師克勞德・夏農發表〈通訊的數學理論〉。他在文中寫道，以 2 為底來量資訊時，單位「可以叫做 binary digits，或更簡短地叫 bits，這個詞是 J. W. Tukey 建議的」。圖基是和他共事的統計學家。論文的下一句簡直就是在講這一頁的模型：一個有兩種穩定位置的裝置，可以存一個位元。

cards.k: An Old Book · 一本古書
cards.en: Leibniz, Bouvet, and the Book of Changes
cards.body_en: People often say that binary came from the Book of Changes (Yijing, or I Ching). The order was the other way around. Leibniz had worked out binary numbers by March 1679. In February 1701 he explained them in a letter to Joachim Bouvet, a Jesuit missionary in China. Bouvet wrote back from Beijing in November 1701 that the hexagrams matched Leibniz’s numbers, and sent a chart of all 64. In his 1703 article, Leibniz explained how to read them: a whole line means 1, and a broken line means 0. The article was printed in 1705.
cards.body_zh: 常有人說二進位是從《易經》來的，其實先後順序正好相反。萊布尼茲在 1679 年 3 月就已經把二進位的數弄清楚了。1701 年 2 月，他寫信給在中國的耶穌會傳教士白晉（Joachim Bouvet），說明自己的二進位。白晉 1701 年 11 月從北京回信，說卦和萊布尼茲的數對得起來，還附上六十四卦的圖。萊布尼茲在 1703 年的文章裡說明怎麼讀：一條完整的線代表 1，一條斷開的線代表 0。這篇文章 1705 年印行。

cards.en: Why is a byte eight bits?
cards.zh: 為什麼一個位元組是八個位元？
cards.body_en: It was not always so. At first, a byte meant any short string of bits that made up one simple piece of information, such as a single character, and there were four-bit and six-bit bytes. In time the standard settled on eight. Eight bits give 256 patterns, so one byte can stand for a number from 0 to 255, exactly what the eight switches in the model show.
cards.body_zh: 並不是一開始就這樣。起初，byte 指的是組成一小份資訊（例如一個字元）的一小串位元，有四個位元的，也有六個位元的；後來標準才定在八個。八個位元有 256 種排法，所以一個位元組可以代表 0 到 255 的一個數，正好就是模型裡那八個開關能表示的範圍。

cards.en: Computers that did not count in twos
cards.body_en: ENIAC, built at the University of Pennsylvania and formally dedicated on February 15, 1946, worked in base 10, not base 2. At Moscow State University, a small computer named Setun was finished in December 1958. It was built on three-valued logic instead of two, and about 50 were made before production stopped in 1965. Both machines worked. Two-state designs still became the standard.
cards.body_zh: 在賓州大學建造、1946 年 2 月 15 日正式啟用的 ENIAC，用的是十進位，不是二進位。在莫斯科大學，一台叫 Setun 的小型電腦於 1958 年 12 月完成，它用的是三值邏輯而不是二值，一共造了大約 50 台，1965 年停產。這兩種機器都能運作，但後來成為標準的還是兩種狀態的設計。

myths.myth_en: There are tiny 0s and 1s written inside a computer.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦裡面寫著一個一個小小的 0 和 1。
myths.fact_en: There are no numerals inside. 0 and 1 are our names for two states of a switch. In computer memory, for example, a 1 is a high voltage and a 0 is a low voltage.
myths.fact_zh: 裡面沒有數字。0 和 1 是我們替開關的兩種狀態取的名字；以電腦的記憶體來說，1 是高電壓，0 是低電壓。

myths.myth_en: With only 0 and 1, a computer can handle only small numbers.
myths.myth_zh: 只有 0 和 1，電腦只能處理很小的數。
myths.fact_en: Every extra bit doubles the count. Eight bits reach 255, sixteen bits reach 65,535, and thirty-two bits give more than four billion patterns (4,294,967,296).
myths.fact_zh: 每多一個位元，能數的範圍就加倍。8 個位元數到 255，16 個位元數到 65,535，32 個位元有四十多億種排法（4,294,967,296）。

myths.myth_en: Binary is a different kind of math.
myths.myth_zh: 二進位是另一種數學。
myths.fact_en: It is the same numbers, written a different way. Thirteen is still thirteen whether you write 13 or 1101, and adding works by the same rule: when a place is full, carry to the left.
myths.fact_zh: 數還是同樣的數，只是寫法不同。十三不管寫成 13 還是 1101 都是十三；加法的規則也一樣：這一位滿了，就往左進位。

myths.myth_en: Binary was copied from the Book of Changes.
myths.myth_zh: 二進位是從《易經》抄來的。
myths.fact_en: Leibniz had worked out binary numbers by 1679. The link to the hexagrams was pointed out to him by Joachim Bouvet, in a letter written in Beijing in 1701 that reached him in 1703.
myths.fact_zh: 萊布尼茲 1679 年就已經把二進位弄清楚了。卦和二進位的關聯，是白晉 1701 年從北京寫信告訴他的，信到 1703 年才收到。

tricks.body_en: One switch, two states, one bit.
tricks.body_zh: 一個開關、兩種狀態，就是一個位元。

tricks.body_en: 1101 is 8 + 4 + 1 = 13. Skip the places that are off.
tricks.body_zh: 1101 就是 8＋4＋1＝13，沒亮的那一位跳過。

tricks.title_en: One more switch, twice as far
tricks.body_en: Five switches reach 31, eight reach 255, and ten reach 1,023.
tricks.body_zh: 五個開關數到 31，八個數到 255，十個數到 1,023。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: The switches in the model are drawings. Never open a wall switch, a socket, or a plugged-in device to look inside: household electricity can kill.
safety.zh: 模型裡的開關是畫出來的。千萬不要拆開牆上的開關、插座或插著電的電器來看：家裡的電會致命。

safety.en: If your class builds a real circuit with a bulb and a switch, use small batteries only, and never the wall socket.
safety.zh: 如果班上要用燈泡和開關接真的電路，只能用小電池，絕對不要用牆上的插座。

safety.en: When you count on your fingers, keep your hand flat on the desk and lift the fingers just a little, so that a number is not mistaken for a gesture.
safety.zh: 用手指數數時，把手平放在桌上，手指稍微翹起來就好，免得數字被看成手勢。

safety.en: In the computer activity, you only open the calculator and look. You do not need to change any settings or install anything.
safety.zh: 電腦上的活動只要打開計算機來看，不需要改任何設定，也不用安裝任何東西。

materials.en: Five large cards with the numbers 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1
materials.zh: 五張大卡片，分別寫 16、8、4、2、1

materials.en: Five chairs in a row at the front of the room
materials.zh: 教室前面排成一排的五張椅子

materials.en: A tally sheet on the board
materials.zh: 黑板上的一張計數表

steps.en: Five students sit facing the class and hold the cards so that the class reads 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 from left to right. Sitting means off (0). Standing means on (1).
steps.zh: 五位同學面向全班坐好，拿著卡片，讓全班從左到右看到 16、8、4、2、1。坐著是關（0），站著是開（1）。

steps.en: The teacher calls a number from 0 to 31. The five students stand or sit to show it, and the class adds up the standing cards to check.
steps.zh: 老師說一個 0 到 31 的數，五位同學用站或坐把它比出來，全班把站著的卡片加起來檢查。

steps.en: Now start from 0 and count up one at a time. The student holding 1 changes on every count. Everyone else follows one rule: change only when the neighbor holding the smaller card sits down.
steps.zh: 接著從 0 開始，一次加一往上數。拿 1 的同學每數一次就變一次；其他人只守一條規則：拿比你小的那張卡的鄰居坐下的時候，你才變。

steps.en: Count all the way to 31. On the board, tally how many times each student stood up or sat down.
steps.zh: 一路數到 31。在黑板上記下每位同學站起來或坐下一共幾次。

activities.tip_en: The tally should come out as 31, 15, 7, 3, and 1, from the 1 card to the 16 card: each place changes half as often as the one before it. Each student watches only one neighbor, and that is all a carry is. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson fits the topic “Data representation, processing, and analysis” (learning content 資 D-IV-2, whose notes list binary data representation).
activities.tip_zh: 記下來應該是 31、15、7、3、1（從拿 1 的到拿 16 的）：每一位變的次數大約是前一位的一半。每個人只要看一位鄰居，這就是進位。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課屬於「資料表示、處理及分析」主題（資 D-IV-2 數位資料的表示方法；附錄的學習內容說明列有「二進位資料表示法」）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A Windows or Mac computer
materials.zh: 一台 Windows 或 Mac 電腦

materials.en: The Calculator app that comes with it
materials.zh: 電腦內建的「計算機」

materials.en: This page, open at the 3D model
materials.zh: 這一頁，捲到 3D 模型

steps.en: Open Calculator and switch to the programmer calculator. On a Mac, choose View > Programmer (or press Command-3), then click Show Binary. On Windows, open the menu at the top left of Calculator and choose Programmer.
steps.zh: 打開「計算機」，切換到程式設計人員用的計算機。Mac：選「顯示方式」＞「程式設計」（或按 Command-3），再按「顯示二進位」。Windows：打開計算機左上角的選單，選「程式設計人員」。

steps.en: Make sure it is set to decimal (DEC, or 10 on a Mac), and type 13. Read the binary line: it should say 1101. Set the model to 13 and compare the lights.
steps.zh: 確定它設在十進位（DEC；Mac 上是 10），輸入 13。看二進位那一行，應該是 1101。把模型也撥成 13，比一比燈。

steps.en: Type 255. How many 1s do you see? Then type 256. What changed?
steps.zh: 輸入 255，你看到幾個 1？再輸入 256，哪裡變了？

steps.en: Pick three numbers of your own. Write each one in binary on paper first, then check your answer with the calculator.
steps.zh: 自己選三個數，先在紙上寫出二進位，再用計算機對答案。

activities.tip_en: 255 is eight 1s, and 256 is a 1 followed by eight 0s: the calculator has a ninth switch, and the model does not. For a second check, open any web browser’s developer console, type (13).toString(2), and press Enter. It answers “1101.” The names of the menus may differ a little in other versions of Windows and macOS.
activities.tip_zh: 255 是八個 1；256 是一個 1 後面接八個 0：計算機有第九個開關，模型沒有。還有第二種驗證法：打開任何瀏覽器的開發人員主控台，輸入 (13).toString(2) 再按 Enter，它會回答 "1101"。不同版本的 Windows 和 macOS，選單的名稱可能略有不同。

links_head.en: The switch itself, where bits are kept, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 開關本身、位元存在哪裡，以及下一課

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體・第二課
links.en: What Does a Transistor Do?
links.note_en: The switches in a real computer are transistors. See how a tiny voltage turns one on and off, with nothing moving at all.
links.note_zh: 真的電腦裡的開關是電晶體。看看一個小小的電壓怎麼讓它開和關，而且沒有任何東西在動。

links.en: How Does a Computer Remember Things?
links.note_en: Once you have 0s and 1s, where do you keep them? Follow the bits into memory chips and drives.
links.note_zh: 有了 0 和 1，要存在哪裡？跟著位元走進記憶體晶片和硬碟。

links.en: How Do 0s and 1s Become Words, Pictures, and Sound?
links.zh: 0 和 1 怎麼變成文字、圖片和聲音？
links.note_en: A row of bits is only a number. Next: how everyone agreed on tables that turn numbers into letters, colors, and sounds.
links.note_zh: 一排位元只是一個數。下一課要看：大家怎麼約好幾張對照表，把數變成字、顏色和聲音。

sources.en: “Bit” is shortened from “binary digit”; in computer memory, 1 is a high voltage and 0 is a low voltage
sources.zh: bit 是 binary digit 的縮寫；在電腦記憶體裡 1 是高電壓、0 是低電壓
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “bit”

sources.en: “…binary digits, or more briefly bits, a word suggested by J. W. Tukey”; a device with two stable positions stores one bit (1948)
sources.zh: 「bits，這個詞是 J. W. Tukey 建議的」；有兩種穩定位置的裝置可以存一個位元（1948）
sources.src: C. E. Shannon, “A Mathematical Theory of Communication,” Bell System Technical Journal 27 (1948), p. 1 of the reprint

sources.en: Shannon’s 1948 paper appears to contain the first published use of “bit”; his MIT master’s thesis used Boolean algebra to lay the foundations of digital circuits
sources.zh: 夏農 1948 年的論文看來是 bit 一詞最早的發表用例；他在麻省理工的碩士論文用布林代數奠定數位電路的基礎
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Claude Shannon”

sources.en: A byte is 8 bits; early bytes had four or six bits before the standard settled on eight; a byte can represent a number from 0 to 255
sources.zh: 一個位元組是 8 個位元；早期有 4 或 6 個位元的 byte，後來標準定為 8；一個位元組可以表示 0 到 255
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “byte”

sources.en: The binary system needs only the two symbols 0 and 1; it matters to computing because 0s and 1s can be represented compactly and reliably by two-state devices (“on-off”)
sources.zh: 二進位只需要 0 和 1 兩個符號；它對電腦重要，是因為 0 和 1 可以用兩種狀態的裝置（開／關）精簡而可靠地表示
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “binary number system”

sources.en: Telling many closely spaced voltage levels apart is impractical because of noise, which is why digital systems use bits
sources.zh: 要分辨很多個靠得很近的電壓並不實際（有雜訊），所以數位系統用位元
sources.src: MIT OpenCourseWare, 6.004 Computation Structures (Spring 2017), “The Digital Abstraction,” annotated slides

sources.en: Leibniz’s 1703 article in English: “I use no other characters in it bar 0 and 1”; “a whole line means unity, or 1,” and “a broken line means zero, or 0”; Bouvet recognized “the key to the figures of Fuxi”
sources.zh: 萊布尼茲 1703 年文章的英譯：只用 0 和 1 兩個符號；完整的線代表 1、斷開的線代表 0；白晉認出這是伏羲卦圖的鑰匙
sources.src: G. W. Leibniz, “Explanation of Binary Arithmetic” (1703), translated by Lloyd Strickland, Leibniz Translations

sources.en: “In March 1679 he perfected the binary system of numeration”
sources.zh: 「1679 年 3 月，他完成了二進位記數法」
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz”

sources.en: Leibniz’s binary manuscript of March 15, 1679; his letter to Bouvet of February 15, 1701; Bouvet’s reply from Beijing in November 1701, received April 1, 1703; the “Explication de l’arithmétique binaire,” printed in 1705
sources.zh: 萊布尼茲 1679 年 3 月 15 日的二進位手稿；1701 年 2 月 15 日致白晉的信；白晉 1701 年 11 月自北京的回信（1703 年 4 月 1 日收到）；〈二進位算術的解說〉1705 年印行

sources.zh: ENIAC 的架構是十進位而非二進位；1946 年 2 月 15 日在摩爾學院正式啟用
sources.src: Engineering and Technology History Wiki (ETHW), “ENIAC”

sources.zh: Setun：1956 年起在莫斯科大學設計，1958 年 12 月完成，採用三值邏輯，共生產 50 台

lessons.title: How Do 0s and 1s Become Words, Pictures, and Sound?
lessons.title_zh: 0 和 1 怎麼變成文字、圖片和聲音？
lessons.blurb_en: Walk up to a wall of pixels in 3D, read the three numbers behind one colored square, and change its color with the eight switches from Lesson 1. Type a character to see its number, draw a picture with 64 bits, and turn a sound wave into a list of numbers.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡走近一面像素牆，讀出一個彩色方塊背後的三個數，再用第一課的八個開關改它的顏色。打一個字看它的編號、用 64 個位元畫一張圖，再把一段聲波變成一串數。
lessons.big_idea_en: Bits can only make numbers. To turn numbers into words, pictures, and sound, people agree on codes: tables that say which number stands for which letter, which color, or how high a sound wave is. The same bits mean different things under different codes.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 位元只能組成數。要把數變成文字、圖片和聲音，靠的是大家約好的「編碼」：一張對照表，規定哪個數代表哪個字、哪個顏色，或聲波有多高。同樣的位元，照不同的表來讀，意思就不一樣。

lab.how_en: The wall is a picture made of 256 squares, called pixels. Tap any square to pick it. The three bars show the three numbers that make its color: how much red, green, and blue, each from 0 to 255. The eight switches in front are the ones from Lesson 1, and they hold one of those numbers. Flip a switch and the pixel changes color. Use Far and Close to see the wall as a picture or as squares.
lab.how_zh: 這面牆是一張由 256 個方塊拼成的圖，每個方塊叫做一個像素。點任何一個方塊就選到它。三根柱子是組成它顏色的三個數：紅、綠、藍各有多少，各從 0 到 255。前面的八個開關就是第一課那八個，存著其中一個數；撥一個開關，像素的顏色就跟著變。按「遠看」和「近看」，看看這面牆什麼時候像一張圖、什麼時候是一格一格的方塊。
lab.total_en: This picture: 16 × 16 = 256 pixels × 3 numbers × 8 bits = 6,144 bits (768 bytes).
lab.total_zh: 這張圖：16 × 16＝256 個像素 × 3 個數 × 8 個位元＝6,144 個位元（768 個位元組）。

legend.en: One square on the wall: one pixel, one flat color
legend.zh: 牆上的一個方塊：一個像素，只有一種顏色

legend.en: Three bars: the pixel’s red, green, and blue, each a number from 0 to 255
legend.zh: 三根柱子：這個像素的紅、綠、藍，各是 0 到 255 的一個數

legend.en: Eight switches: the eight bits of the number you chose
legend.zh: 八個開關：你選的那個數的八個位元

legend.en: White frame and white line: the pixel you picked, and the color its three numbers mix into
legend.zh: 白框與白線：你選的像素，以及它的三個數混出來的顏色

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The picture is tiny on purpose: 256 pixels, where a phone screen has millions. A real pixel is not a painted square; on a screen, each pixel is made of three small dots that give off red, green, and blue light, and the numbers set how brightly each one glows. The bars and switches are drawings that show the numbers; inside a computer they are bits in memory. The arithmetic is exact, and the colors are the ones a web browser shows for the same three numbers.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。圖故意做得很小：只有 256 個像素，手機螢幕則有幾百萬個。真正的像素不是塗上顏色的方塊；在螢幕上，每個像素由三個會發出紅、綠、藍光的小點組成，那三個數決定每個小點多亮。柱子和開關是把數畫出來的示意，在電腦裡它們是記憶體裡的位元。算術是精確的，顏色也就是瀏覽器遇到同樣三個數時顯示的顏色。
lab.credit_html:
Model, picture, and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The codes and counts are tested in tools/computers/test/codes.test.mjs.
模型、圖與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；編號與數量有自動測試（tools/computers/test/codes.test.mjs）。

paras: In Lesson 1, a row of switches could show a number, and nothing else. But a computer shows you words and photos, and it plays music. How can numbers do all that? The answer is an agreement. People decide that a certain number will stand for a certain thing, and they write the agreement down in a table. Such a table is called a code. Once everyone uses the same code, any computer can turn numbers back into the same letters, colors, and sounds.

Start with letters. In 1963, American computer makers agreed on a code called ASCII. It uses seven bits, so it has room for 128 characters: the English letters, the digits, punctuation marks, and a few signals for machines. In ASCII, the capital letter A is number 65, B is 66, and a lowercase a is 97. When you press A on a keyboard, the computer does not store the shape of the letter. It stores 65, which in bits is 1000001.

But 128 characters are not enough for the world. For years, different places made their own codes, and the same number could mean different characters on different computers. Text opened with the wrong code turned into nonsense. Unicode fixes this with one giant table for every writing system. The 2026 version, Unicode 18.0, lists 172,808 characters. The Chinese character 永 is number 27,704, usually written U+6C38. Most web pages store these numbers with a method called UTF-8, which uses one byte for an English letter and three bytes for a common Chinese character such as 永.

Pictures work the same way. A picture on a screen is a grid of tiny squares called pixels, and each pixel has just one color. That color is stored as three numbers: how much red, how much green, and how much blue. Each number usually gets one byte, so it runs from 0 to 255. Red 255, green 0, blue 0 is pure red. Three bytes give 16,777,216 possible colors. A photo 4,000 pixels wide and 3,000 pixels tall has 12 million pixels, so before any shrinking it needs 36 million bytes.

Sound becomes numbers, too. A microphone turns sound into an electrical wave that rises and falls. A computer measures the height of that wave again and again, at equal steps of time, and writes down each measurement as a number. This is called sampling. For a music CD, the wave is measured 44,100 times every second, and each measurement is a 16-bit number. To play the music, the computer reads the numbers back in order and a speaker rebuilds the wave.

Here is the surprising part: the bits themselves do not say what they are. The eight bits 01000001 can be the number 65, the letter A, or a dim shade of red. Nothing in the bits tells you which. The meaning comes from the code that the computer uses to read them. That is why a photo opened as if it were text looks like nonsense. Everything in a computer is numbers, plus an agreement about what the numbers mean.
paras_zh: 在第一課，一排開關能表示一個數，也只能表示一個數。可是電腦會顯示文字和照片，還會播放音樂。數怎麼做得到這些事？答案是「約定」。人們決定某個數代表某樣東西，並且把這個約定寫成一張表。這樣的表叫做「編碼」。只要大家都用同一套編碼，任何一台電腦都能把數變回同樣的字、顏色和聲音。
先說字。1963 年，美國的電腦廠商約定了一套叫 ASCII 的編碼。它用七個位元，所以容得下 128 個字元：英文字母、數字、標點符號，還有幾個給機器用的訊號。在 ASCII 裡，大寫的 A 是 65 號，B 是 66 號，小寫的 a 是 97 號。你在鍵盤上按 A 的時候，電腦存的不是這個字母的形狀，而是 65，寫成位元就是 1000001。

可是 128 個字元不夠全世界用。有很多年，不同的地方各自訂了自己的編碼，同一個數在不同的電腦上可能代表不同的字；用錯編碼打開的文字，就變成一堆看不懂的亂碼。Unicode 的解決辦法是：替所有的文字做一張超大的表。2026 年的版本 Unicode 18.0 收了 172,808 個字元。中文的「永」是 27,704 號，通常寫成 U+6C38。大多數的網頁用一種叫 UTF-8 的方法來存這些編號：一個英文字母用一個位元組，像「永」這樣的常用中文字用三個位元組。

圖片也是同樣的道理。螢幕上的一張圖是由很多小方格排成的，這些小方格叫做「像素」，每個像素只有一種顏色。這個顏色存成三個數：紅有多少、綠有多少、藍有多少。每個數通常用一個位元組，所以是 0 到 255。紅 255、綠 0、藍 0 就是純紅。三個位元組一共可以表示 16,777,216 種顏色。一張寬 4,000 像素、高 3,000 像素的照片有 1,200 萬個像素，還沒縮小之前就需要 3,600 萬個位元組。
聲音也會變成數。麥克風把聲音變成一條上上下下的電波。電腦每隔一小段相等的時間，就量一次這條波有多高，把每一次量到的結果記成一個數。這叫做「取樣」。音樂 CD 每一秒要量 44,100 次，每一次記成一個 16 位元的數。要播放音樂時，電腦照順序把這些數讀出來，喇叭再把波重新做出來。
最讓人意外的是：位元自己並沒有說它是什麼。01000001 這八個位元，可以是數 65，可以是字母 A，也可以是一種暗暗的紅色。位元裡沒有任何東西告訴你是哪一種。意思來自電腦用哪一套編碼去讀它。所以把一張照片當成文字打開，看到的就是一堆亂碼。電腦裡的一切都是數，再加上一個「這些數代表什麼」的約定。
questions: What is a code, and why does everyone need to use the same one?
How is the color of one pixel stored?
The bits 01000001 can mean 65, the letter A, or a shade of red. How does a computer know which one is meant?
answers: A code is a table that says which number stands for which thing, such as a letter. If two computers use different codes, the same numbers turn into different characters, and the text becomes nonsense.
It is stored as three numbers: how much red, how much green, and how much blue. Each number is usually one byte, from 0 to 255.
The bits do not say. The meaning comes from the code the computer uses to read them: read as a number they are 65, read with ASCII they are A, and read as a color they are an amount of red.

vocab.ex: Morse code uses dots and dashes to stand for letters.
vocab.exzh: 摩斯電碼用點和線來代表字母。

vocab.ex: A password should have at least eight characters.
vocab.exzh: 密碼至少要有八個字元。

vocab.ex: All the chargers follow the same standard, so any one of them fits my phone.
vocab.exzh: 這些充電器都照同一個標準，所以每一個都插得進我的手機。

vocab.ex: On this map, the blue lines represent rivers.
vocab.exzh: 在這張地圖上，藍色的線代表河流。

vocab.ex: If you zoom in far enough, you can see every pixel in the photo.
vocab.exzh: 放大到夠大，就能看見照片裡的每一個像素。

vocab.ex: The nurse measured my height and weight.
vocab.exzh: 護理師量了我的身高和體重。

vocab.ex: The recorder samples the sound thousands of times each second.
vocab.exzh: 錄音機每秒對聲音取樣好幾千次。

vocab.ex: The two teams made an agreement to share the field.
vocab.exzh: 兩隊約定好一起用這個場地。

quiz.q: In ASCII, which number stands for the capital letter A?
Why was Unicode needed?
options: The world’s writing systems need far more than 128 characters, in one shared table.
Computers could not store numbers above 128.

quiz.q: Which three numbers are stored for the color of one pixel?
What does a computer do when it samples a sound?
options: It measures the height of the sound wave again and again.
It turns the sound into letters.

quiz.q: According to the reading, what gives a row of bits its meaning?
options: The code used to read them

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.en: A picture is made of squares
parts.text_en: From far away you see an apple. Walk up to the wall and count how the picture turns into squares.
parts.text_zh: 遠遠看是一顆蘋果。走近這面牆，看圖怎麼變成一格一格的方塊。

parts.text_en: Read the three numbers of a red pixel on the apple, then of a green pixel on the leaf.
parts.text_zh: 先讀蘋果上一個紅色像素的三個數，再讀葉子上一個綠色像素的。

parts.meta_en: All off is 0, all on is 255
parts.text_en: The switches from Lesson 1 turn all the way off, then all the way on. Watch the pixel.
parts.text_zh: 第一課的開關先全部關掉，再全部打開。看那個像素怎麼變。

parts.text_en: Set the switches to 0100 0001 and read them as a number, as a letter, and as a color.
parts.text_zh: 把開關設成 0100 0001，分別當成數、當成字、當成顏色來讀。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then make your own color: pick a pixel and try to turn it yellow. Which two of the three numbers have to be high?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己調一個顏色：選一個像素，試著把它變成黃色。三個數裡面，哪兩個要很大？

chars.en: Type a Character, See Its Number
chars.lead_en: Type anything: English, Chinese, or an emoji. For each character you will see its number in the Unicode table and the bytes that a web page stores for it in UTF-8.
chars.lead_zh: 隨便打：英文、中文或表情符號都可以。每個字都會列出它在 Unicode 表上的編號，以及網頁用 UTF-8 存它的時候用到的位元組。

tips.en: A is 65 and a is 97. Every lowercase English letter is exactly 32 more than its capital.
tips.zh: A 是 65，a 是 97。每個小寫英文字母都剛好比大寫多 32。

tips.en: The character “0” is number 48, not zero. A digit you type is a character, not yet a number.
tips.zh: 字元「0」是 48 號，不是零。你打的數字是「字元」，還不是「數」。

tips.en: In UTF-8, an English letter takes 1 byte, a common Chinese character such as 永 takes 3, and the emoji 😀 takes 4.
tips.zh: 在 UTF-8 裡，一個英文字母用 1 個位元組，像「永」這樣的常用中文字用 3 個，表情符號 😀 用 4 個。

draw.zh: 用 64 個位元畫一張圖
draw.lead_en: The simplest picture has only two colors, so each pixel needs just one bit: 1 for dark, 0 for light. Tap or drag on the grid to draw. Each row of eight squares is one byte, so the whole picture is eight numbers.
draw.lead_zh: 最簡單的圖只有兩種顏色，所以每個像素只要一個位元：1 是深色，0 是淺色。在格子上點或拖曳來畫。每一列八格就是一個位元組，所以整張圖就是八個數。

tips.en: Read a row like the lights in Lesson 1: the left square is worth 128 and the right square is worth 1.
tips.zh: 讀一列的方法和第一課的燈一樣：最左邊那格代表 128，最右邊那格代表 1。

tips.en: Send a friend only the eight numbers. Can they draw your picture without seeing it?
tips.zh: 只把那八個數傳給朋友。對方沒看到圖，能不能把它畫出來？

tips.en: Try to draw the picture for these numbers: 24, 60, 126, 255, 255, 126, 60, 24.

sound.en: Turn a Sound Wave into Numbers
sound.lead_en: The smooth line is one wave of sound. The computer measures its height at equal steps and keeps only the numbers. Slide to measure more often, and choose how many bits each measurement gets. Watch the steps get closer to the wave.
sound.lead_zh: 那條平滑的線是聲音的一個波。電腦每隔一段相等的時間量一次它的高度，只把數留下來。拉滑桿讓它量得更密，再選每一次用幾個位元來記。看那些階梯怎麼越來越貼近原來的波。
sound.note_en: This is an illustration; the wave is drawn, not recorded. The sounds people can hear have up to about 20,000 waves every second, which is why a CD takes 44,100 measurements a second. At 16 bits each, that is 705,600 bits for every second of sound.
sound.note_zh: 這是示意，這條波是畫出來的，不是錄下來的。人聽得到的聲音，每秒最多大約有兩萬個波，所以 CD 每秒要量 44,100 次。每次 16 個位元，每一秒的聲音就是 705,600 個位元。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Codes · 編碼的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A table from 1963, one table for the world, three bytes of color, and a shiny disc
culture_cards.title_zh: 1963 年的一張表、全世界共用的表、三個位元組的顏色、一張亮亮的光碟
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about the agreements behind your screen and speakers.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 螢幕和喇叭背後的四個「約定」。

cards.en: When computers could not talk to each other
cards.zh: 電腦之間講不通的年代
cards.body_en: Before ASCII, each computer maker represented letters and digits in its own way; IBM alone used nine different character sets. A committee of computer makers worked out a common code, and ASCII was approved as the American standard on June 17, 1963. The name stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange. With seven bits it has 128 codes: 1010000 is a capital P, and 1110000 is a lowercase p.
cards.body_zh: 在 ASCII 之前，每家電腦廠商各用各的方法表示字母和數字，光是 IBM 一家就用了九套不同的字元集。電腦廠商組成的委員會訂出一套共同的編碼，1963 年 6 月 17 日，ASCII 獲准成為美國標準。ASCII 是 American Standard Code for Information Interchange（美國資訊交換標準碼）的縮寫。它用七個位元，有 128 個編號：1010000 是大寫的 P，1110000 是小寫的 p。

cards.en: One table for every writing system
cards.zh: 所有文字共用的一張表
cards.body_en: Unicode gives every character a number of its own, whatever the language. The table keeps growing: version 18.0, released on September 16, 2026, added 13,007 characters for a total of 172,808. The way most web pages store those numbers, UTF-8, was designed by Ken Thompson. His colleague Rob Pike recalled that it happened “on a placemat in a New Jersey diner one night in September or so 1992.”
cards.body_zh: 不管是哪一種語言，Unicode 都給每個字元一個自己的編號。這張表一直在長大：2026 年 9 月 16 日發布的 18.0 版新增 13,007 個字元，總共 172,808 個。大多數網頁存這些編號的方法 UTF-8，是肯・湯普遜（Ken Thompson）設計的。他的同事羅布・派克（Rob Pike）回憶，那是「1992 年 9 月左右的一個晚上，在紐澤西一家小餐館的餐墊紙上」寫出來的。

cards.en: Why three numbers are enough
cards.body_en: A screen makes colors by adding light. Look at a screen through a magnifying glass and you will see that each pixel is made of three small dots: one gives off red light, one green, and one blue. Red and green light together look yellow, and all three together look white. With one byte for each of the three, there are 256 × 256 × 256 = 16,777,216 possible colors.
cards.body_zh: 螢幕是用「把光加在一起」的方法做出顏色的。用放大鏡看螢幕，會看到每個像素由三個小點組成：一個發紅光，一個發綠光，一個發藍光。紅光加綠光看起來是黃色，三種光全開看起來是白色。三個小點各用一個位元組，就有 256 × 256 × 256＝16,777,216 種可能的顏色。

cards.en: Music as a list of numbers
cards.body_en: The compact disc was invented together by Philips and Sony and went on sale in 1982. It was how most people first owned music stored as numbers. People can hear sounds up to about 20,000 waves a second, and to catch a wave you must measure it at least twice. So a CD samples a little more than twice that fast: 44,100 times a second.
cards.body_zh: CD（光碟）由飛利浦和索尼共同發明，1982 年上市。對大多數人來說，這是第一次擁有「存成數字」的音樂。人最高大約能聽到每秒兩萬個波的聲音，而要抓住一個波，至少得量它兩次。所以 CD 取樣的速度比兩倍再快一點：每秒 44,100 次。

myths.myth_en: A computer stores the letter A as a tiny picture of an A.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦把字母 A 存成一個小小的 A 的圖。
myths.fact_en: It stores a number, 65. The shape you see comes from a font, which is a separate file that tells the screen how to draw each numbered character.
myths.fact_zh: 它存的是一個數：65。你看到的形狀來自「字型」，那是另一個檔案，告訴螢幕每個編號的字要怎麼畫。

myths.myth_en: A row of bits knows whether it is a letter, a color, or a sound.
myths.myth_zh: 一排位元自己知道它是字、是顏色，還是聲音。
myths.fact_en: It does not. 01000001 is 65, or A, or a shade of red, depending on the code used to read it. Open a file with the wrong code and you get nonsense.
myths.fact_zh: 它不知道。01000001 是 65、是 A、還是某種紅，要看用哪一套編碼去讀。用錯編碼打開檔案，看到的就是亂碼。

myths.myth_en: An emoji is a small picture that is sent to your friend.
myths.myth_zh: 表情符號是一張小圖，傳給了朋友。
myths.fact_en: An emoji is a character with a number in Unicode, like a letter. Only the number is sent. Each phone or computer maker draws its own picture for that number, so the same emoji can look different on a friend’s screen.
myths.fact_zh: 表情符號和字母一樣，是 Unicode 裡有編號的字元。傳出去的只有編號；每家手機或電腦廠商各自替這個編號畫圖，所以同一個表情符號在朋友的螢幕上可能長得不一樣。

myths.myth_en: The character “5” and the number 5 are the same thing to a computer.
myths.myth_zh: 對電腦來說，字元「5」和數 5 是同一個東西。
myths.fact_en: The character “5” is stored as number 53. A program has to convert the character into the number 5 before it can do arithmetic with it.
myths.fact_zh: 字元「5」存起來是 53 號。程式要先把這個字元轉成數 5，才能拿它來計算。

tricks.body_en: Bits make numbers. A code says what the numbers mean.
tricks.body_zh: 位元組成數；編碼規定這些數代表什麼。

tricks.body_en: A letter is stored as its number in a table, not as its shape.
tricks.body_zh: 字存的是它在表上的編號，不是它的形狀。

tricks.body_en: One pixel, three numbers, each from 0 to 255.
tricks.body_zh: 一個像素、三個數，每個數從 0 到 255。

tricks.body_en: Sound is a wave measured many times a second: 44,100 times on a CD.
tricks.body_zh: 聲音是每秒量很多次的一條波：CD 每秒量 44,100 次。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: The developer console is a powerful tool. Type only what this lesson shows, and never paste in code that a stranger or a website tells you to paste: it could give away your account.
safety.zh: 開發人員主控台是很強的工具。只輸入這一課寫的那幾行；陌生人或網站叫你貼進去的程式碼絕對不要貼，那可能會讓你的帳號被盜。

safety.en: Changes you make with Inspect are only on your own screen. They disappear when you reload, and they do not change the real website.
safety.zh: 用「檢查」改的東西只在你自己的螢幕上，重新整理就不見了，不會改到真正的網站。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission, and do not change its settings.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意，也不要更改設定。

safety.en: Look away from the screen every 20 minutes and let your eyes rest.
safety.zh: 每看 20 分鐘螢幕，就把視線移開，讓眼睛休息一下。

materials.en: A code table on the board: A = 65, B = 66, C = 67 … Z = 90
Paper and a pencil for each pair
materials.zh: 每組一張紙、一枝鉛筆

materials.en: Eight small cards or coins (optional), to use as switches
materials.zh: 八張小卡片或硬幣（可有可無），當成開關

steps.en: With a partner, choose a secret word of three or four capital letters. Do not show it to other pairs.
steps.zh: 兩人一組，選一個三到四個大寫字母的祕密單字，不要讓別組看到。

steps.en: Look up the number of each letter in the table. For example, CAT is 67, 65, 84.
steps.zh: 在表上查出每個字母的編號。例如 CAT 是 67、65、84。

steps.en: Write each number as eight bits, the way you learned in Lesson 1. 65 is 0100 0001.
steps.zh: 用第一課學的方法，把每個數寫成八個位元。65 是 0100 0001。

steps.en: Trade papers with another pair. Turn their bits back into numbers, and the numbers back into letters.
steps.zh: 和另一組交換。把對方的位元變回數，再把數變回字母。

activities.tip_en: Then ask: what if one pair had used a different table, with A = 1? The same bits would spell a different word, or nothing at all. That is what happens when a file is opened with the wrong code. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson fits “Data representation, processing, and analysis” (資 D-IV-1 and 資 D-IV-2; the notes list sampling and the idea of encoding).
activities.tip_zh: 接著問：如果有一組用的是另一張表（A＝1），會怎樣？同樣的位元會拼出另一個字，或者什麼都不是。這就是用錯編碼打開檔案時發生的事。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課屬於「資料表示、處理及分析」（資 D-IV-1、資 D-IV-2；附錄的說明列有「取樣、量化」與「編碼的概念」）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A computer with a web browser such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari
materials.zh: 一台有瀏覽器的電腦（Chrome、Edge、Firefox 或 Safari）

materials.en: This page
materials.zh: 這一頁

steps.en: Open the browser’s developer tools and choose the Console tab. In Chrome, press Command+Option+J on a Mac, or Control+Shift+J on Windows.
steps.zh: 打開瀏覽器的開發人員工具，選「Console」（主控台）分頁。Chrome：Mac 按 Command＋Option＋J，Windows 按 Control＋Shift＋J。

steps.en: Type 'A'.charCodeAt(0) and press Enter. The browser answers 65.
steps.zh: 輸入 'A'.charCodeAt(0) 再按 Enter，瀏覽器會回答 65。

steps.en: Type '永'.codePointAt(0) and press Enter. It answers 27704. Now go the other way: String.fromCodePoint(27704).
steps.zh: 輸入 '永'.codePointAt(0) 再按 Enter，它會回答 27704。再反過來試：String.fromCodePoint(27704)。

steps.en: Now find a color. Right-click any colored part of this page and choose Inspect. In the Styles panel, look for a color written as rgb(…) or as # followed by six characters.
steps.zh: 接著找一個顏色。在這一頁任何有顏色的地方按右鍵，選「檢查」。在 Styles（樣式）面板裡找寫成 rgb(…)，或是 # 後面接六個字元的顏色。

activities.tip_en: A color written as #d62828 is the same three numbers in another form: d6 is 214, 28 is 40, and 28 is 40. That is the red of the apple in the model. Web developers read these numbers every day. In Safari you must first turn on the developer tools in Settings, and menu names differ a little between browsers.
activities.tip_zh: 寫成 #d62828 的顏色，是同樣三個數的另一種寫法：d6 是 214，28 是 40，28 是 40——就是模型裡蘋果的紅。寫網站的人每天都在讀這些數。Safari 要先在設定裡打開開發人員工具；各家瀏覽器的選單名稱略有不同。

links_head.en: Where the bits came from, the character 永, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 位元從哪裡來、「永」這個字，以及下一課

links.en: Why Do Computers Use Only 0 and 1?
links.zh: 電腦為什麼只用 0 和 1？
links.note_en: The eight switches in this lesson come from here: how a row of on-and-off switches counts from 0 to 255.
links.note_zh: 這一課的八個開關就是從這裡來的：一排開和關的開關怎麼從 0 數到 255。

links.en: Can One Character Teach You Every Stroke?
links.zh: 永字八法：一個字學會所有筆畫？
links.note_en: To a computer, 永 is number 27,704. To a calligrapher, it is five strokes that hold eight ways of moving the brush.

lessons.title: How Does a Computer Make a Decision?
lessons.blurb_en: Wire two switches in a row, side by side, or as a seesaw, and watch a light answer AND, OR, and NOT in 3D. Then connect gates to solve six everyday puzzles and test yourself on truth tables.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡把開關排成一排、一上一下，或做成蹺蹺板，看一盞燈怎麼回答「而且」「或者」「不是」。再把閘接起來解六個生活裡的題目，用真值表考考自己。
lessons.big_idea_en: A computer decides by wiring switches together. Switches in a row answer AND, switches side by side answer OR, and a switch that works backward answers NOT. These logic gates take in 0s and 1s and give out a 0 or a 1, and gates joined to other gates can answer any yes-or-no question.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電腦做決定，靠的是把開關接在一起。排成一排的開關回答「而且」，一上一下的開關回答「或者」，反著做的開關回答「不是」。這些邏輯閘吃進 0 和 1、吐出一個 0 或 1；一個閘接一個閘，就能回答任何「是或不是」的問題。

lab.title_en: Three Ways to Wire a Switch
lab.how_en: A battery, a light, and switches on a board. Tap a switch to push its handle down: down means 1, up means 0. When there is a complete path of copper from the battery to the light and back, dots run along the wire and the light turns on. Choose AND, OR, or NOT to rewire the board, and watch which row of the truth table you are on.
lab.how_zh: 木板上有一顆電池、一盞燈和幾個開關。點一下開關，把它的把手壓下去：壓下去是 1，翹起來是 0。只要從電池到燈、再回到電池有一條完整的銅線，線上就有光點在跑，燈也會亮。選 AND、OR 或 NOT 換一種接法，同時看看自己現在在真值表的哪一列。

gates.rule_en: Two switches in a row. The light is on only if A AND B are both 1.
gates.rule_zh: 兩個開關排成一排。A「而且」B 都是 1，燈才亮。

gates.rule_en: Two switches side by side. The light is on if A OR B is 1, or both.
gates.rule_zh: 兩個開關一上一下。A「或者」B 是 1（兩個都是也算），燈就亮。

gates.rule_en: One seesaw switch. The light is on only if A is NOT 1.
gates.rule_zh: 一個蹺蹺板開關。A「不是」1 的時候，燈才亮。

legend.en: Copper arm: pushed down, it bridges the gap in the wire (1); lifted, it leaves a gap (0)
legend.zh: 銅臂：壓下去就搭在缺口上（1），翹起來就留下缺口（0）

legend.en: Seesaw switch: pushing the handle down lifts the contact at the other end
legend.zh: 蹺蹺板開關：把手壓下去，另一頭的接點反而翹起來

legend.en: Moving dots: there is a complete path, so current is flowing
legend.zh: 會動的光點：路是通的，有電流在流

legend.en: Light on: the answer is 1
legend.zh: 燈亮：答案是 1

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. In a real computer nobody pushes the switches: each gate is built from a few transistors, which are switches turned on and off by electricity, and the output of one gate drives the inputs of others. Real gates are far too small to see, and they do not have copper arms or light bulbs. The dots only show that a path is complete; electric current is not a row of little balls. The logic is exact: every row of the truth tables matches what real AND, OR, and NOT gates do.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。真的電腦裡沒有人去壓開關：每個閘是用幾個電晶體做成的，電晶體是由電來控制開和關的開關，一個閘的輸出會去推動別的閘的輸入。真的閘小到看不見，也沒有銅臂和燈泡。光點只是表示「路通了」，電流並不是一排小球。邏輯是精確的：真值表的每一列，都和真的 AND、OR、NOT 閘一樣。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The truth tables and puzzles are tested in tools/computers/test/logic.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；真值表與題目有自動測試（tools/computers/test/logic.test.mjs）。

paras: Every day a computer makes countless small decisions. Your phone unlocks only if the passcode is right. A game ends if you run out of lives. A message goes out if you tap Send and you are online. But Lessons 1 and 2 showed that a computer holds nothing except switches and numbers. Nobody inside is thinking. So how can a pile of switches decide anything? The secret is in how the switches are wired together.

Start with a battery, a light, and two switches, A and B. Wire the switches in a row, one after the other. Now the current has to pass through both, so the light turns on only if A and B are both on. This arrangement is called an AND gate. Next, wire the two switches side by side, so that the current has two roads to choose from. Now the light turns on if A or B is on, or both. This is an OR gate.

The third kind is the simplest and the strangest. It has only one input, and its output is always the opposite. If the input is on, the output is off. If the input is off, the output is on. It is called a NOT gate, and in the model it is a switch built like a seesaw. AND, OR, and NOT are the three basic logic gates. Each one takes in 0s and 1s and gives out a single 0 or 1.

You can write down everything a gate does in a small chart called a truth table. It has one row for every possible set of inputs. Two inputs can be set in four ways, so the table for AND has four rows, and only the last row, 1 and 1, gives a 1. In a real computer, nobody flips the switches by hand. The gates are made of transistors, which are switches turned on and off by electricity. That is why the output of one gate can become the input of the next.

The idea is older than computers. In 1854, a largely self-taught English mathematician named George Boole published a book known as The Laws of Thought. He showed that logic could be worked out like algebra, with symbols and rules. His system is now called Boolean algebra, and it is the basis for designing computer circuits. Boole died in 1864, long before anyone built an electronic computer. Decades later, a student named Claude Shannon showed that Boole’s algebra fits circuits made of switches.

One gate answers one small question. The power comes from joining gates together. “Go out to play if it is NOT raining AND your homework is done” needs two gates: a NOT and an AND. Join more of them, and a circuit can compare two numbers, choose between two paths, or, as you will see in the next lesson, add. A modern chip holds billions of transistors wired into gates. Every decision a computer seems to make is really a great many tiny yes-or-no questions, answered by gates one after another.
paras_zh: 電腦每天要做數不清的小決定。密碼對了，手機才會解鎖。命用完了，遊戲就結束。你按了「傳送」而且有連上網路，訊息才會送出去。可是第一課和第二課告訴我們，電腦裡除了開關和數，什麼都沒有，裡面並沒有誰在思考。那麼一堆開關怎麼能決定任何事？祕密就在這些開關是怎麼接在一起的。
先準備一顆電池、一盞燈，還有兩個開關 A 和 B。把兩個開關排成一排，一個接一個。這樣電流兩個都得通過，所以只有 A 和 B 都打開，燈才會亮。這種接法叫做 AND 閘（及閘）。接著把兩個開關改成一上一下並排，讓電流有兩條路可以選。這樣只要 A 或 B 打開（兩個都開也算），燈就會亮。這是 OR 閘（或閘）。
第三種最簡單，也最奇怪。它只有一個輸入，輸出永遠和輸入相反：輸入是開，輸出就是關；輸入是關，輸出就是開。它叫做 NOT 閘（反閘），在模型裡是一個做成蹺蹺板的開關。AND、OR、NOT 是三種基本的邏輯閘。每一種都吃進 0 和 1，吐出一個 0 或 1。
一個閘做的所有事，可以寫成一張小表，叫做「真值表」。每一種可能的輸入各占一列。兩個輸入有四種設法，所以 AND 的真值表有四列，只有最後一列（1 和 1）的結果是 1。在真的電腦裡，沒有人用手去撥開關。邏輯閘是用電晶體做的，電晶體是由電來控制開和關的開關。所以一個閘的輸出，可以變成下一個閘的輸入。
這個想法比電腦還老。1854 年，一位大半靠自學的英國數學家喬治・布爾（George Boole）出版了一本書，通稱《思維的法則》。他證明邏輯可以像代數一樣，用符號和規則來運算。他的這套系統現在叫做「布林代數」，是設計電腦電路的基礎。布爾在 1864 年過世，離第一台電子電腦出現還早得很。幾十年後，一位名叫克勞德・夏農的學生指出，布爾的代數正好能用來描述開關接成的電路。
一個閘只回答一個小問題，把閘接在一起才有力量。「沒下雨，而且功課做完了，才可以出去玩」需要兩個閘：一個 NOT、一個 AND。再多接幾個，電路就能比較兩個數的大小、在兩條路之間做選擇，或者——下一課就會看到——做加法。一顆現代的晶片上有幾十億個電晶體，接成了邏輯閘。電腦看起來在做的每一個決定，其實是非常多個小小的「是或不是」，由邏輯閘一個接一個回答出來的。
questions: How are the switches wired in an AND gate, and when does the light turn on?
What does a NOT gate do?
Why does it matter that the output of one gate can be the input of another?
answers: They are wired in a row, one after the other. The current must pass through both, so the light turns on only if both switches are on.
It has one input, and its output is always the opposite: 1 becomes 0, and 0 becomes 1.

Because one gate answers only one small question. When gates are joined, they can answer bigger questions, such as “NOT raining AND homework done,” and with enough gates a circuit can compare, choose, and add.

vocab.ex: There is no logic in wearing a coat on such a hot day.
vocab.exzh: 這麼熱的天穿外套，一點也不合邏輯。

vocab.ex: A logic gate lets current through only when its rule is met.
vocab.exzh: 邏輯閘只有在符合它的規則時，才讓電流通過。

vocab.ex: A keyboard sends input to the computer.
vocab.exzh: 鍵盤把輸入送進電腦。

vocab.ex: The output of a NOT gate is the opposite of what goes in.
vocab.exzh: 反閘的輸出和進去的東西相反。

vocab.ex: The light will not work until the circuit is complete.
vocab.exzh: 電路沒有接通之前，燈不會亮。

vocab.ex: Hot is the opposite of cold.
vocab.exzh: 熱是冷的相反。

vocab.ex: Choosing a high school is a big decision.
vocab.exzh: 選高中是一個重大的決定。

vocab.ex: Combine the flour and the eggs in a large bowl.
vocab.exzh: 把麵粉和蛋放進大碗裡混在一起。

options: Only when both switches are on
Only when both switches are off

quiz.q: A is 1 and B is 0. What is A OR B?
What is NOT 1?
How many rows does a truth table need for a gate with two inputs?
According to the reading, what are the gates in a real computer made of?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch all four rows of the table. In how many of them does the light turn on?
parts.text_zh: 把真值表的四列都看一遍。有幾列燈會亮？

parts.meta_zh: 至少有一個是 1 就是 1
parts.text_en: Now the current has two roads. Which is the only row that leaves the light off?
parts.text_zh: 現在電有兩條路可以走。只有哪一列燈不亮？

parts.text_en: Push the handle down and look at the other end of the seesaw. Why does the light go off?
parts.text_zh: 把把手壓下去，看看蹺蹺板的另一頭。燈為什麼滅了？

parts.zh: 同樣的開關，不同的接法
parts.text_en: Leave the switches alone and change only the wires, from AND to OR and back.
parts.text_zh: 開關不動，只把線從 AND 改成 OR，再改回來。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try it yourself: set A to 1 and B to 1. Which wirings turn the light on, and which one cannot even use B?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己試：把 A 和 B 都設成 1。哪幾種接法燈會亮？哪一種根本用不到 B？

wire.lead_en: Each puzzle is a rule from everyday life. Choose AND or OR, and decide whether to put a NOT in front of A or B. The table compares what the rule wants with what your circuit does. When all four rows match, the light turns on.
wire.lead_zh: 每一題都是生活裡的一條規則。選 AND 或 OR，再決定要不要在 A 或 B 的前面加一個 NOT。表格會把「規則要的」和「你接的電路做的」一列一列對照；四列都對了，燈就亮。

puzzles.en: The alarm rings if the door is open AND the alarm is switched on.
puzzles.zh: 門開著，而且警報器有打開，警鈴才響。

puzzles.en: The doorbell rings if someone presses the front button OR the back button.
puzzles.zh: 有人按前門的按鈕，或者按後門的按鈕，門鈴就響。

puzzles.en: You may go out to play if it is NOT raining AND your homework is done.
puzzles.zh: 沒有下雨，而且功課做完了，才可以出去玩。

puzzles.en: The warning beeps if the car is moving AND the seat belt is NOT fastened.
puzzles.zh: 車子在動，而且安全帶沒有繫上，警示音就會響。

puzzles.en: Take an umbrella if it is raining OR the sky is NOT clear.
puzzles.zh: 正在下雨，或者天空不晴朗，就帶傘。

puzzles.en: The night-light turns on if the room light is NOT on AND it is NOT daytime.
puzzles.zh: 房間的燈沒開，而且不是白天，小夜燈才亮。

tips.en: Read the rule out loud and listen for the words and, or, and not. Each one is a gate.
tips.zh: 把規則唸出來，聽聽裡面的「而且」「或者」「不」：每一個就是一個閘。

tips.en: With AND or OR, and a NOT you can put in front of each input, you can build eight different circuits.
tips.zh: AND 或 OR，加上每個輸入前面可以放的 NOT，一共能接出八種不同的電路。

tips.en: These are made-up rules for practice. A real alarm or car has many more inputs than two.
tips.zh: 這些是練習用的規則。真正的警報器或汽車，輸入遠遠不只兩個。

lquiz.lead_en: Eight questions. You are given A and B, and you answer 0 or 1. The first questions use one gate; the last three join two. The game counts how many you get right on the first try.
lquiz.lead_zh: 一共八題。題目給你 A 和 B，你回答 0 或 1。前面幾題只有一個閘，最後三題把兩個閘接在一起。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾題。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Gates · 邏輯閘的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A schoolteacher, a student, a word in every program, and the word “or”
culture_cards.title_zh: 一位小學老師、一個學生、每個程式裡都有的字、還有「或」這個字
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about where the logic in a computer came from.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 電腦裡的邏輯從哪裡來的四個小故事。

cards.en: The teacher who turned logic into algebra
cards.zh: 把邏輯變成代數的老師
cards.body_en: George Boole was born in Lincoln, England, in 1815. Apart from lessons from his father and a few years at local schools, he was self-taught in mathematics. He began teaching in village schools at 16 and opened his own school at 20. In 1849 he became professor of mathematics at Queen’s College in Cork, Ireland, even though he had no university degree. His 1854 book on the laws of thought was, in his own view, the mature statement of his ideas.
cards.body_zh: 喬治・布爾 1815 年生於英格蘭的林肯。除了父親教他的和在當地學校讀的幾年，他的數學都是自學的。他 16 歲開始在鄉村學校教書，20 歲自己開了一所學校。1849 年，他成為愛爾蘭科克的皇后學院數學教授，雖然他沒有大學學位。1854 年那本談思維法則的書，是他自己認為最成熟的一次陳述。

cards.en: The student who saw algebra in the switches
cards.zh: 在開關裡看見代數的學生
cards.body_en: For decades, Boole’s algebra was a subject for logicians. Claude Shannon, the same person who gave us the word “bit” in Lesson 1, changed that. His master’s thesis at MIT, A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits, used Boolean algebra to work out circuits made of switches. Britannica says it established the theoretical underpinnings of digital circuits and has been called one of the most significant master’s theses of the 20th century.
cards.body_zh: 有好幾十年，布爾的代數是邏輯學家在研究的東西。改變這件事的是克勞德・夏農，就是第一課裡讓「bit」這個詞傳開的那個人。他在麻省理工學院的碩士論文〈繼電器與開關電路的符號分析〉，用布林代數來推算開關接成的電路。大英百科說，這篇論文奠定了數位電路的理論基礎，被稱為二十世紀最重要的碩士論文之一。

cards.en: Boole’s name is in every program
cards.zh: 每個程式裡都有布爾的名字
cards.body_en: Programmers call a value that can only be true or false a Boolean, after George Boole. Programming languages have the three gates built in. In JavaScript, the language of web pages, AND is written &&, OR is written ||, and NOT is written !. So true && false gives false, true || false gives true, and !true gives false. You can try all three in your browser in the second activity below.
cards.body_zh: 寫程式的人把「只能是真或假」的值叫做 Boolean（布林值），就是用喬治・布爾的名字取的。程式語言裡本來就有這三種閘。在網頁用的 JavaScript 裡，AND 寫成 &&，OR 寫成 ||，NOT 寫成 !。所以 true && false 得到 false，true || false 得到 true，!true 得到 false。下面的第二個活動，就是在瀏覽器裡把這三個都試一遍。

cards.en: Two kinds of “or”
cards.body_en: “Soup or salad?” usually means choose one, not both. A logic OR is different: A OR B is 1 when A is 1, when B is 1, and also when both are 1. A truth table shows it plainly: “p or q” is false only when both are false. The choose-only-one kind has its own name, exclusive OR, or XOR. It is 1 when exactly one input is 1, and it will be useful in the next lesson.
cards.body_zh: 「湯或沙拉？」通常是要你選一樣，不是兩樣都要。邏輯的 OR 不一樣：A 是 1、B 是 1，或者兩個都是 1 的時候，A OR B 都是 1。真值表寫得很清楚：「p 或 q」只有在兩個都是假的時候才是假。「只能選一個」的那種有自己的名字，叫做互斥或（XOR）：恰好只有一個輸入是 1 的時候才是 1。下一課會用到它。

myths.myth_en: A computer thinks about a question the way a person does.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦像人一樣思考問題。
myths.fact_en: A gate does not know what its inputs mean. It only follows its wiring: 1s and 0s in, a 1 or a 0 out. People decide what the inputs stand for and how the gates are joined.
myths.fact_zh: 邏輯閘不知道它的輸入代表什麼。它只是照著接線走：進來 1 和 0，出去一個 1 或 0。輸入代表什麼、閘要怎麼接，是人決定的。

myths.myth_en: 1 AND 1 is 2.
myths.myth_zh: 1 AND 1 等於 2。
myths.fact_en: AND is not addition. It asks a question: are both inputs 1? The answer is yes, which is written 1. A gate can never give out anything but 0 or 1.
myths.fact_zh: AND 不是加法。它在問一個問題：兩個輸入都是 1 嗎？答案是「是」，寫成 1。邏輯閘吐出來的永遠只有 0 或 1。

myths.myth_en: OR means one or the other, but not both.
myths.myth_zh: OR 的意思是二選一，不能兩個都是。
myths.fact_en: In logic, A OR B is also 1 when both are 1. The one-but-not-both kind is a different gate called XOR.
myths.fact_zh: 在邏輯裡，兩個都是 1 的時候 A OR B 也是 1。「只能一個、不能兩個」是另一種閘，叫做 XOR。

myths.myth_en: A computer needs a different kind of part for every kind of decision.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦每做一種決定，就需要一種不同的零件。
myths.fact_en: The same few kinds of gates are used over and over. What changes is how many there are and how they are wired together.
myths.fact_zh: 用來用去就是那幾種閘。不一樣的是用了多少個、怎麼接在一起。

tricks.body_en: In a row. 1 only when both are 1.
tricks.body_zh: 排成一排。兩個都是 1 才是 1。

tricks.body_en: Side by side. 0 only when both are 0.
tricks.body_zh: 一上一下。兩個都是 0 才是 0。

tricks.body_en: One in, the opposite out.
tricks.body_zh: 一個進去，相反的出來。

tricks.body_en: A truth table lists every possible input: 2 rows for one input, 4 for two, 8 for three.
tricks.body_zh: 真值表把每一種可能的輸入都列出來：一個輸入 2 列，兩個 4 列，三個 8 列。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: If you build these circuits for real, use only small batteries such as AA cells and a small bulb or LED made for them. Never use the wall socket.
safety.zh: 如果要真的接這些電路，只能用小電池（例如三號電池）和搭配它的小燈泡或 LED，絕對不要用牆上的插座。

safety.en: Never join the two ends of a battery directly with a wire. With nothing in between to use the energy, the wire and the battery can get hot very quickly.
safety.zh: 絕對不要用一條線直接把電池的兩頭接在一起。中間沒有東西用電，電線和電池會很快變燙。

safety.en: In the developer console, type only what this lesson shows, and never paste in code that someone else tells you to paste.
safety.zh: 在開發人員主控台裡，只輸入這一課寫的那幾行；別人叫你貼的程式碼絕對不要貼。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission, and do not change its settings.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意，也不要更改設定。

materials.en: Three cards: AND, OR, NOT
materials.zh: 三張卡片：AND、OR、NOT

materials.en: Two more cards for the inputs: A and B
materials.zh: 另外兩張輸入卡片：A、B

materials.en: Space at the front of the room
materials.zh: 教室前面的空間

steps.en: Two students are the inputs A and B. A raised hand means 1, and a hand down means 0. A third student is the gate and holds the AND card.
steps.zh: 兩位同學當輸入 A 和 B：舉手是 1，手放下是 0。第三位同學當邏輯閘，拿著 AND 卡片。

steps.en: The gate student looks only at the two inputs and follows the rule on the card: stand up for 1, sit down for 0. Try all four ways A and B can be set, and write the results on the board as a truth table.
steps.zh: 當邏輯閘的同學只看這兩個輸入，照卡片上的規則做：站起來是 1，坐下是 0。把 A、B 的四種情況都試一遍，把結果寫在黑板上，就是一張真值表。

steps.en: Change the card to OR and fill in a second table. Then try NOT with only one input.
steps.zh: 把卡片換成 OR，填出第二張表。再用一個輸入試 NOT。

steps.en: Now join two gates. A NOT student watches input A, and an AND student watches the NOT student and input B. The class calls out a rule for the row where the AND student stands, such as “NOT raining AND homework done.”
steps.zh: 接著把兩個閘接起來：一位 NOT 同學看著輸入 A，一位 AND 同學看著 NOT 同學和輸入 B。AND 同學站起來的那一列，請全班替它想一句規則，例如「沒下雨，而且功課做完了」。

activities.tip_en: The gate students never need to know what A and B stand for. They only follow a card. That is exactly the point of the first myth above. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, logic gates are not listed by name; this lesson supports the topic “System platforms” (資 S-IV-2, how system platforms are built and basically work).
activities.tip_zh: 當邏輯閘的同學完全不需要知道 A、B 代表什麼，只要照卡片做。這正是上面第一個迷思要說的事。十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容沒有直接列出邏輯閘；這一課可以用來支援「系統平台」主題（資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A computer with a web browser such as Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari
materials.zh: 一台有瀏覽器的電腦（Chrome、Edge、Firefox 或 Safari）

materials.en: A sheet of paper for your predictions
materials.zh: 一張紙，用來寫下你的預測

steps.en: Open the browser’s developer console. In Chrome, press Command+Option+J on a Mac, or Control+Shift+J on Windows.
steps.zh: 打開瀏覽器的開發人員主控台。Chrome：Mac 按 Command＋Option＋J，Windows 按 Control＋Shift＋J。

steps.en: Type true && false and press Enter. The browser answers false. That is AND: 1 AND 0 is 0.
steps.zh: 輸入 true && false 再按 Enter，瀏覽器會回答 false。這就是 AND：1 AND 0 是 0。

steps.en: Type true || false and then !true. Before you press Enter each time, write down what you expect.
steps.zh: 再輸入 true || false，然後輸入 !true。每次按 Enter 之前，先把你預測的答案寫下來。

steps.en: Now join gates the way the puzzles do: type !true && true, then !(true && true). Check each answer against a truth table you draw yourself.
steps.zh: 接著像小遊戲那樣把閘接起來：輸入 !true && true，再輸入 !(true && true)。自己畫真值表，核對每一個答案。

activities.tip_en: The answers are false, true, false, false, and false. A spreadsheet has the same gates: in Google Sheets or Excel, type =AND(TRUE, FALSE), =OR(TRUE, FALSE), and =NOT(TRUE). The words are different, but the truth tables are the same ones Boole’s algebra describes.
activities.tip_zh: 答案依序是 false、true、false、false、false。試算表裡也有同樣的閘：在 Google 試算表或 Excel 輸入 =AND(TRUE, FALSE)、=OR(TRUE, FALSE)、=NOT(TRUE)。寫法不同，真值表卻是布林代數描述的同一張。

links_head.en: The switch inside the gate, the lessons before, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 閘裡面的開關、前面兩課，以及下一課

links.en: How Do 0s and 1s Become Words, Pictures, and Sound?
links.zh: 0 和 1 怎麼變成文字、圖片和聲音？
links.note_en: The 0s and 1s that go into a gate can stand for anything. Lesson 2 shows how people agree on what they mean.
links.note_zh: 進到邏輯閘裡的 0 和 1 可以代表任何東西。第二課講的是大家怎麼約好它們的意思。

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體・第二課
links.en: What Does a Transistor Do?
links.note_en: The switches in a real gate are transistors. See how a small voltage turns one on, with no handle and no moving parts.
links.note_zh: 真的邏輯閘裡的開關是電晶體。看看一個小小的電壓怎麼把它打開：沒有把手，也沒有會動的零件。

links.en: How Does a Computer Add?
links.note_en: Gates only answer yes or no. Next: how a handful of them, wired the right way, add two numbers and pass the carry along.
links.note_zh: 邏輯閘只會回答是或不是。下一課要看：幾個閘用對的方法接起來，怎麼把兩個數加起來，還會進位。

lessons.title: How Does a Computer Add?
lessons.blurb_en: Set two numbers with switches and watch a four-bit adder work in 3D, one column at a time, as the carry hops from right to left. See the two gates inside a half adder, then be the adder yourself.
lessons.blurb_zh: 用開關設好兩個數，在 3D 裡看一台四位元加法器一位一位地算，進位從右邊跳到左邊。看看半加器裡面的兩個閘，再換你自己當加法器。
lessons.big_idea_en: A few logic gates wired together can add. For one column, an XOR gate gives the sum and an AND gate gives the carry. Put one adder in every column, pass each carry to the column on its left, and the circuit adds whole numbers.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 幾個邏輯閘接起來就能做加法。只看一位的話，XOR 閘算出「和」，AND 閘算出「進位」。每一位放一個加法器，把進位傳給左邊那一位，整個電路就能把兩個數加起來。

lab.how_en: The two back rows are the numbers A and B: tap their switches to set them. The front row is the answer. Each block marked + adds one column: a bit of A, a bit of B, and the carry from the block on its right. The answer changes the moment you flip a switch. Press Watch it add to clear the answer and see it worked out one column at a time, from right to left.
lab.how_zh: 後面兩排是 A 和 B 兩個數：點它們的開關來設定。最前面一排是答案。每個標著「＋」的方塊負責一位：A 的一個位元、B 的一個位元，加上右邊方塊傳過來的進位。你一撥開關，答案馬上跟著變。按「看它怎麼加」，答案會先清掉，再由右往左一位一位算給你看。

legend.en: Back rows: the numbers A and B, set by switches (light on = 1)
legend.zh: 後面兩排：用開關設定的 A 和 B（燈亮＝1）

legend.en: A block marked +: one full adder, for one column
legend.zh: 標著「＋」的方塊：一個全加器，負責一位

legend.en: Teal ball: a carry going to the next column on the left
legend.zh: 青色小球：進到左邊那一位的進位

legend.en: Front row: the answer, with a fifth light worth 16 for the last carry
legend.zh: 最前面一排：答案；第五盞燈代表 16，用來放最後的進位

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. In a real chip there are no bulbs and no balls: each block is a handful of transistors, and a carry is just a wire that is on or off. The model shows the columns one after another so you can follow them; in a real adder every column works at once, and only the carries have to wait for the column on their right. This adder is four bits wide. Real processors use the same idea on much longer rows of bits. The arithmetic is exact for every pair of numbers from 0 to 15.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。真的晶片裡沒有燈泡也沒有小球：每個方塊是幾個電晶體，進位只是一條「有電或沒電」的線。模型把每一位排隊做給你看；真的加法器每一位是同時在算的，只有進位得等右邊那一位算好。這台加法器只有四位，真的處理器用同樣的想法處理長得多的一排位元。0 到 15 的每一對數，模型算出來的都是精確的。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The adder is built only from the AND, OR, and XOR of Lesson 3 and is checked against real addition in tools/computers/test/adder.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫。加法器只用第三課的 AND、OR、XOR 做成，並在 tools/computers/test/adder.test.mjs 裡和真正的加法逐一核對。

paras: Lesson 3 ended with a promise: logic gates, which only answer yes or no, can add. That sounds odd. AND, OR, and NOT know nothing about numbers. But Lesson 1 showed that a number is only a row of switches, and adding is a job you can do one column at a time. If gates can handle one column, a row of them can handle the whole sum.

Start with the smallest problem: add two bits. There are only four cases. 0 + 0 is 0, 0 + 1 is 1, 1 + 0 is 1, and 1 + 1 is two, which in binary is written 10: write 0 and carry 1. Now look at what you write down in each case: 0, 1, 1, 0. That is the table for XOR. Look at the carry: 0, 0, 0, 1. That is the table for AND. So one XOR gate and one AND gate, side by side, add two bits. This small circuit is called a half adder.

A half adder is enough for the column on the far right. Every other column has a third number to add: the carry coming in from its right. A circuit that adds three bits is called a full adder. It can be built from two half adders and an OR gate. Its hardest case is 1 + 1 + 1, which is three, written 11 in binary: write 1 and carry 1.

Now give every column its own full adder, and connect each carry out to the carry in of the column on its left. That is a complete adding machine. Try 0111 + 0001 in the model. The right column makes a carry, the next column passes it on, and so does the next, until it lands in the fourth column: 1000. This is the same falling-domino carry you saw in Lesson 1. Because the carry ripples along, engineers call this a ripple-carry adder.

People built adding machines long before electronics. About 1642, the French mathematician Blaise Pascal designed one that added by turning wheels, to help his father, a tax collector. Nearly three hundred years later, George Stibitz of Bell Laboratories took two telephone relays, which are switches worked by electricity, some flashlight bulbs, and strips cut from a tobacco can, and made a circuit that added two binary digits. He built it at home on his kitchen table, so it became known as the Model K.

The adder inside a processor today works on many more bits at once than our four: 16, 32, or 64, depending on the computer. Its designers also use clever circuits that work out the carries ahead of time, so the answer does not have to wait for a long ripple. The idea has not changed. This is also the end of Unit 1. You started with one switch, on or off. A row of switches became a number. Codes turned numbers into words, pictures, and sound. Gates answered questions, and now gates add. Everything else a computer does is built from these few ideas.
paras_zh: 第三課最後留下一句話：只會回答「是或不是」的邏輯閘，可以做加法。聽起來很奇怪，AND、OR、NOT 根本不懂什麼是數。可是第一課說過，一個數只不過是一排開關；而加法是一件可以一位一位做的事。只要邏輯閘處理得了一位，一排邏輯閘就處理得了整個加法。
先從最小的問題開始：把兩個位元加起來。一共只有四種情況：0＋0 是 0，0＋1 是 1，1＋0 是 1，1＋1 是二，二進位寫成 10，也就是寫 0、進 1。現在看看每一種情況你寫下來的那個數字：0、1、1、0，這正是 XOR 的真值表。再看進位：0、0、0、1，這正是 AND 的真值表。所以一個 XOR 閘和一個 AND 閘並排，就能把兩個位元加起來。這個小電路叫做「半加器」。
最右邊那一位用半加器就夠了。其他每一位都多了第三個數要加：從右邊進過來的進位。能把三個位元加起來的電路叫做「全加器」，它可以用兩個半加器和一個 OR 閘做出來。它最難的一種情況是 1＋1＋1，也就是三，二進位寫成 11：寫 1、進 1。
現在給每一位一個自己的全加器，再把每一位的「進位出去」接到左邊那一位的「進位進來」，就是一台完整的加法機了。在模型裡試試 0111＋0001：最右邊那一位產生進位，下一位把它傳下去，再下一位也一樣，最後落在第四位，得到 1000。這就是第一課看過的、像骨牌一樣倒過去的進位。因為進位是像漣漪一樣一位一位傳過去的，工程師把這種電路叫做「漣波進位加法器」。

早在有電子零件之前，人們就做過加法機。大約 1642 年，法國數學家巴斯卡為了幫當稅務官的父親，設計了一台轉動輪子來做加法的機器。將近三百年後，貝爾實驗室的喬治・史提比茲（George Stibitz）拿了兩個電話用的繼電器（用電來控制的開關）、幾個手電筒燈泡，還有從菸草罐上剪下來的金屬片，做出一個能把兩個二進位數字加起來的電路。他是在自家廚房的桌子上做的，所以後來大家叫它「K 型」（K 就是 kitchen，廚房）。
今天處理器裡的加法器，一次處理的位元比我們這四位多得多：16、32 或 64 位，看是哪一種電腦。設計的人還用了聰明的電路，事先把進位算出來，答案就不必等一長串的進位慢慢傳完。但想法沒有變。單元一也到這裡結束。你從一個開關開始，它不是開就是關；一排開關變成一個數；編碼把數變成文字、圖片和聲音；邏輯閘會回答問題，現在邏輯閘還會做加法。電腦做的其他每一件事，都是用這幾個想法搭起來的。
questions: Which two gates make a half adder, and what does each one give?
Why does every column except the rightmost need a full adder instead of a half adder?
What happens when you add 0111 and 0001, and why is it called a ripple?
answers: An XOR gate and an AND gate. The XOR gives the sum digit to write down, and the AND gives the carry.
Because those columns have three bits to add: one from each number and the carry coming in from the column on the right. A half adder can add only two.

The right column makes a carry, and each column passes a carry to the next until it reaches the fourth column, giving 1000. The carry moves along one column at a time, like a ripple or a row of falling dominoes.

vocab.exzh: 5 和 3 的和是 8。

vocab.ex: An adder is a circuit that adds binary numbers.
vocab.exzh: 加法器是把二進位的數加起來的電路。

vocab.ex: The news rippled through the school in minutes.
vocab.exzh: 這個消息幾分鐘內就傳遍了全校。

vocab.ex: Connect the printer to the computer with this cable.
vocab.exzh: 用這條線把印表機接到電腦上。

vocab.ex: A relay is a switch that is turned on and off by electricity.
vocab.exzh: 繼電器是用電來控制開和關的開關。

vocab.ex: Before batteries, clocks were mechanical and had to be wound.
vocab.exzh: 在有電池以前，鐘是機械的，要上發條。

vocab.exzh: 你可以算出該找我多少錢嗎？

In a half adder, which gate gives the carry?
How many bits does a full adder add together?
