parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: No column has two 1s. Watch each block work alone, with nothing passed along.
parts.text_zh: 沒有哪一位同時有兩個 1。看每個方塊各算各的，什麼都不用傳。

parts.text_en: The smallest sum that needs a carry. Where does the 1 end up?
parts.text_zh: 需要進位的最小的加法。那個 1 最後跑到哪裡去了？

parts.text_en: In slow motion, count how many blocks the carry passes through.
parts.text_zh: 用慢動作看，數數進位經過了幾個方塊。

parts.text_en: Fifteen plus one. Watch the last carry leave the fourth block. Where can it go?
parts.text_zh: 十五加一。看最後的進位離開第四個方塊：它能去哪裡？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then set your own numbers. What is the biggest answer this adder can give, and how many lights does it take?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己設兩個數。這台加法器最大能算出多少？需要幾盞燈來顯示？

half.lead_en: Tap A and B to set them to 0 or 1 and watch the two outputs. Then switch to the full adder, which has a third input for the carry coming in. The table shows every possible case, and the row you are on is highlighted.
half.lead_zh: 點 A 和 B，把它們設成 0 或 1，看兩個輸出怎麼變。再切到全加器，它多了第三個輸入：進來的進位。表格列出每一種可能的情況，你現在在哪一列會亮起來。

tips.en: Read the two outputs together as one binary number: carry first, then sum. 10 is two, and 11 is three.
tips.zh: 把兩個輸出合起來當成一個二進位的數來讀：先進位、再和。10 是二，11 是三。

tips.en: A half adder uses 2 gates and a full adder uses 5. The four-bit adder in the model uses 4 full adders: 20 gates.
tips.zh: 半加器用 2 個閘，全加器用 5 個閘。模型裡的四位元加法器用了 4 個全加器，一共 20 個閘。

tips.en: In a full adder, the carry is 1 whenever at least two of the three inputs are 1.
tips.zh: 在全加器裡，三個輸入中只要至少有兩個是 1，進位就是 1。

addq.lead_en: Two sums, four columns each. Start at the right. For each column, add the two bits and the carry, then choose what to write and what to carry. The game counts how many columns you get right on the first try.
addq.lead_zh: 兩道加法，每道四位。從最右邊開始。每一位把兩個位元和進位加起來，再選要寫什麼、進什麼。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾格。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Adding Machines · 加法機的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Gears for a tax collector, a kitchen table, one gate for everything, and the adder’s home
culture_cards.title_zh: 替稅務官做的齒輪、一張廚房的桌子、一種閘做出全部、加法器住的地方
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about machines that add.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於會做加法的機器的四個小故事。

cards.en: An adding machine with wheels
cards.body_en: Blaise Pascal designed and built his machine between 1642 and 1644 for his father, a tax collector. Numbers were entered by turning its dials, and it could only add and subtract. Britannica calls it the first calculator or adding machine to be produced in any quantity and actually used: Pascal built 50 of them over the next ten years. It counted in tens, not twos, and it was made of moving parts, not switches.
cards.body_zh: 巴斯卡在 1642 到 1644 年之間，為當稅務官的父親設計並製造了這台機器。用轉盤把數撥進去，它只會加和減。大英百科說，它是第一種有一定產量、而且真的有人使用的計算機：之後十年間巴斯卡造了 50 台。它用的是十進位，不是二進位；裡面是會動的機械零件，不是開關。

cards.en: The adder on the kitchen table
cards.body_en: One weekend at home, George Stibitz of Bell Laboratories fastened two relays from the laboratory’s scrap pile to a piece of plywood, added flashlight bulbs and strips cut from a tobacco can, and had a one-digit binary adder. It was named the Model K, for the kitchen table it was built on. Most accounts date it to 1937; some say 1936. The Computer History Museum says it proved that Boolean logic could be used to design computers.
cards.body_zh: 某個週末，貝爾實驗室的喬治・史提比茲在家裡，把兩個從實驗室廢料堆撿來的繼電器釘在一塊夾板上，加上手電筒燈泡和從菸草罐剪下來的金屬片，做出一個一位的二進位加法器。它叫做 Model K，K 就是它誕生的那張廚房（kitchen）桌子。大多數資料說這是 1937 年的事，也有說 1936 年的。電腦歷史博物館說，它證明了布林邏輯可以用來設計電腦。

cards.en: One kind of gate is enough
cards.body_en: The adder in this lesson uses three kinds of gates: AND, OR, and XOR. Surprisingly, a chip does not need three kinds. A NAND gate is an AND followed by a NOT, and every other gate can be built out of NAND gates alone. So a whole adder, and in principle a whole computer, can be made by repeating one tiny part again and again.
cards.body_zh: 這一課的加法器用了三種閘：AND、OR、XOR。讓人意外的是，晶片並不需要三種。NAND 閘就是 AND 後面接一個 NOT，而其他每一種閘都可以只用 NAND 閘做出來。所以一整個加法器，原則上連一整台電腦，都可以靠同一個小零件一再重複做出來。

cards.en: Where the adder lives
cards.body_en: Inside a processor, the adder is part of a section called the arithmetic logic unit, or ALU. The same section also holds the circuits for the logic of Lesson 3. When a program adds two numbers, compares them, or combines them with AND or OR, the work is done here. You will meet the rest of the processor in Unit 2.
cards.body_zh: 在處理器裡，加法器屬於一個叫做「算術邏輯單元」（ALU）的部分，第三課的邏輯運算電路也在這裡。程式要把兩個數加起來、比大小，或用 AND、OR 把它們合起來的時候，工作就是在這裡做的。處理器其他的部分，單元二會看到。

myths.myth_en: A computer looks up the answer to a sum, the way you remember that 7 + 8 is 15.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦是用「查」的，就像你背得出 7＋8＝15。
myths.fact_en: There is nothing to remember. The answer falls out of the wiring: each column’s gates produce a sum bit and a carry, every time, for any two numbers.
myths.fact_zh: 它沒有背任何東西。答案是從接線裡自己跑出來的：每一位的閘都會算出一個和、一個進位，不管是哪兩個數，每次都一樣。

myths.myth_en: In binary, 1 + 1 = 10 means one plus one is ten.
myths.myth_zh: 二進位的 1＋1＝10，意思是一加一等於十。
myths.fact_en: The amount is still two. “10” is how two is written with binary digits: one in the twos place and zero in the ones place.
myths.fact_zh: 數量還是二。「10」只是二用二進位寫出來的樣子：「二」那一位是 1，「一」那一位是 0。

myths.myth_en: The adder works on one column at a time, like a person with a pencil.
myths.myth_zh: 加法器跟拿筆算的人一樣，一次只做一位。
myths.fact_en: All the columns are wired up at once, and every block starts working as soon as its inputs arrive. Only the carries have to wait, because each one depends on the column to its right.
myths.fact_zh: 每一位的線路都是同時接好的，輸入一到，每個方塊就開始工作。要等的只有進位，因為每個進位都得看右邊那一位的結果。

myths.myth_en: Adding bigger numbers needs a smarter kind of circuit.
myths.myth_zh: 要加更大的數，就需要更聰明的電路。
myths.fact_en: It needs more of the same. Each extra column is one more full adder, and each extra column doubles the largest number the adder can take.
myths.fact_zh: 需要的是更多同樣的東西。每多一位就多一個全加器，而每多一位，加法器能處理的最大的數就加倍。

tricks.title_en: Sum is XOR, carry is AND
tricks.body_en: Two gates add two bits: a half adder.
tricks.body_zh: 兩個閘就能加兩個位元：半加器。

tricks.body_en: A full adder adds A, B, and the carry in. It gives a sum and a carry out.
tricks.body_zh: 全加器把 A、B 和進來的進位加起來，給出一個和、一個出去的進位。

tricks.body_en: Each column hands its carry to the next, like falling dominoes.
tricks.body_zh: 每一位把進位交給下一位，像骨牌一樣倒過去。

tricks.body_en: In one column: none is 0, one is 1, two is 10, three is 11.
tricks.body_zh: 只看一位：沒有是 0，一個是 1，兩個是 10，三個是 11。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: If your class builds an adder with real switches and bulbs, use only small batteries, and never the wall socket.
safety.zh: 如果班上要用真的開關和燈泡做加法器，只能用小電池，絕對不要用牆上的插座。

safety.en: Never join the two ends of a battery directly with a wire. The wire and the battery can get hot very quickly.
safety.zh: 絕對不要用一條線直接把電池的兩頭接在一起，電線和電池會很快變燙。

safety.en: In the developer console, type only what this lesson shows, and never paste in code that someone else tells you to paste.
safety.zh: 在開發人員主控台裡，只輸入這一課寫的那幾行；別人叫你貼的程式碼絕對不要貼。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission, and do not change its settings.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意，也不要更改設定。

materials.en: Eight cards showing 0 on one side and 1 on the other
materials.zh: 八張卡片，一面寫 0、一面寫 1

materials.en: Four small balls or beanbags, to be the carries
materials.zh: 四顆小球或沙包，當作進位

materials.en: Space for four students to stand in a row facing the class
materials.zh: 讓四位同學面向全班站成一排的空間

steps.en: Four students stand in a row. Each one is the adder for one column: 8, 4, 2, and 1, as the class sees them from left to right.
steps.zh: 四位同學站成一排，每人負責一位。從全班看過去，由左到右是 8、4、2、1。

steps.en: The teacher gives each student two cards, one bit of A and one bit of B. For example, 0111 and 0001.
steps.zh: 老師發給每位同學兩張卡片：A 的一個位元和 B 的一個位元。例如 0111 和 0001。

steps.en: Start with the student on the class’s right. Count your 1s, including a ball if someone hands you one. With two or three 1s, pass a ball to the student on your left.
steps.zh: 從全班看過去最右邊的同學開始。數數自己有幾個 1（有人交球給你的話，球也算一個）。有兩個或三個 1，就把一顆球交給自己左邊的同學。

steps.en: Then show your answer: raise a hand if your count was one or three, and keep it down if it was zero or two. The class reads the four hands as a binary number.
steps.zh: 接著比出自己的答案：數到一個或三個就舉手，零個或兩個就不舉。全班把四隻手當成一個二進位的數讀出來。

activities.tip_en: Nobody in the row knows what the whole sum is. Each student only counts to three and follows two rules, and the right answer still appears. That is exactly how the adder in a chip works. Try 1111 + 0001 and ask where the last ball should go. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, adders are not listed by name; this lesson supports the topic “System platforms” (資 S-IV-2, how system platforms are built and basically work).
activities.tip_zh: 這一排人沒有一個知道整個加法是多少。每個人只數到三、照兩條規則做，正確答案還是出現了。晶片裡的加法器就是這樣工作的。試試 1111＋0001，問問大家最後那顆球該交給誰。十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容沒有直接列出加法器；這一課可以用來支援「系統平台」主題（資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A Windows or Mac computer with its Calculator app
materials.zh: 一台 Windows 或 Mac 電腦，以及內建的「計算機」

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: On paper, add 0101 and 0011 in binary, one column at a time from the right. Write the carries above the columns.
steps.zh: 先在紙上用二進位算 0101＋0011，從右邊開始一位一位加，把進位寫在每一位的上面。

steps.en: Open Calculator in programmer mode, as you did in Lesson 1. On a Mac, choose View > Programmer and click Show Binary. On Windows, choose Programmer from the menu.
steps.zh: 照第一課的方法，把「計算機」切換到程式設計的模式。Mac：選「顯示方式」＞「程式設計」，再按「顯示二進位」。Windows：在選單裡選「程式設計人員」。

steps.en: Type 5 + 3 and press =. Read the binary line and compare it with your paper.
steps.zh: 輸入 5＋3 再按 =。看二進位那一行，和你紙上的答案比一比。

steps.en: Try 7 + 1, and then 15 + 1. Find the carry in each answer.
steps.zh: 再試 7＋1，然後 15＋1。在每個答案裡找出進位。

activities.tip_en: The answers are 1000, 1000, and 10000. For a second check, open a browser’s developer console and type (0b0101 + 0b0011).toString(2). In JavaScript, a number that starts with 0b is written in binary. The console answers "1000".
activities.tip_zh: 答案分別是 1000、1000、10000。還有第二種驗證法：打開瀏覽器的開發人員主控台，輸入 (0b0101 + 0b0011).toString(2)。在 JavaScript 裡，0b 開頭的數就是用二進位寫的。主控台會回答 "1000"。

links_head.zh: 邏輯閘、進位，以及下一個單元

links.en: How Does a Computer Make a Decision?

links.note_zh: 每個加法方塊裡的 AND、OR、XOR，都是從這一課來的。

links.en: Why Do Computers Use Only 0 and 1?
links.zh: 電腦為什麼只用 0 和 1？
links.note_en: Go back and press Count up. Adding one, again and again, is the same carry you just built out of gates.
links.note_zh: 回去按一次「往上數」。一次又一次地加一，就是你剛才用邏輯閘做出來的那個進位。

links.note_en: Unit 1 built numbers, codes, gates, and an adder. Next, open the case and see where they all live.
links.note_zh: 單元一做出了數、編碼、邏輯閘和加法器。接下來打開機殼，看看它們都住在哪裡。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); every sum in the model is computed from gates and tested against real addition
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代與事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；模型裡的每一個加法都是用邏輯閘算的，並和真正的加法核對過

sources.en: Half adder: adds two bits; its sum and carry are identical to the Xor and And functions. Full adder: adds three bits, and can be built from two half adders and one more gate. An n-bit adder is an array of n full adders that passes the carries up
sources.zh: 半加器：把兩個位元相加，「和」與「進位」正好就是 XOR 與 AND。全加器：把三個位元相加，可以用兩個半加器再加一個閘做成。n 位元加法器是 n 個全加器排成一排，把進位往上傳
sources.src: Noam Nisan and Shimon Schocken, The Elements of Computing Systems, chapter 2, “Boolean Arithmetic”

sources.en: A full adder “can be built out of two half-adders and an OR gate”
sources.zh: 全加器「可以用兩個半加器和一個 OR 閘做出來」
sources.src: Justin Wyss-Gallifent, “CMSC 250: Adder Circuits,” University of Maryland

sources.en: “The carry ‘ripples’ from one bit to the next,” so the time needed grows with the number of bits; faster adders such as carry lookahead exist
sources.zh: 進位從一位「漣漪般」傳到下一位，所以位數越多越花時間；另有進位前瞻等更快的加法器
sources.src: Allan Gottlieb, Computer Architecture class notes, New York University

sources.en: Computers handle n-bit patterns, “n being 16, 32, 64, and so forth”; carry look-ahead techniques ease the delay of the carry; every Boolean function can be constructed from Nand operations alone (chapter 1)
sources.zh: 電腦處理 n 位元的資料，n 是 16、32、64 等等；進位前瞻的技巧可以減少等進位的時間；每一個布林函數都可以只用 NAND 做出來（第一章）
sources.src: Nisan and Schocken, The Elements of Computing Systems, chapters 1 and 2

sources.en: The Pascaline: designed and built by Blaise Pascal between 1642 and 1644 for his father, a tax collector; it could only add and subtract; the first calculator produced in any quantity and actually used; he built 50 over the next 10 years
sources.zh: Pascaline：巴斯卡在 1642 到 1644 年間為當稅務官的父親設計製造；只會加和減；第一種有一定產量且真正被使用的計算機；之後十年造了 50 台
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Pascaline”

sources.en: Stibitz fastened two relays from the Bell Labs scrap pile to plywood, with strips from a tobacco can and flashlight bulbs, to make a one-digit binary adder, one weekend at home in 1937; called the Model K for the kitchen table
sources.zh: 史提比茲 1937 年某個週末在家，把兩個貝爾實驗室廢料堆的繼電器釘在夾板上，加上菸草罐的金屬片與手電筒燈泡，做出一位的二進位加法器；因廚房桌子而稱 Model K
sources.src: IEEE Computer Society, Computer Pioneers, “George Robert Stibitz”

sources.en: The “Model K” adder, named for his kitchen table, proved the concept of applying Boolean logic to the design of computers (the museum’s replica page gives 1936 for the original)
sources.zh: Model K 加法器因廚房桌子得名，證明了布林邏輯可以用來設計電腦（博物館的複製品頁面寫原件是 1936 年）
sources.src: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History, 1937

sources.en: The arithmetic logic unit is the part of the processor that performs arithmetic and logic operations on binary numbers
sources.zh: 算術邏輯單元是處理器裡對二進位的數做算術與邏輯運算的部分
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “arithmetic logic unit”

sources.en: In JavaScript, a number starting with 0b is written in binary; toString(2) writes a number in binary
sources.zh: 在 JavaScript 裡，0b 開頭的數是二進位寫法；toString(2) 把數寫成二進位
sources.src: MDN Web Docs, “Lexical grammar” and “Number.prototype.toString()”

sources.en: Mac: View > Programmer, then Show Binary; Windows Calculator has a Programmer mode
sources.zh: Mac：「顯示方式」＞「程式設計」，再按「顯示二進位」；Windows 計算機有「程式設計人員」模式
sources.src: Apple Support, “Use the programmer calculator on Mac”; Microsoft, Windows Calculator

sources.en: A short circuit across a battery generates high heat
sources.zh: 電池短路會產生高熱
sources.src: Energizer, Alkaline Manganese Dioxide Handbook and Application Manual

sources.en: Taiwan terms: half adder 半加器, full adder 全加器, adder 加法器, carry 進位, overflow 溢位, ripple carry adder 漣波進位加法器, arithmetic logic unit 算術邏輯單元, relay 繼電器
sources.zh: 台灣用語：half adder 半加器、full adder 全加器、adder 加法器、carry 進位、overflow 溢位、ripple carry adder 漣波進位加法器、arithmetic logic unit 算術邏輯單元、relay 繼電器（電子計算機名詞等）
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《樂詞網》

sources.en: 資 S-IV-2, how system platforms are built and basically work (p. 10); adders are not listed by name
sources.zh: 資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（第 10 頁）；學習內容沒有直接列出加法器
sources.src: 教育部《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校 科技領域》（2018）
sources.url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/816/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校-科技領域.pdf

sources.en: The four cases of a half adder and the eight of a full adder; all 256 sums of two numbers from 0 to 15; 2 gates in a half adder, 5 in a full adder, 20 in the model; the examples 0101 + 0010, 0111 + 0001, and 1111 + 0001
sources.zh: 半加器的四種情況、全加器的八種情況；0 到 15 兩兩相加的 256 種結果；半加器 2 個閘、全加器 5 個、模型 20 個；例子 0101＋0010、0111＋0001、1111＋0001
sources.src: Our own work, checked by tools/computers/test/adder.test.mjs

units.blurb_en: Open the case: what each part does, what a processor is busy with all day, why there are two kinds of memory, and what happens when you press one key.
units.blurb_zh: 打開機殼：每個零件各做什麼、處理器整天在忙什麼、為什麼要有兩種記憶，以及按下一個鍵之後發生了什麼。

lessons.title: What Is Inside a Computer?
lessons.blurb_en: Take the side off a desktop computer in 3D and pull out its parts one by one: motherboard, processor, memory, storage, graphics card, and power supply. Press the power button and follow the data from part to part.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡拿掉桌上型電腦的側板，把零件一個一個拉出來看：主機板、處理器、記憶體、儲存裝置、顯示卡和電源供應器。再按下電源，跟著資料從一個零件走到另一個零件。
lessons.big_idea_en: A computer is a small team of parts, and each part has one job. The processor carries out instructions, memory holds what is in use right now, storage keeps things when the power is off, the graphics card makes the picture, the power supply feeds them all, and the motherboard connects everything.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電腦是一小隊零件，每個零件只做一件事。處理器執行指令，記憶體放現在正在用的東西，儲存裝置在關機後把東西留住，顯示卡把畫面做出來，電源供應器供電給大家，主機板把所有零件連在一起。

lab.title_en: A Computer with Its Side Off
lab.how_en: This is a desktop computer with one side panel removed. Tap any part to light it up and read what it does, or use the slider to pull the parts out of the case. Then press the power button to watch four steps: power goes to every part, a program is copied from storage into memory, the processor does its work, and the graphics card draws the picture for the screen.
lab.how_zh: 這是一台拿掉一片側板的桌上型電腦。點任何一個零件，它會亮起來，右邊說明它做什麼；也可以拉滑桿，把零件從機殼裡拉出來。接著按下電源，看四個步驟：電送到每個零件、程式從儲存裝置複製到記憶體、處理器開始工作、顯示卡把畫面畫出來給螢幕顯示。

parts.job_en: The largest board in the case. Every other part plugs into it, and the thin copper lines on it connect the parts so that they can pass data to one another.
parts.job_zh: 機殼裡最大的一塊板子。其他每個零件都插在它上面，板子上細細的銅線把零件連起來，讓它們能互相傳資料。
parts.note_en: It is like the streets of a town: it does none of the work itself, but nothing can reach anything else without it. Unlike streets, its paths are fixed when it is made, and each part fits only the socket built for it.
parts.note_zh: 它像一座城鎮的街道：自己不做事，可是沒有它，誰也到不了誰那裡。和街道不同的是，它的路在製造時就固定了，每個零件只能插進為它做的那個插槽。

parts.job_en: Carries out the instructions of programs, one after another. The adding and deciding from Lessons 3 and 4 happen inside this small square.
parts.job_zh: 一條接一條地執行程式的指令。第三課的「做決定」和第四課的「做加法」，就發生在這一小片方形的東西裡。
parts.note_en: People call it the brain of the computer. Unlike a brain, it does not think or understand. It follows instructions exactly, very fast.
parts.note_zh: 大家常說它是電腦的大腦。和大腦不同的是，它不會思考、也不懂意思，只是一字不差地照指令做，而且做得非常快。

parts.job_en: A block of metal fins with a fan. It carries heat away from the processor so that the processor does not get too hot.
parts.job_zh: 一塊金屬鰭片加上一個風扇，把處理器的熱帶走，讓處理器不會太燙。
parts.note_en: When people open a computer, this is the big thing they notice, and many take it for the processor. The processor is the small square hidden underneath.
parts.note_zh: 打開電腦時，大家最先注意到的就是這一大塊，很多人以為它就是處理器。處理器其實是藏在它底下的那一小片。

parts.job_en: Holds the programs and data that are in use right now, where the processor can reach them quickly. It is wiped when the power goes off.
parts.job_zh: 放著現在正在用的程式和資料，處理器可以很快拿到。電一關，裡面的東西就清空。
parts.note_en: It is like the top of your desk: quick to reach, but limited, and cleared at the end of the day. Unlike a desk, it empties the instant the power is gone.
parts.note_zh: 它像你的桌面：伸手就拿得到，可是放不多，放學就要收乾淨。和桌面不同的是，電一斷，它一瞬間就空了。

parts.job_en: Keeps programs and files even when the power is off. This one is a solid-state drive, which stores data in chips and has no moving parts.
parts.job_zh: 就算關了電，也把程式和檔案留著。這一個是固態硬碟，把資料存在晶片裡，沒有任何會動的零件。
parts.note_en: It is like a bookcase: it holds far more than the desk, but fetching from it takes longer. Some computers use a hard disk drive, with spinning disks inside, for the same job.
parts.note_zh: 它像書櫃：放得比桌面多得多，可是去拿要花比較久。有些電腦用的是硬碟，裡面有會轉的碟片，做的是同一件事。

parts.job_en: Draws the picture that the screen shows. In many computers this job is done by graphics built into the processor, with no separate card.
parts.job_zh: 把螢幕要顯示的畫面畫出來。很多電腦沒有獨立的顯示卡，這件事由內建在處理器裡的顯示功能來做。
parts.note_en: Lesson 2 said a picture is a grid of pixels, each with three numbers. This is the part that works those numbers out for the whole screen.
parts.note_zh: 第二課說過，一張圖是一格一格的像素，每個像素有三個數。替整個螢幕把這些數算出來的，就是這個零件。

parts.job_en: Changes the electricity from the wall socket into the low voltages the parts need, such as 12, 5, and 3.3 volts, and sends it to them.
parts.job_zh: 把牆上插座來的電，變成零件需要的低電壓（例如 12、5、3.3 伏特），再送給各個零件。
parts.note_en: It is the one part that takes wall electricity directly, at 100 to 240 volts. It is a sealed box, and it is not meant to be opened. Leave it closed.
parts.note_zh: 它是唯一直接接牆上的電（100 到 240 伏特）的零件。它是一個封起來的盒子，本來就不是要讓人打開的。不要去拆它。

boot.en: The power supply changes the electricity from the wall into low voltages and sends it to the parts.
boot.zh: 電源供應器把牆上來的電變成低電壓，送給各個零件。

boot.en: The program you asked for is copied from storage into memory, where the processor can reach it quickly.
boot.zh: 你要用的程式從儲存裝置複製到記憶體，處理器在那裡才拿得快。

boot.en: The processor takes instructions from memory one after another, carries them out, and puts the results back. The cooler carries its heat away.
boot.zh: 處理器從記憶體一條一條拿出指令、照著做，再把結果放回去。散熱器把它的熱帶走。

boot.en: The results go to the graphics card, which draws the picture, pixel by pixel, for the screen to show.
boot.zh: 結果送到顯示卡，顯示卡一個像素一個像素把畫面畫出來，交給螢幕顯示。

legend.en: A lit part: the one you picked, or one that is busy in this step
legend.zh: 亮起來的零件：你選的那一個，或這一步正在忙的零件

legend.en: Green board at the back: the motherboard, which everything plugs into
legend.zh: 後面那塊綠色的板子：主機板，所有零件都插在它上面

legend.en: Moving dots: power (gold) or data (teal) going from one part to another
legend.zh: 會動的光點：從一個零件送到另一個零件的電（金色）或資料（青色）

legend.en: Screen beside the case: lights up when the picture arrives
legend.zh: 機殼旁邊的螢幕：畫面送到時亮起來

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not a picture of any real product. Real parts come in many shapes and sizes, and a real case is crowded with cables, which are left out here. In a real computer the data travels through copper lines inside the motherboard, not through the air, and far too fast to see. A real start-up also has many more steps than these four. What each part does is real.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型，不是任何一個真實產品的樣子。真的零件有各種形狀和大小，真的機殼裡還擠滿了線，這裡都省略了。在真的電腦裡，資料是走主機板裡面的銅線，不是在空中飛，而且快到看不見。真的開機過程也比這四個步驟多得多。但每個零件做的事是真的。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The model is generic and does not show any maker’s product.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫。模型是通用的示意，不代表任何廠牌的產品。

paras: In Unit 1 you built the ideas a computer runs on: switches, numbers, codes, logic gates, and an adder. Now it is time to open the box and see where those ideas live. You might expect something mysterious inside. What you find is a small team of parts. Each part has one job, and one big board holds them all together.

That board is the motherboard. It is the largest board inside the case, and every other part plugs into it. Thin copper lines run across it and connect the parts, so that they can pass data to one another. The motherboard does not do any calculating itself. Its job is to connect.

The most important part plugged into the motherboard is the processor, also called the CPU. It carries out the instructions of programs, one after another. All the adding and deciding you saw in Lessons 3 and 4 happens here, on one small chip. Its transistors turn electrical energy into heat as they work, so a block of metal fins and a fan sit on top of the processor to carry the heat away.

A computer has two places to keep things, and they are easy to mix up. Memory, or RAM, holds the programs and data that are in use right now. It is fast, but it loses everything when the power is turned off. Storage keeps your programs and files even when the computer is off. In many computers today the storage is a solid-state drive, which keeps data in chips and has no moving parts. Others use a hard disk, with disks that spin.

Two more parts finish the team. The graphics card draws the picture that you see, working out the color of every pixel. In many computers this job is done by graphics built into the processor, with no separate card. The power supply takes electricity from the wall socket and changes it into the low voltages that the other parts need.

Now watch the team work. When you open an app, it is copied from storage into memory. The processor takes its instructions from memory and carries them out. The graphics card draws the result as a picture for the screen. The power supply keeps every part running, and the motherboard connects them all. A laptop has the same kinds of parts, only smaller and packed closer together. Some chips even combine the processor, the graphics, and more in a single piece, called a system on a chip.
paras_zh: 在單元一，你把電腦運作靠的幾個想法都做出來了：開關、數、編碼、邏輯閘，還有加法器。現在該打開箱子，看看這些想法住在哪裡。你也許以為裡面會是什麼神祕的東西，結果看到的是一小隊零件。每個零件只做一件事，一塊大板子把它們全部連在一起。
那塊板子就是主機板。它是機殼裡最大的一塊板子，其他每個零件都插在它上面。板子上有細細的銅線把零件連起來，讓它們能互相傳資料。主機板自己不做任何計算，它的工作是「連接」。
插在主機板上最重要的零件是處理器，也叫 CPU。它一條接一條地執行程式的指令。第三課和第四課看到的那些「做決定」和「做加法」，全都發生在這裡，一片小小的晶片上。它裡面的電晶體工作時會把電能變成熱，所以處理器上面壓著一塊金屬鰭片和一個風扇，把熱帶走。
電腦有兩個放東西的地方，很容易搞混。記憶體（RAM）放的是現在正在用的程式和資料。它很快，可是電一關，裡面的東西就全部不見了。儲存裝置則是在電腦關機的時候，也把你的程式和檔案留住。現在很多電腦的儲存裝置是固態硬碟，把資料存在晶片裡，沒有任何會動的零件；也有的用硬碟，裡面有會轉的碟片。
還有兩個零件，這一隊才算到齊。顯示卡把你看到的畫面畫出來，每個像素的顏色都是它算的。很多電腦沒有獨立的顯示卡，這件事由內建在處理器裡的顯示功能來做。電源供應器從牆上的插座取電，把它變成其他零件需要的低電壓。
現在看看這一隊怎麼合作。你打開一個 App，它就從儲存裝置複製到記憶體。處理器從記憶體拿出它的指令，一條一條照著做。顯示卡把結果畫成畫面，交給螢幕。電源供應器讓每個零件都有電，主機板把它們全部連在一起。筆記型電腦裡也有同樣這幾種零件，只是比較小、擠得比較近。有些晶片甚至把處理器、顯示功能和更多東西做在同一顆裡面，叫做「系統單晶片」。
questions: What is the job of the motherboard?
How is memory different from storage?
What happens, step by step, when you open an app?
answers: It is the largest board in the case. Every other part plugs into it, and its copper lines connect the parts so that they can pass data to one another. It does not do any calculating itself.
Memory holds the programs and data in use right now. It is fast, but it loses everything when the power is turned off. Storage keeps programs and files even when the computer is off.
The app is copied from storage into memory. The processor takes its instructions from memory and carries them out. The graphics card draws the result as a picture for the screen.

vocab.ex: The engine is the most expensive component of the car.
vocab.exzh: 引擎是這輛車最貴的零件。

vocab.ex: Every part of the computer plugs into the motherboard.
vocab.exzh: 電腦的每個零件都插在主機板上。

vocab.ex: A faster processor can carry out more instructions each second.
vocab.exzh: 比較快的處理器每秒能執行比較多的指令。

vocab.ex: With too many apps open, the computer runs out of memory.
vocab.exzh: 開太多 App，電腦的記憶體就不夠用了。

vocab.ex: My phone has no storage left for new photos.
vocab.exzh: 我的手機沒有空間存新照片了。

vocab.ex: The game has beautiful graphics.
vocab.exzh: 這個遊戲的畫面很漂亮。

vocab.ex: The river supplies water to the whole city.
vocab.exzh: 這條河供應整座城市的用水。

vocab.exzh: 這間教室只是圖書館的書暫時放的地方。

parts.meta_zh: 一塊板子上的七個零件
parts.text_en: Watch the parts come out of the case. What are they all attached to?
parts.text_zh: 看零件從機殼裡被拉出來。它們全都接在什麼東西上？

parts.en: The cooler is not the processor
parts.meta_zh: 大大的鰭片，小小的晶片
parts.text_en: The biggest thing on the board is only there to carry heat away. Find the small square under it.
parts.text_zh: 板子上最大的那個東西，只是用來把熱帶走的。找找它底下那一小片。

parts.meta_zh: 記憶體會忘，儲存裝置留得住
parts.text_en: See memory and storage one after the other. Which one is wiped when the power goes off?
parts.text_zh: 先看記憶體，再看儲存裝置。哪一個在關電之後會清空？

parts.meta_en: Four steps, from socket to screen
parts.meta_zh: 四個步驟，從插座到螢幕
parts.text_en: Follow the dots: power first, then data from storage to memory, to the processor, and out to the screen.
parts.text_zh: 跟著光點走：先是電，接著資料從儲存裝置到記憶體、到處理器，最後送到螢幕。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then test yourself: with the labels switched off, can you name all seven parts?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著考考自己：把標示關掉，你說得出七個零件的名字嗎？

jobs.lead_en: Eight jobs, seven parts. Read each job and choose the part that does it. The game counts how many you get right on the first try.
jobs.lead_zh: 八件工作，七個零件。讀一讀每件工作，選出做這件事的零件。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾題。

tasks.en: It keeps your photos after the computer is switched off.
tasks.zh: 電腦關機以後，它還留著你的照片。
tasks.why_en: Storage keeps files without power.
tasks.why_zh: 儲存裝置不用電也留得住檔案。

tasks.en: It carries out the instructions of a program, such as adding 3 and 4.
tasks.zh: 它執行程式的指令，例如把 3 和 4 加起來。
tasks.why_en: Carrying out instructions is the processor’s job.
tasks.why_zh: 執行指令是處理器的工作。

tasks.en: It holds the app you are using right now, and loses it when the power goes off.
tasks.zh: 它放著你現在正在用的 App，電一關就不見了。
tasks.why_en: Memory holds what is in use, and it is wiped without power.
tasks.why_zh: 記憶體放正在用的東西，沒電就清空。

tasks.en: It draws the picture that the screen shows.
tasks.zh: 它把螢幕要顯示的畫面畫出來。
tasks.why_en: The graphics card draws the picture.
tasks.why_zh: 畫面是顯示卡畫出來的。

tasks.en: It changes electricity from the wall into the kind the parts can use.
tasks.zh: 它把牆上來的電，變成零件能用的電。
tasks.why_en: That is the power supply.
tasks.why_zh: 這是電源供應器。

tasks.en: It connects all the other parts so that they can pass data to one another.
tasks.zh: 它把其他所有零件連起來，讓它們能互相傳資料。
tasks.why_en: The motherboard connects everything.
tasks.why_zh: 把所有零件連在一起的是主機板。

tasks.en: It carries heat away from the processor.
tasks.zh: 它把處理器的熱帶走。
tasks.why_en: The cooler’s fins and fan move the heat away.
tasks.why_zh: 散熱器的鰭片和風扇把熱帶走。

tasks.en: When you install a game, this is where it is kept.
tasks.zh: 安裝一個遊戲的時候，遊戲就是放在這裡。
tasks.why_en: Installed programs live in storage until you open them.
tasks.why_zh: 安裝好的程式住在儲存裝置裡，打開時才載入記憶體。

fits.lead_en: The size of a drive is given in gigabytes (GB) or terabytes (TB). One gigabyte is one billion bytes, and a byte is eight of the switches from Lesson 1. Choose a drive and something to put on it.
fits.lead_zh: 儲存裝置的大小用 GB 或 TB 來表示。1 GB 是十億個位元組，而一個位元組就是第一課的八個開關。選一顆固態硬碟的大小，再選要放什麼。

items.size_zh: 一個英文字母占 1 個位元組（第二課）。

items.zh: 張 4,000 × 3,000 像素、沒有壓縮的照片
items.size_en: One such photo takes 36,000,000 bytes: 12 million pixels, 3 bytes each (Lesson 2). Real photo files are compressed and much smaller, as you will see in Lesson 12.
items.size_zh: 這樣一張照片占 36,000,000 個位元組：1,200 萬個像素，每個 3 個位元組（第二課）。真正的照片檔會壓縮，小得多，第十二課會講。

items.en: minutes of CD-quality sound, one channel
items.zh: 分鐘 CD 規格的聲音（一個聲道）
items.size_en: One minute takes 5,292,000 bytes: 44,100 measurements a second, 2 bytes each, for 60 seconds (Lesson 2).
items.size_zh: 一分鐘占 5,292,000 個位元組：每秒量 44,100 次、每次 2 個位元組，共 60 秒（第二課）。

fits.note_en: A computer may show a smaller number for the same drive. Windows, for example, counts in units of 1,073,741,824 bytes (2 to the 30th power) and still writes “GB.” Counted that way, this drive is
fits.note2_en: of those units. No space is missing; it is the same number of bytes, counted in bigger units.
fits.note_zh: 電腦顯示的數字可能比較小。例如 Windows 用 1,073,741,824 個位元組（2 的 30 次方）當一個單位，卻一樣寫「GB」。用這種算法，這顆硬碟是

tips.en: Kilo, mega, giga, tera: each step is a thousand times bigger. 1 TB is 1,000 GB.
tips.zh: KB、MB、GB、TB：每一級是前一級的一千倍。1 TB 是 1,000 GB。

tips.en: A 512 GB drive holds 4,096,000,000,000 bits. That is more than four trillion of the switches from Lesson 1.
tips.zh: 512 GB 的硬碟有 4,096,000,000,000 個位元，也就是四兆多個第一課的開關。

tips.en: Memory is measured in gigabytes too, but a computer has much less memory than storage.
tips.zh: 記憶體也是用 GB 來量，只是一台電腦的記憶體比儲存空間少得多。

fits.note2_zh: 個這樣的單位。空間沒有不見：位元組一樣多，只是用比較大的單位來數。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Parts · 零件的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A processor on one chip, a drive with nothing moving, two kinds of gigabyte, and a coffee shop in Taipei
culture_cards.title_zh: 一顆晶片上的處理器、沒有東西在動的硬碟、兩種 GB、台北的一家咖啡店
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about the parts inside the case.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 機殼裡這些零件的四個小故事。

cards.en: The processor on a single chip
cards.zh: 做在一顆晶片上的處理器
cards.body_en: Early computers needed many separate parts to do the work of a processor. In 1971 Intel introduced the 4004, which became the first general-purpose microprocessor: a processor on one chip. Today’s processors do the same basic job of interpreting and carrying out program instructions, with vastly more transistors. The chip lessons on this site tell that part of the story.
cards.body_zh: 早期的電腦要用很多分開的零件，才做得了處理器的工作。1971 年，英特爾推出 4004，它成為第一顆通用的微處理器：做在一顆晶片上的處理器。今天的處理器做的還是同一件基本的事（看懂並執行程式的指令），只是電晶體多了非常非常多。這一段故事，本站的晶片系列有講。

cards.en: A drive with nothing moving
cards.body_en: A hard disk drive stores data on a spinning platter, with an arm that moves across it. A solid-state drive stores data in chips of flash memory instead, so it does not rely on any moving parts. Both do the same job for the computer: they are its long-term storage, remembering files even when the device is off.
cards.body_zh: 硬碟把資料存在會轉的碟片上，還有一支讀寫臂在碟片上移動。固態硬碟改用快閃記憶體晶片來存資料，所以不靠任何會動的零件。對電腦來說，兩者做的是同一件事：當它長期存放東西的地方，就算關機也記得檔案。

cards.en: Why a 1 TB drive shows as 931 GB
cards.zh: 為什麼 1 TB 的硬碟顯示成 931 GB
cards.body_en: Drive makers count in tens: one gigabyte is 1,000,000,000 bytes. But some software counts in twos and treats a “gigabyte” as 1,073,741,824 bytes. To end the confusion, a standard approved in 1998 gave the binary units their own names, such as gibibyte (GiB). Seagate notes that people are often confused when a 1 TB drive is reported as only about 931 gigabytes. Nothing is missing: 1,000,000,000,000 bytes is about 931 GiB.
cards.body_zh: 硬碟廠商用十進位來數：1 GB 是 1,000,000,000 個位元組。可是有些軟體用二進位來數，把「1 GB」當成 1,073,741,824 個位元組。為了不再混淆，1998 年通過的一項標準替二進位的單位另外取了名字，例如 gibibyte（GiB）。希捷（Seagate）提到，1 TB 的硬碟被顯示成只有大約 931 GB 時，很多人會搞不清楚。其實什麼都沒少：1,000,000,000,000 個位元組，大約就是 931 GiB。

cards.en: Motherboards from Taiwan
cards.body_en: ASUS, one of the best-known makers of motherboards, was established in 1989. By the company’s own account, the idea began with a conversation among engineers in a coffee shop in Taipei, and within eight months they had built their first two motherboards. ASUS says that the success of those early boards helped make Taiwan known around the world as a place for high-quality computer products.
cards.body_zh: 華碩（ASUS）是最有名的主機板廠商之一，成立於 1989 年。照華碩自己的說法，這家公司的構想來自幾位工程師在台北一家咖啡店裡的一次談話，八個月內他們就做出了最早的兩款主機板。華碩說，這些早期主機板的成功，讓世界開始知道台灣能做出高品質的電腦產品。

myths.myth_en: Memory and storage are the same thing.
myths.myth_zh: 記憶體和儲存空間是同一個東西。
myths.fact_en: They are two different parts. Memory holds what is in use right now and is wiped when the power goes off. Storage keeps your files without power. “My phone is out of memory” usually means it is out of storage.
myths.fact_zh: 它們是兩個不同的零件。記憶體放現在正在用的東西，電一關就清空；儲存裝置不用電也留得住檔案。大家說「手機記憶體滿了」，通常指的其實是儲存空間滿了。

myths.myth_en: The screen is the computer.
myths.myth_zh: 螢幕就是電腦。
myths.fact_en: A screen only shows the picture that is sent to it. The work is done by the parts on the motherboard. In a laptop or an all-in-one computer, those parts are simply behind or under the screen.
myths.fact_zh: 螢幕只是把送來的畫面顯示出來，工作是主機板上那些零件做的。筆記型電腦或一體成型的電腦，只是把那些零件放在螢幕的後面或下面。

myths.myth_en: The big metal block with a fan is the processor.
myths.myth_zh: 那一大塊有風扇的金屬就是處理器。
myths.fact_en: That is the cooler. The processor is the small flat square underneath it.
myths.fact_zh: 那是散熱器。處理器是它底下那一小片扁扁的方形晶片。

myths.myth_en: A laptop works in a completely different way from a desktop computer.
myths.myth_zh: 筆記型電腦和桌上型電腦的運作方式完全不同。
myths.fact_en: It has the same kinds of parts doing the same jobs. They are smaller and closer together, and some are combined: a system on a chip puts the processor, the graphics, and more on one chip.
myths.fact_zh: 它有同樣那幾種零件，做同樣的事，只是比較小、擠得比較近，有的還合在一起：「系統單晶片」把處理器、顯示功能和更多東西做在同一顆晶片上。

tricks.body_en: Everything plugs into the motherboard.
tricks.body_zh: 每個零件都插在主機板上。

tricks.body_en: It carries out instructions, one after another.
tricks.body_zh: 它一條接一條地執行指令。

tricks.title_en: Memory is now, storage is later
tricks.title_zh: 記憶體管現在，儲存管以後
tricks.body_en: Memory forgets when the power goes off. Storage keeps.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體關電就忘；儲存裝置留得住。

tricks.body_en: The power supply feeds every part. The graphics card feeds the screen.
tricks.body_zh: 電源供應器供電給每個零件；顯示卡把畫面送給螢幕。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前
safety_head.zh: 要看真的電腦裡面之前

safety.en: Do not open a computer on your own. Ask a teacher or a parent, and use only a machine you have permission to open.
safety.zh: 不要自己拆電腦。先問老師或家長，而且只能拆有得到同意的那一台。

safety.en: Before anyone opens the case, the computer must be shut down completely and its power cable unplugged from the wall socket.
safety.zh: 任何人打開機殼之前，電腦一定要完全關機，並把電源線從牆上的插座拔掉。

safety.en: Static electricity can permanently damage the parts, even from a spark too small to feel. Touch an unpainted metal surface first, or wear an anti-static wrist strap.
safety.zh: 靜電會讓零件永久損壞，就算是小到你感覺不到的火花也一樣。先摸一下沒有上漆的金屬表面，或戴上防靜電手環。

safety.en: Leave the power supply closed. It is a sealed box that takes wall electricity directly, and it is not meant to be opened.
safety.zh: 不要拆電源供應器。它是一個直接接牆上的電、封起來的盒子，本來就不是要讓人打開的。

materials.en: Six signs: Storage, Memory, Processor, Graphics, Screen, Power
materials.zh: 六張牌子：儲存裝置、記憶體、處理器、顯示卡、螢幕、電源

materials.en: A stack of cards with one simple instruction on each, such as “draw a circle” or “add 3 and 4”
materials.zh: 一疊卡片，每張寫一個簡單的指令，例如「畫一個圓」「把 3 和 4 加起來」

materials.en: A whiteboard for the Screen
materials.zh: 一塊白板，當作螢幕

steps.en: Six students take the signs and stand in order: Storage, Memory, Processor, Graphics, Screen. Power stands to one side. The rest of the class is the motherboard and passes things along.
steps.zh: 六位同學拿牌子，照順序站好：儲存裝置、記憶體、處理器、顯示卡、螢幕；電源站在旁邊。其他同學當主機板，負責傳東西。

steps.en: Power says “On.” Storage holds the whole stack of cards. To open an app, Storage hands a copy of five cards to Memory.
steps.zh: 電源說「開」。儲存裝置拿著整疊卡片。要打開一個 App 時，儲存裝置把其中五張的副本交給記憶體。

steps.en: Processor takes one card at a time from Memory, does exactly what it says, and tells Graphics the result. Graphics draws it on the whiteboard, the Screen.
steps.zh: 處理器一次從記憶體拿一張卡片，一字不差地照著做，把結果告訴顯示卡。顯示卡把它畫在白板（螢幕）上。

steps.en: Power says “Off.” Memory drops all its cards. Storage still has the full stack. Start again and see what was lost.
steps.zh: 電源說「關」。記憶體把手上的卡片全部丟掉，儲存裝置手上那一疊還在。再開一次，看看什麼不見了。

activities.tip_en: The moment Memory drops its cards is the point of the game: anything that was not handed back to Storage is gone. That is why you save your work. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson matches the topic “System platforms”: 資 S-IV-2, whose notes list the CPU, memory, and input and output.
activities.tip_zh: 記憶體把卡片丟掉的那一刻，就是這個遊戲的重點：沒有交回給儲存裝置的東西，就不見了。這就是為什麼作業要記得存檔。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課對應「系統平台」主題：資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（附錄的說明列有 CPU、記憶體、輸入輸出）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A Windows or Mac computer (you do not open the case)
materials.zh: 一台 Windows 或 Mac 電腦（不用打開機殼）

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: On a Mac, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac. On Windows, right-click Start, choose Settings, select System, and pick About.
steps.zh: Mac：打開蘋果選單，選「關於這台 Mac」（About This Mac）。Windows：在「開始」上按右鍵，選「設定」（Settings），再選「系統」（System）裡的 About 那一頁。

steps.en: Find the processor. A Mac shows the chip or processor. Windows lists the processor type under Device specifications. Write its name down.
steps.zh: 找出處理器。Mac 會顯示晶片或處理器；Windows 在「裝置規格」（Device specifications）下面列出處理器的型號。把它的名字寫下來。

steps.en: Find the memory. A Mac shows the amount of memory. Windows shows the amount of RAM installed. How many gigabytes?
steps.zh: 找出記憶體。Mac 會顯示記憶體有多少；Windows 會顯示安裝了多少 RAM。是幾 GB？

steps.en: Find the storage. On Windows, go back to System and pick Storage. On a Mac, open System Settings, click General, then About, and look for Storage. How many gigabytes, and how many are free?
steps.zh: 找出儲存空間。Windows：回到「系統」，選 Storage（儲存空間）。Mac：打開「系統設定」，按「一般」（General），再按 About，找到儲存空間那一行。一共幾 GB？還剩多少？

activities.tip_en: You should now have three facts about your own computer: its processor, its memory, and its storage. Notice that storage is many times larger than memory. Use “How Much Fits?” above to see what your storage could hold. The names of menus differ a little between versions of Windows and macOS.
activities.tip_zh: 現在你手上有自己電腦的三件事：處理器、記憶體、儲存空間。注意儲存空間比記憶體大了好多倍。用上面的「裝得下多少？」看看你的儲存空間能放多少東西。不同版本的 Windows 和 macOS，選單的名稱會略有不同。

links_head.en: Chips, heat, memory, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 晶片、熱、記憶，以及下一課

links.en: How Does a Computer Add?
links.note_en: The adder you built from gates lives inside the processor you just found.
links.note_zh: 你用邏輯閘做出來的加法器，就住在你剛才找到的處理器裡。

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體・第九課
links.en: Why Do Chips Get Hot?
links.note_en: Why does the processor need that big cooler? Follow the heat from the transistors to the fins.
links.note_zh: 處理器為什麼需要那麼大的散熱器？跟著熱從電晶體一路走到鰭片。

links.en: How Does a Computer Remember Things?
links.note_en: What is actually inside a memory chip and a drive? See where each 0 and 1 is kept.
links.note_zh: 記憶體晶片和硬碟裡面到底是什麼？看看每一個 0 和 1 存在哪裡。

links.en: What Does a Processor Do All Day?
links.note_en: Next, zoom in on the small square under the cooler: fetch an instruction, work out what it means, do it, and fetch the next.
links.note_zh: 下一課要放大散熱器底下那一小片：拿一條指令、看懂它、照著做，再拿下一條。

lessons.sources_note_en: Facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); the sizes in “How Much Fits?” are computed and tested
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；「裝得下多少？」裡的數字是自己算的，並有測試

sources.en: The motherboard is the printed circuit board that connects all components of a computer; it is the largest board in the case; thin lines of copper or aluminum, called traces, run across it; the CPU, RAM, and expansion cards go into its slots
sources.zh: 主機板是把電腦所有零件連在一起的印刷電路板，是機殼裡最大的一塊板子；上面有細細的銅或鋁的線路；處理器、記憶體和擴充卡插在它的插槽上
sources.src: Adam Volle, “motherboard,” Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.en: A microprocessor can “interpret and execute program instructions”; the first microprocessor was the Intel 4004, introduced in 1971
sources.zh: 微處理器能看懂並執行程式的指令；第一顆微處理器是 1971 年推出的 Intel 4004
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “microprocessor”

sources.en: The Intel 4004 “became the first general-purpose microprocessor”
sources.zh: Intel 4004「成為第一顆通用微處理器」
sources.src: Intel, “Announcing a New Era of Integrated Electronics” (Intel history)

sources.en: Main memory holds instructions and data when a program is executing; nonvolatile memories, unlike SRAM and DRAM, do not lose their contents when power is turned off; auxiliary memory holds programs and data for future use
sources.zh: 主記憶體放正在執行的程式的指令與資料；非揮發性記憶體和 SRAM、DRAM 不同，斷電後不會失去內容；輔助記憶（儲存裝置）放以後要用的程式與資料
sources.src: David Hemmendinger, “computer memory,” Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.en: “Application data is first loaded into RAM from permanent storage before the CPU processes it”
sources.zh: 應用程式的資料會先從永久的儲存裝置載入 RAM，處理器才去處理它
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “RAM”

lessons.title: What Does a Processor Do All Day?
lessons.blurb_en: Step through a tiny processor in 3D as it fetches an instruction, decodes it, and executes it, again and again. Arrange four instructions to make it add 3 and 4, then predict what each instruction will do.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡一步一步看一顆小處理器怎麼拿指令、看懂、照做，然後一再重複。自己排四條指令讓它算出 3＋4，再猜猜每一條指令會做什麼。
lessons.big_idea_en: A processor does the same three small steps over and over: fetch an instruction from memory, decode it, and execute it. Each step is tiny. A processor is powerful only because it repeats this loop billions of times a second.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 處理器一直重複同樣三個小步驟：從記憶體拿一條指令、看懂它、照著做。每一步都很小。處理器厲害的地方，只在於它每秒能把這個迴圈重複幾十億次。

lab.title_zh: 只有五種指令的處理器
lab.how_en: On the left is memory: eight numbered cells holding a program and some numbers. On the right is the inside of a processor: a counter that keeps its place, a box for the instruction it is looking at, a box called A for the number it is holding, and an adder. Press Step to do one small step, and read what happened. Press Run to let it go by itself.
lab.how_zh: 左邊是記憶體：八個有編號的格子，放著一個程式和幾個數。右邊是處理器的裡面：一個記住「做到哪裡」的計數器、一個放「正在看的指令」的格子、一個叫 A 的格子（放它手上的那個數），還有一個加法器。按「下一步」走一個小步驟，讀讀右邊寫了什麼；按「執行」讓它自己一直跑。

legend.en: Blue cell: holds an instruction
legend.zh: 藍色的格子：放的是指令

legend.en: Dark cell: holds a number
legend.zh: 深色的格子：放的是數

legend.en: Green board: inside the processor (counter, instruction, A, adder)
legend.zh: 綠色的板子：處理器的裡面（計數器、指令、A、加法器）

legend.en: Teal ball: something being copied from one place to another
legend.zh: 青色小球：正在從一個地方抄到另一個地方的東西

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. This processor and its five instructions are our own invention; no real processor uses this exact set. A real processor has many more instructions and much more memory, and every instruction is stored as a pattern of bits, not as a word like LOAD. The model is slowed down enormously so that you can read each step. What is real is the loop itself: fetch, decode, execute, and move on to the next instruction.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。這顆處理器和它的五種指令是我們自己設計的，沒有哪一顆真的處理器用的是這一套。真的處理器指令多得多、記憶體也大得多，而且每條指令是存成一串位元，不是像 LOAD 這樣的字。模型被放慢了非常非常多倍，好讓你讀得到每一步。真實的是這個迴圈本身：拿、看懂、照做，再換下一條。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The simulator is tested in tools/computers/test/cpu.test.mjs, and its ADD uses the adder from Lesson 4.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫。模擬器有自動測試（tools/computers/test/cpu.test.mjs），其中的 ADD 用的就是第四課的加法器。

paras: In Lesson 5 you found the processor, a small square hiding under a big cooler, and you learned that it carries out the instructions of programs. But what does that actually look like? The answer is surprisingly plain. A processor does the same three small steps, over and over, for as long as the power is on. It fetches an instruction, decodes it, and executes it.

A program is a list of instructions kept in memory. The processor has a small counter that holds the place of the next instruction. To fetch, the processor looks at the counter and copies the instruction at that place out of memory. In the model, the counter starts at 0, so the first instruction comes from cell 0.

Next the processor decodes the instruction, which means working out what it is asking for. Our model understands only five instructions. LOAD copies a number from memory into the processor. ADD adds a number from memory to it, using an adder like the one in Lesson 4. STORE copies the result back into memory. Then the processor executes the instruction: it does that one small thing and nothing more.

After that, the counter goes up by one, and the three steps begin again with the next instruction. Adding 3 and 4 takes four instructions. The fourth kind of instruction, JUMP, is different. It changes the counter itself, so the processor goes back and repeats instructions it has already done. That is how a program only a few lines long can keep a processor busy all day. The fifth, STOP, ends the program.

Each step is tiny, so the power of a processor comes from speed. A clock inside it sets the pace. Clock speed is measured in gigahertz, which means billions of cycles per second: a 3.2-gigahertz processor goes through 3.2 billion cycles every second. A cycle is not exactly one instruction. Some instructions take several cycles, and sometimes several instructions finish in one. Many processors also contain more than one core, so the work can be shared among them.

Keeping the program in the same memory as the numbers was one of the great ideas in computing. In 1945 the mathematician John von Neumann described a stored-program computer in a widely read report. On June 21, 1948, at the University of Manchester in England, a machine nicknamed the Baby ran the first program ever stored in the memory of an electronic computer. It was seventeen instructions long. With a stored program, the same processor, doing the same three steps, can become a calculator, a game, or a music player. You only have to load a different program.
paras_zh: 在第五課，你找到了處理器，一片躲在大散熱器底下的小方塊，也知道它負責執行程式的指令。可是「執行指令」到底是什麼樣子？答案出乎意料地平淡。只要有電，處理器就一直重複同樣三個小步驟：拿一條指令、看懂它、照著做。
程式是一串放在記憶體裡的指令。處理器有一個小小的計數器，記著下一條指令在哪裡。要「拿」指令的時候，處理器看一下計數器，把那個位置的指令從記憶體抄出來。在模型裡，計數器從 0 開始，所以第一條指令來自第 0 格。
接著處理器要「看懂」這條指令，也就是弄清楚它在要求什麼。我們的模型只懂五種指令。LOAD 把記憶體裡的一個數抄進處理器；ADD 把記憶體裡的一個數加上去，用的是像第四課那樣的加法器；STORE 把結果抄回記憶體。然後處理器「照著做」：就做那一件小事，不多做別的。
做完之後，計數器加一，三個步驟又從下一條指令重新開始。把 3 和 4 加起來要四條指令。第四種指令 JUMP 不一樣：它改的是計數器本身，所以處理器會回頭，把做過的指令再做一次。就是因為這樣，一個只有幾行的程式，可以讓處理器忙上一整天。第五種指令 STOP 讓程式結束。
每一步都很小，所以處理器的本事來自「快」。它裡面有一個時脈在打拍子。時脈的快慢用 GHz（吉赫）來表示，意思是每秒幾十億個週期：一顆 3.2 GHz 的處理器，每秒走過 32 億個週期。一個週期不等於剛好一條指令：有的指令要好幾個週期，有時候一個週期可以做完好幾條。很多處理器裡面還不只一個核心，工作可以分給它們一起做。

把程式和數放在同一個記憶體裡，是電腦史上很了不起的一個想法。1945 年，數學家約翰・馮紐曼（John von Neumann）在一份流傳很廣的報告裡，描述了這種「儲存程式」的電腦。1948 年 6 月 21 日，在英國的曼徹斯特大學，一台綽號叫「Baby」的機器，跑出了史上第一個存在電子電腦記憶體裡的程式，一共十七條指令。有了儲存的程式，同一顆處理器、做同樣三個步驟，就可以變成計算機、遊戲機或音樂播放器，只要換一個程式載進去就行了。
questions: What three steps does a processor repeat?
What does the counter do, and how does a JUMP instruction change it?
A 3.2-gigahertz processor goes through 3.2 billion cycles every second. Does that mean it carries out exactly 3.2 billion instructions every second? Why or why not?
answers: It fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it (works out what it asks for), and executes it (does it). Then it moves on to the next instruction.

The counter holds the place of the next instruction, and it normally goes up by one after each instruction. A JUMP sets the counter to a different place, so the processor can go back and repeat instructions.
No. A cycle is not exactly one instruction. Some instructions take several cycles, and sometimes several instructions finish in a single cycle.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Watch the first small step in slow motion. Which cell does the instruction come from, and why that one?
parts.text_zh: 用慢動作看第一個小步驟。指令是從哪一格來的？為什麼是那一格？

parts.text_en: A already holds 3. Watch the number 4 travel from memory to the adder, and the answer come back to A.
parts.text_zh: A 已經是 3 了。看 4 這個數從記憶體跑到加法器，答案再回到 A。

parts.text_en: This program has no STOP. Watch cell 6 while the counter keeps jumping back to 0.
parts.text_zh: 這個程式沒有 STOP。看著第 6 格，同時注意計數器一直跳回 0。

parts.meta_zh: 四條指令，十二個小步驟
parts.text_en: Run 3 + 4 from start to finish at full speed. Where does the answer end up?
parts.text_zh: 用最快的速度把 3＋4 從頭跑到尾。答案最後放在哪裡？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then step through by hand and say each step out loud before you press: fetch, decode, or execute?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己一步一步按，每按之前先說出這一步是什麼：拿、看懂，還是照做？

prog.lead_en: Cells 5 and 6 hold 3 and 4. Choose four instructions, in order, so that cell 7 ends up holding their sum. Press Run, and the list shows what each instruction did to A. If something goes wrong, the message tells you what.
prog.lead_zh: 第 5 格和第 6 格放著 3 和 4。照順序選四條指令，讓第 7 格最後放的是它們的和。按「執行」，右邊會列出每一條指令讓 A 變成什麼；出了問題，訊息會告訴你是哪裡不對。

tips.en: A number has to be in A before you can add to it. Which instruction puts it there?
tips.zh: 要先有一個數在 A 裡面，才能往上加。哪一條指令會把數放進去？

tips.en: Try leaving out STOP, or ending with JUMP 0, and read what happens.
tips.zh: 試試看不放 STOP，或者最後放 JUMP 0，讀讀會發生什麼事。

tips.en: The processor does exactly what the list says, in order, even when the list is wrong.
tips.zh: 處理器會照清單一條一條做，一字不差，就算清單是錯的也一樣。

pred.lead_en: Eight questions. You are told what is in A, in the counter, and in one memory cell, and you are given one instruction. Choose what the answer will be after the processor executes it. The game counts how many you get right on the first try.
pred.lead_zh: 一共八題。題目告訴你 A、計數器和某一格記憶體現在是多少，再給你一條指令。選出處理器執行完之後的結果。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾題。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Loop · 這個迴圈的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A report, a Baby, a clock, and a cell that could be anything
culture_cards.title_zh: 一份報告、一個 Baby、一個時脈、一格什麼都可能是的記憶體
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about programs and the processors that run them.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於程式、以及執行程式的處理器的四個小故事。

cards.en: The program moves into memory
cards.body_en: The earliest electronic computers were set up for each new job by hand, with plugboards, punched cards, and paper tape. In 1945 the mathematician John von Neumann wrote the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC. This widely circulated paper outlined a stored-program computer, in which programming information is kept electronically, just like the data. The model on this page works that way: instructions and numbers sit side by side in the same eight cells.
cards.body_zh: 最早的電子電腦，每換一件工作就要動手重新設定：插接線板、打孔卡、紙帶。1945 年，數學家馮紐曼寫了〈EDVAC 報告初稿〉。這份流傳很廣的文件，勾勒出「儲存程式電腦」的架構：程式和資料一樣，用電子的方式存起來。這一頁的模型就是這樣運作的：指令和數並排放在同樣那八個格子裡。

cards.en: Seventeen instructions
cards.body_en: At the University of Manchester, Frederic Williams, Tom Kilburn, and Geoff Toothill built a small machine to test a new kind of memory. Its official name was the Small-Scale Experimental Machine, but it is better known as the Manchester Baby. Its first program was written by Kilburn and was seventeen instructions long. It ran on June 21, 1948. The Computer History Museum calls it the first program in history to run on a digital, electronic, stored-program computer.
cards.body_zh: 在曼徹斯特大學，威廉斯（Frederic Williams）、基爾本（Tom Kilburn）和圖希爾（Geoff Toothill）做了一台小機器，用來測試一種新的記憶體。它的正式名稱是「小型實驗機」，但大家比較常叫它「曼徹斯特 Baby」。它的第一個程式是基爾本寫的，一共十七條指令，在 1948 年 6 月 21 日執行。電腦歷史博物館說，這是史上第一個在數位、電子、儲存程式的電腦上執行的程式。

cards.en: What the clock number means
cards.zh: 時脈那個數字是什麼意思
cards.body_en: The speed printed on a processor’s box is its clock speed. One gigahertz is one billion cycles per second, so 3.2 GHz is 3.2 billion cycles every second. During each cycle, billions of transistors inside the processor open and close. Older processors were measured in megahertz, or millions of cycles per second. Intel points out that clock speed is only one thing to look at: the number of cores matters, too.
cards.body_zh: 處理器包裝盒上印的那個速度，是它的時脈頻率。1 GHz 是每秒十億個週期，所以 3.2 GHz 就是每秒 32 億個週期。每一個週期裡，處理器裡面有幾十億個電晶體在開和關。比較早的處理器是用 MHz 來算的，也就是每秒幾百萬個週期。英特爾提醒，時脈只是該看的其中一項，核心的數目也很重要。

cards.en: Is this cell an instruction or a number?
cards.body_en: In Lesson 2 you learned that bits do not say what they are. The same is true here. The processor never checks whether a cell is “meant” to be an instruction. Whatever the counter points to, it tries to obey. In the model, if the counter reaches a cell with a number or nothing in it, the processor has to stop. Try it in the activity above by leaving out STOP. Keeping the counter away from the data is the programmer’s job.
cards.body_zh: 第二課說過，位元自己不會說它是什麼。這裡也是一樣。處理器從來不會檢查某一格「本來是不是」指令：計數器指到哪一格，它就想照那一格做。在模型裡，如果計數器走到一格放的是數、或什麼都沒有，處理器就只好停下來。在上面的活動裡故意不放 STOP，就能看到這件事。不讓計數器闖進資料裡，是寫程式的人的責任。

myths.myth_en: A processor does big, complicated things in one go.
myths.myth_zh: 處理器一次就能做很大、很複雜的事。
myths.fact_en: Each instruction is tiny: copy one number, add two numbers, change the counter. Big jobs are long lists of tiny steps, done very fast.
myths.fact_zh: 每條指令都很小：抄一個數、把兩個數加起來、改一下計數器。大事情是一長串的小步驟，只是做得非常快。

myths.myth_en: A 3 GHz processor carries out exactly 3 billion instructions a second.
myths.myth_zh: 3 GHz 的處理器每秒剛好執行 30 億條指令。
myths.fact_en: Gigahertz counts clock cycles, not instructions. Some instructions take several cycles, and sometimes several instructions finish in one cycle.
myths.fact_zh: GHz 數的是時脈的週期，不是指令。有的指令要好幾個週期，有時候一個週期可以做完好幾條。

myths.myth_en: The processor understands the program it is running.
myths.myth_zh: 處理器懂它正在跑的程式是在做什麼。
myths.fact_en: It has no idea whether it is running a game or doing your homework. It only fetches the next instruction and does what that one instruction says.
myths.fact_zh: 它完全不知道自己是在跑遊戲還是在算你的作業。它只是拿下一條指令，照那一條說的做。

myths.myth_en: A program always runs from the first line to the last, once.
myths.myth_zh: 程式一定是從第一行跑到最後一行，跑一次就結束。
myths.fact_en: A jump can send the processor back to repeat instructions, thousands or millions of times. Most of what a processor does all day is repeating.
myths.fact_zh: 跳躍指令可以把處理器送回去，把同樣幾條指令重複幾千次、幾百萬次。處理器整天在做的，大部分就是重複。

tricks.body_en: Three small steps, over and over.
tricks.body_zh: 三個小步驟，一再重複。

tricks.body_en: It goes up by one after each instruction.
tricks.body_zh: 每做完一條指令，它就加一。

tricks.body_en: Change the counter, and the processor repeats.
tricks.body_zh: 把計數器改掉，處理器就重來一遍。

tricks.body_en: 1 GHz is one billion clock cycles a second.
tricks.body_zh: 1 GHz 是每秒十億個時脈週期。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: In Activity Monitor or Task Manager, only look. Do not quit or end anything in the list: some of those programs keep the computer running.
safety.zh: 在「活動監視器」或「工作管理員」裡只要看就好，不要結束清單裡的任何東西：有些程式是讓電腦正常運作用的。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission, and do not change its settings.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意，也不要更改設定。

safety.en: The Count forever program never stops by itself. In the model that is harmless: press Pause or Reset.
safety.zh: 「一直加一」那個程式不會自己停。在模型裡這沒有關係：按「暫停」或「重來」就好。

safety.en: Look away from the screen every 20 minutes and let your eyes rest.
safety.zh: 每看 20 分鐘螢幕，就把視線移開，讓眼睛休息一下。

materials.en: Eight sheets of paper numbered 0 to 7, taped in a row on the board: the memory
materials.zh: 八張紙，編號 0 到 7，在黑板上貼成一排：這是記憶體

materials.en: Cards for the program: LOAD 5, ADD 6, STORE 7, STOP, and the numbers 3, 4, and 0
materials.zh: 程式用的卡片：LOAD 5、ADD 6、STORE 7、STOP，以及數字 3、4、0

materials.en: Two small whiteboards: one for the counter, one for A
materials.zh: 兩塊小白板：一塊當計數器，一塊當 A

steps.en: Put the four instruction cards on sheets 0 to 3, and the numbers 3, 4, and 0 on sheets 5, 6, and 7. One student holds the counter, which starts at 0. Another holds A.
steps.zh: 把四張指令卡放在第 0 到 3 張紙上，把 3、4、0 放在第 5、6、7 張紙上。一位同學拿計數器（從 0 開始），另一位拿 A。

steps.en: A third student is the processor. Fetch: read the counter, walk to that sheet, and read the card aloud.
steps.zh: 第三位同學當處理器。拿：看一下計數器，走到那一張紙前面，把卡片大聲唸出來。

steps.en: Decode: say in your own words what the card asks for. Execute: do exactly that, and nothing else. Then the counter student adds one.
steps.zh: 看懂：用自己的話說出這張卡片要做什麼。照做：就做那一件事，不多做別的。然後拿計數器的同學把數字加一。

steps.en: Repeat until you reach STOP. Then swap ADD 6 and LOAD 5 and run it again. What ends up on sheet 7 this time, and why?
steps.zh: 一直重複到 STOP 為止。接著把 ADD 6 和 LOAD 5 的位置對調，再跑一次。這次第 7 張紙上是什麼？為什麼？

activities.tip_en: With the two cards swapped, sheet 7 ends up with 3, not 7. The processor student did nothing wrong. The order of the instructions was wrong, and the processor obeyed it anyway. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson matches the topic “System platforms”: 資 S-IV-2, whose notes list the CPU and memory.
activities.tip_zh: 兩張卡片對調之後，第 7 張紙上會是 3，不是 7。當處理器的同學並沒有做錯：錯的是指令的順序，而處理器照樣照著做了。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課對應「系統平台」主題：資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（附錄的說明列有 CPU、記憶體）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A Windows or Mac computer
materials.zh: 一台 Windows 或 Mac 電腦

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: On a Mac, open the Activity Monitor app and click CPU. On Windows, open Task Manager and select the Performance tab.
steps.zh: Mac：打開「活動監視器」（Activity Monitor），按 CPU。Windows：打開「工作管理員」（Task Manager），選 Performance（效能）分頁。

steps.en: With nothing much running, read how busy the processor is. On a Mac, look at the Idle percentage at the bottom of the window. Write the number down.
steps.zh: 在沒開什麼程式的時候，看看處理器有多忙。Mac 上看視窗最下面的「閒置」（Idle）百分比。把數字寫下來。

steps.en: Now open several apps or a video, and watch the numbers change. Close them and watch again.
steps.zh: 接著打開幾個 App 或一段影片，看數字怎麼變。把它們關掉，再看一次。

steps.en: Find how many cores your processor has. On Windows, the Performance tab lists the cores. On a Mac, choose Window > CPU History to see a graph of recent processor activity.
steps.zh: 找出你的處理器有幾個核心。Windows 的 Performance 分頁會列出核心數；Mac 選「視窗」＞「CPU 記錄」（CPU History），可以看到處理器最近活動的圖。

activities.tip_en: Apple’s guide says that most of the time, the processor uses only a small percentage of its processing power. So what does a processor do all day? Much of the time it is waiting for something to do. When you ask for something that needs heavy calculation, it gets busy. The names of menus differ a little between versions of Windows and macOS.
activities.tip_zh: Apple 的說明寫道，大部分的時候，處理器只用到它運算能力的一小部分。所以處理器整天在忙什麼？很多時候，它其實在等事情做；等你要它做需要大量計算的事，它才忙起來。不同版本的 Windows 和 macOS，選單的名稱會略有不同。

links_head.en: The adder, many cores, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 加法器、很多核心，以及下一課

links.en: What Is Inside a Computer?
links.note_en: Where the processor sits, and the parts it works with: memory, storage, graphics, and power.
links.note_zh: 處理器在哪裡，以及和它一起工作的零件：記憶體、儲存裝置、顯示卡和電源。

links.en: How Does a Computer Add?
links.note_en: The adder inside this lesson’s processor is the one you built from gates.
links.note_zh: 這一課的處理器裡面那個加法器，就是你用邏輯閘做出來的那一個。

links.k_zh: 晶片與半導體・第十課
links.en: How Is an AI Chip Different from a CPU?
links.zh: AI 晶片和一般 CPU 有什麼不同？
links.note_en: One core does one step at a time. See what changes when a chip has thousands of small units working side by side.
links.note_zh: 一個核心一次只做一步。看看當一顆晶片有幾千個小單元同時工作時，會有什麼不同。

links.en: Why Does a Computer Need Two Kinds of Memory?
links.zh: 電腦為什麼要有兩種記憶？
links.note_en: The processor fetches from memory billions of times a second. Next: why that memory has to be fast, and why it cannot also be the place where your files are kept.
links.note_zh: 處理器每秒要去記憶體拿東西幾十億次。下一課要看：為什麼記憶體一定要快，又為什麼它不能同時是存放檔案的地方。

lessons.sources_note_en: Names, dates, and facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); the model’s processor is our own design, and its simulator is tested
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的人名、年代與事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；模型裡的處理器是我們自己設計的，模擬器有測試

sources.en: The control unit of a CPU selects and retrieves instructions from the main memory in proper sequence and interprets them; the arithmetic-logic unit does the arithmetic and logic
sources.zh: CPU 的控制單元依序從主記憶體選出並取回指令、加以解讀；算術邏輯單元負責算術與邏輯運算
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “central processing unit”

sources.en: A microprocessor can “interpret and execute program instructions”
sources.zh: 微處理器能解讀並執行程式的指令
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “microprocessor”

sources.en: Clock speed is expressed in gigahertz, billions of cycles per second; a 3.2 GHz CPU executes 3.2 billion cycles per second; during each cycle, billions of transistors open and close; sometimes multiple instructions are completed in one cycle, and one instruction may take multiple cycles; older CPUs were measured in megahertz; the number of cores matters, too
sources.zh: 時脈頻率用 GHz 表示，即每秒幾十億個週期；3.2 GHz 的 CPU 每秒 32 億個週期；每個週期有幾十億個電晶體開關；有時一個週期完成多條指令，有時一條指令要多個週期；較早的 CPU 用 MHz；核心數也很重要
sources.src: Intel, “CPU Speed: What Is CPU Clock Speed?”

sources.en: In 1945 John von Neumann wrote the First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC, a widely circulated paper outlining a stored-program computer, which removed the need for plugboards, punched cards, and paper
sources.zh: 1945 年馮紐曼寫了〈EDVAC 報告初稿〉，這份流傳很廣的文件勾勒出儲存程式電腦的架構，不必再用接線板、打孔卡與紙帶來設定程式
sources.src: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History, 1945

sources.en: The Manchester “Baby” (Small-Scale Experimental Machine), built by Williams, Kilburn, and Toothill to test a new memory; its first program, seventeen instructions written by Kilburn, ran on June 21, 1948: the first program to run on a digital, electronic, stored-program computer
sources.zh: 曼徹斯特 Baby（小型實驗機）由威廉斯、基爾本、圖希爾建造，用來測試新的記憶體；第一個程式由基爾本撰寫，共十七條指令，1948 年 6 月 21 日執行，是第一個在數位、電子、儲存程式電腦上執行的程式
sources.src: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History, 1948

sources.en: “Most of the time, the processor on your Mac uses only a small percentage of its processing power”; in Activity Monitor, click CPU, and choose Window > CPU History
sources.zh: 「大部分的時候，Mac 的處理器只用到它運算能力的一小部分」；在活動監視器按 CPU，並選「視窗」＞「CPU 記錄」
sources.src: Apple Support, “View CPU activity in Activity Monitor on Mac”

sources.en: “Open Task Manager, then select the Performance tab to see how many cores and logical processors” a Windows device has
sources.zh: 打開工作管理員，選 Performance 分頁，就能看到處理器有幾個核心與邏輯處理器
sources.src: Microsoft Support, “Find out how many cores a processor on a Windows device has”

sources.zh: 台灣用語：program counter 程式計數器、register 暫存器、instruction 指令、clock rate 時脈頻率（高中以下資訊名詞）、CPU 中央處理單元
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《樂詞網》

sources.zh: 資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（第 10 頁）；附錄三的說明：「系統軟硬體架構與運作原理：作業系統、CPU、記憶體、輸入輸出」（第 43 頁）
sources.src: 教育部《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校 科技領域》（2018）
