sources.en: The model’s processor: eight cells, five instructions, three small steps for each instruction; the 3 + 4 program takes four instructions and twelve small steps; the counting program never stops; 3.2 × 1,000,000,000 = 3,200,000,000
sources.zh: 模型裡的處理器：八格記憶體、五種指令、每條指令三個小步驟；3＋4 的程式是四條指令、十二個小步驟；一直加一的程式永遠不會停；3.2 × 1,000,000,000＝3,200,000,000
sources.src: Our own design, checked by tools/computers/test/cpu.test.mjs

lessons.title: Why Does a Computer Need Two Kinds of Memory?
lessons.title_zh: 電腦為什麼要有兩種記憶？
lessons.blurb_en: A desk and a bookcase in 3D: open things, fill the desk, change something without saving, and switch off the power to see what survives. Then sort eight things into memory or storage, and watch what happens when memory fills up.
lessons.blurb_zh: 3D 裡的一張書桌和一座書櫃：把東西打開、把桌子放滿、改了不存檔，再把電關掉，看看什麼留得下來。接著把八樣東西分到記憶體或儲存裝置，再看記憶體滿了會怎樣。
lessons.big_idea_en: No single kind of memory is fast, large, cheap, and lasting all at once. So a computer uses two that work together. Memory is fast but small, and it forgets when the power goes off. Storage is slower but large, and it keeps things without power.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 沒有哪一種記憶能同時又快、又大、又便宜、又留得住。所以電腦用兩種，搭配著用。記憶體很快，可是小，而且一斷電就忘光；儲存裝置比較慢，可是大，而且沒有電也留得住。

lab.how_en: The bookcase is storage: it holds everything, and it keeps it when the power is off. The desk is memory: there is room for only four things, but whatever is on it is right at hand. Tap a book to open it and watch a copy being carried to the desk. Tap something on the desk to use it at once. Then change something, save it or not, and switch off the power.
lab.how_zh: 書櫃是儲存裝置：什麼都放在這裡，關了電也都還在。書桌是記憶體：只放得下四樣東西，可是放在上面的伸手就拿得到。點一本書把它打開，看一份副本被搬到桌上；點桌上的東西，馬上就能用。接著改一改某樣東西，存檔或不存檔，然後把電關掉。

legend.en: Books in the bookcase: programs and files in storage
legend.zh: 書櫃裡的書：放在儲存裝置裡的程式和檔案

legend.en: The desk: memory, with room for four things
legend.zh: 書桌：記憶體，只放得下四樣東西

legend.en: The lamp: on means the power is on
legend.zh: 檯燈：亮著表示有電

legend.en: Teal ball: a saved copy going back to the bookcase
legend.zh: 青色小球：存檔時抄回書櫃的那一份

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Real memory is a set of chips, not a desk, and it holds billions of bytes, not four things. The walk to the bookcase stands for the extra time storage takes; the real difference in speed is not shown to scale. Opening a program copies it into memory, and the original stays in storage, just as the book stays on the shelf here. When real memory fills up, the computer does something like what you see: it moves what is not being used to storage and brings it back when needed.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。真的記憶體是一組晶片，不是一張桌子；它放的是幾十億個位元組，不是四樣東西。走到書櫃的那一趟，代表儲存裝置多花的時間，但真正的速度差距並沒有照比例畫。打開程式是把它抄一份到記憶體，原來那一份還留在儲存裝置，就像這裡書還留在架上一樣。真的記憶體滿了的時候，電腦做的事也和你看到的類似：把暫時沒在用的東西移到儲存裝置，需要時再搬回來。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The rules of the desk are tested in tools/computers/test/memory.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；書桌的規則有自動測試（tools/computers/test/memory.test.mjs）。

paras: In Lesson 5 you met two parts that both keep things: memory and storage. That seems wasteful. Why not build one kind of memory that is fast, holds everything, and never forgets? Engineers would love to. The trouble is that no single kind of memory can do all of that. The fast kinds are small and expensive. The large, cheap kinds are slow. So a computer uses two, and lets each do what it is good at.

Think of a desk and a bookcase. The bookcase holds hundreds of books, but to use one you have to get up and fetch it. The desk holds only a few things, but they are right in front of you. Storage is the bookcase. Memory is the desk. In Lesson 6 you saw that the processor fetches from memory again and again without stopping, so memory has to be the fast one.

When you open a program, the computer copies it from storage into memory. The first time is the slow part, like walking to the bookcase. After that, the processor works with the copy in memory, which is quick. The original stays in storage. When you change a file, you are changing only the copy in memory. Saving means copying the new version back to storage.

Memory has one more weakness: it needs power to hold on to anything. Switch the computer off, and everything in memory is gone. Storage does not lose its contents when the power is turned off. That is why work you have not saved can disappear, and why a computer needs a little time to start up: it has to copy what it needs from storage into memory all over again.

What if you open more than memory can hold? The computer does not simply give up. It takes something you are not using at the moment and moves it out of memory onto storage, to make room. When you go back to it, the computer has to move it in again. Everything still works, but storage is slower, so the computer feels slow. That is the usual reason a computer with too many things open drags.

So the two kinds of memory are a team. Storage is large and lasting. Memory is fast and close to the processor. A typical computer has many times more storage than memory, because storage is the cheaper of the two. In fact a computer has more than two levels: from tiny, very fast memory inside the processor itself, to memory, to storage, each one larger and slower than the one before it.
paras_zh: 在第五課，你認識了兩個都是用來「放東西」的零件：記憶體和儲存裝置。這看起來很浪費。為什麼不做一種又快、什麼都放得下、又永遠不會忘的記憶就好？工程師也很想。問題是，沒有哪一種記憶做得到全部：快的那幾種又小又貴，又大又便宜的那幾種很慢。所以電腦用兩種，讓它們各做自己擅長的事。
想像一張書桌和一座書櫃。書櫃放得下幾百本書，可是要用哪一本，都得站起來去拿。書桌只放得下幾樣東西，可是它們就在你面前。儲存裝置是書櫃，記憶體是書桌。第六課說過，處理器一刻不停地從記憶體拿東西，所以記憶體一定得是快的那一個。
你打開一個程式的時候，電腦會把它從儲存裝置抄一份到記憶體。第一次是慢的那一段，就像走到書櫃去拿。之後處理器用的是記憶體裡那一份，很快。原來那一份還留在儲存裝置。你修改一個檔案的時候，改的只是記憶體裡的那一份；「存檔」就是把新的版本抄回儲存裝置。
記憶體還有一個弱點：它要有電才留得住東西。電腦一關，記憶體裡的東西就全部不見了。儲存裝置在斷電之後不會失去內容。這就是為什麼沒存檔的東西會消失，也是為什麼電腦開機要花一點時間：它得把需要的東西重新從儲存裝置抄進記憶體。
如果你打開的東西比記憶體放得下的還多呢？電腦不會就這樣放棄。它會把你這時候沒在用的某樣東西，從記憶體移到儲存裝置，把位置空出來。等你回頭要用它，電腦又得把它搬回來。東西都還能用，可是儲存裝置比較慢，所以電腦用起來就慢。開太多東西的電腦會拖拖拉拉，通常就是這個原因。
所以這兩種記憶是一個團隊。儲存裝置又大又留得住；記憶體又快，又離處理器近。一般的電腦，儲存空間是記憶體的好多倍，因為儲存裝置是比較便宜的那一種。其實電腦不只兩層：從處理器裡面非常小、非常快的記憶，到記憶體，再到儲存裝置，每一層都比前一層更大、也更慢。
questions: Why does a computer not use just one kind of memory?
What happens to a file when you open it, change it, and save it?
Why does a computer get slow when too many things are open?
answers: Because no single kind is fast, large, cheap, and lasting all at once. The fast kinds are small and expensive, and the large, cheap kinds are slow. Using two lets each do what it is good at.
Opening it copies it from storage into memory. Changing it changes only the copy in memory. Saving it copies the new version back to storage, where it stays even when the power is off.
Memory fills up, so the computer moves things you are not using out to storage and has to move them back in when you return to them. Storage is slower than memory, so everything takes longer.

vocab.ex: Memory is only a temporary home for your work.
vocab.exzh: 記憶體只是你的工作暫時待的地方。

vocab.ex: Save the file to keep a permanent copy.
vocab.exzh: 把檔案存起來，才留得下一份長期的副本。

vocab.ex: This drive has a capacity of 512 gigabytes.
vocab.exzh: 這顆硬碟的容量是 512 GB。

vocab.ex: Please copy these notes into your notebook.
vocab.exzh: 請把這些筆記抄到你的筆記本上。

vocab.ex: Remember to save your essay before you close it.
vocab.exzh: 關掉作文之前，記得先存檔。

vocab.ex: Fast memory is more expensive than slow storage.
vocab.exzh: 快的記憶體比慢的儲存裝置貴。

vocab.ex: Space on the desk is limited, so put away what you do not need.
vocab.exzh: 桌上的空間有限，所以用不到的東西要收起來。

vocab.ex: The unsaved work disappeared when the power went out.
vocab.exzh: 停電的時候，沒存檔的東西就消失了。

quiz.q: In the desk-and-bookcase picture, what is the desk?
Why can a computer not use one kind of memory for everything?
options: Because no single kind is fast, large, cheap, and lasting all at once

quiz.q: What does saving a file do?
options: It deletes the old file from the screen.
It copies the new version from memory back to storage.

quiz.q: What happens to the contents of memory when the power goes off?
options: They are sent to the printer.

quiz.q: According to the reading, why does a computer feel slow with too many things open?
options: It has to keep moving things between memory and the slower storage.

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.meta_en: A slow trip from the bookcase
parts.text_en: Watch the essay travel from the shelf to the desk. Is the book still on the shelf afterward?
parts.text_zh: 看「作文」從架上走到桌上。走完之後，架上那一本還在嗎？

parts.meta_en: On the desk: no trip at all
parts.text_en: The essay is used three more times. Watch the two counters. Which one goes up?
parts.text_zh: 「作文」又被用了三次。看那兩個計數，哪一個在增加？

parts.meta_en: A fifth thing, room for four
parts.meta_zh: 第五樣東西，只有四個位置
parts.text_en: Four things fill the desk. When a fifth is opened, which one has to leave, and how many trips does it take?
parts.text_zh: 四樣東西把桌子放滿。打開第五樣時，哪一樣要離開？一共走了幾趟？

parts.meta_en: The desk is wiped; the bookcase is not
parts.text_en: The essay is changed but not saved, and then the power goes off. What comes back when it is opened again?
parts.text_zh: 改了「作文」卻沒存檔，然後電就關了。再打開的時候，回來的是什麼？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then do it the safe way yourself: open the essay, change it, save it, switch off, and open it again.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著自己用安全的方法做一次：打開作文、改一改、存檔、關機，再打開。

where.lead_en: Eight things. For each one, decide where it is at this moment: in memory, like something on the desk, or in storage, like a book in the bookcase. The game counts how many you get right on the first try.
where.lead_zh: 一共八樣東西。每一樣都想一想它「現在」在哪裡：在記憶體（像桌上的東西），還是在儲存裝置（像書櫃裡的書）。遊戲會記下你第一次就答對幾題。

tasks.en: The changes you just typed in an essay and have not saved yet
tasks.zh: 你剛在作文裡打的、還沒存檔的修改
tasks.why_en: Until you save, the new words exist only in memory.
tasks.why_zh: 存檔之前，新打的字只在記憶體裡。

tasks.en: Photos you took last year
tasks.zh: 你去年拍的照片
tasks.why_en: They have to last with the power off, so they are in storage.
tasks.why_zh: 它們關了電也要留著，所以在儲存裝置裡。

tasks.en: The game you are playing at this very moment
tasks.zh: 你這一刻正在玩的遊戲
tasks.why_en: A running program has been copied into memory.
tasks.why_zh: 正在執行的程式已經被抄進記憶體了。

tasks.en: A movie you downloaded but have not opened
tasks.zh: 下載好了、還沒打開的電影
tasks.why_en: Nothing has copied it into memory yet. It is waiting in storage.
tasks.why_zh: 還沒有人把它抄進記憶體，它在儲存裝置裡等著。

tasks.en: The numbers the processor is adding right now
tasks.zh: 處理器現在正在加的那幾個數
tasks.why_en: The processor works with what is in memory.
tasks.why_zh: 處理器用的是記憶體裡的東西。

tasks.en: An app you installed last week and have never opened
tasks.zh: 上星期裝好、從來沒打開過的 App
tasks.why_en: Installing puts a program into storage. Opening it copies it into memory.
tasks.why_zh: 安裝是把程式放進儲存裝置；打開它，才會抄進記憶體。

tasks.en: A drawing you saved and closed an hour ago
tasks.zh: 一小時前存好檔、已經關掉的那張圖
tasks.why_en: Saving copied it to storage, and it stays there.
tasks.why_zh: 存檔把它抄回儲存裝置，它就留在那裡。

tasks.en: The web page you are looking at now
tasks.zh: 你現在正在看的網頁
tasks.why_en: What is open and in use is in memory.
tasks.why_zh: 打開著、正在用的東西在記憶體裡。

full.lead_en: This computer has 8 GB of memory. Open and close the apps and watch the bar. When the apps want more than 8 GB, the extra does not fit, and the computer has to keep moving things to storage and back.
full.lead_zh: 這台電腦有 8 GB 的記憶體。把 App 打開、關掉，看看用量條。當這些 App 要的超過 8 GB，多出來的放不下，電腦就得一直把東西搬到儲存裝置、再搬回來。
full.note_en: The sizes here are made up for the example. Real apps use different amounts, and the amounts change as you use them. A real computer also has other ways to save memory. To see the real numbers for your own computer, try the second activity below.
full.note_zh: 這裡的大小是為了舉例自己訂的。真的 App 用量各不相同，而且用著用著還會變；真的電腦也有其他節省記憶體的辦法。想看自己電腦真正的數字，試試下面的第二個活動。

tips.en: Closing an app you are not using gives its memory back.
tips.zh: 把沒在用的 App 關掉，它占的記憶體就還回來了。

tips.en: A nearly full bar is not a problem by itself. Trouble starts only when things no longer fit.
tips.zh: 用量條快滿了，本身不是問題；放不下的時候才會出問題。

tips.en: Nothing is lost when memory overflows. The computer is only slower, because storage is slower.
tips.zh: 記憶體不夠時，東西不會不見，只是電腦變慢，因為儲存裝置比較慢。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Two Memories · 兩種記憶的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A staircase of memories, a trick called virtual memory, a colored graph, and a habit
culture_cards.title_zh: 一道記憶的階梯、一招叫虛擬記憶體、一張有顏色的圖、一個習慣
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about memory and storage.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於記憶體和儲存裝置的四個小故事。

cards.en: Not two levels, but a staircase
cards.zh: 不只兩層，而是一道階梯
cards.body_en: This lesson talks about two kinds of memory, but Britannica describes a whole hierarchy. At the top are very small, fast, and expensive registers inside the processor. Next comes small, fast cache memory, then the larger main memory, then very large hard disks, and finally slow, inexpensive backup storage. Each step down is bigger and slower than the one above. The counter and the box called A in Lesson 6 were registers.
cards.body_zh: 這一課講的是兩種記憶，但大英百科描述的是一整個階層。最上面是處理器裡非常小、非常快、也很貴的暫存器；接著是小而快的快取記憶體，再來是比較大的主記憶體，然後是非常大的硬碟，最後是又慢又便宜的備份儲存。每往下一階，都比上面那一階更大、更慢。第六課的計數器和那個叫 A 的格子，就是暫存器。

cards.en: Pretending there is more room
cards.body_en: What you saw when the desk filled up has a name: virtual memory. Britannica explains that it gives each program a portion of main memory and stores the rest of its code and data on a hard disk, automatically copying blocks to and from main memory as needed. The program does not have to know. It works as if it had all the memory it wanted, and the computer does the fetching and carrying.
cards.body_zh: 桌子滿了的時候你看到的那件事，有個名字：虛擬記憶體。大英百科的解釋是：它給每個程式一部分的主記憶體，把程式其餘的程式碼和資料放在硬碟上，需要的時候再自動把一塊一塊的內容在兩邊抄來抄去。程式本身不需要知道這些，它照樣工作，好像想要多少記憶體都有，搬來搬去的事由電腦負責。

cards.en: A graph that shows the squeeze
cards.zh: 一張看得出擠不擠的圖
cards.body_en: A Mac shows this in its Activity Monitor app. The Memory pane displays how much memory the Mac is using and how often it is swapping memory between RAM and the startup disk. A graph called Memory Pressure is green when the computer is using its RAM efficiently, yellow when it might eventually need more, and red when it needs more RAM.
cards.body_zh: Mac 在「活動監視器」這個 App 裡把這件事顯示出來。「記憶體」那一頁會顯示 Mac 用了多少記憶體，以及它多常在 RAM 和開機磁碟之間交換記憶體。有一張叫「記憶體壓力」的圖：電腦有效率地使用 RAM 時是綠色，之後可能需要更多時是黃色，需要更多 RAM 時是紅色。

cards.en: Why “save” exists at all
cards.zh: 為什麼會有「存檔」這回事
cards.body_en: Saving is not a ceremony. It is the moment your work is copied from the fast memory that forgets to the slower storage that remembers. Everything in this lesson explains that one button: you work in memory because it is fast, and you save to storage because it lasts. However an app handles saving, the rule underneath is the same: what is only in memory is gone when the power goes off.
cards.body_zh: 存檔不是一個儀式。它是把你的工作，從「很快但會忘」的記憶體，抄到「比較慢但記得住」的儲存裝置的那一刻。這一課講的所有事情，都在解釋這一個按鈕：在記憶體裡工作，因為它快；存到儲存裝置，因為它留得住。不管 App 怎麼處理存檔，底下的規則都一樣：只在記憶體裡的東西，斷電就沒了。

myths.myth_en: Opening a file moves it out of storage.
myths.myth_zh: 打開檔案，就是把它從儲存裝置搬走。
myths.fact_en: Opening copies it. The original stays in storage, which is why closing a file without saving leaves the old version untouched.
myths.fact_zh: 打開是「抄一份」。原來那一份還在儲存裝置裡，所以不存檔就關掉，舊的版本還是原封不動。

myths.myth_en: More storage makes a computer faster.
myths.myth_zh: 儲存空間越大，電腦就越快。
myths.fact_en: More storage lets you keep more. It is more memory that lets you keep more things open at once without the slow trips to storage.
myths.fact_zh: 儲存空間大，是能「放」更多東西。能同時開更多東西而不用一直慢慢跑去儲存裝置的，是比較多的記憶體。

myths.myth_en: When memory is full, the computer starts losing things.
myths.myth_zh: 記憶體滿了，電腦就開始丟東西。
myths.fact_en: It does not lose them. It moves what is not being used to storage and brings it back when needed. The cost is speed, not your work.
myths.fact_zh: 它不會把東西丟掉，而是把暫時沒在用的移到儲存裝置，需要時再搬回來。代價是速度，不是你的東西。

myths.myth_en: Free memory is good, so a computer should keep its memory as empty as possible.
myths.myth_zh: 記憶體空著比較好，所以應該盡量讓它空著。
myths.fact_en: Apple’s guide says that free or unused memory does not necessarily improve performance. A computer does best by making good use of all the memory it has.
myths.fact_zh: Apple 的說明寫道，有空著沒用的記憶體，效能不見得比較好。電腦把手上所有的記憶體都好好用上，表現才最好。

tricks.body_en: Memory is the desk. Storage is the bookcase.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體是書桌，儲存裝置是書櫃。

tricks.body_en: Memory is wiped without power. Storage is not.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體沒電就清空；儲存裝置不會。

tricks.title_en: Open copies in, save copies back
tricks.title_zh: 打開是抄進來，存檔是抄回去
tricks.body_en: The original never leaves storage.
tricks.body_zh: 原來那一份從來沒有離開儲存裝置。

tricks.title_en: Too much open, lots of trips
tricks.body_en: A full memory means slow trips to storage.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體滿了，就得慢慢地一趟一趟跑儲存裝置。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Do not switch a real computer off at the wall or hold the power button to see what is lost. Shut it down the normal way.
safety.zh: 不要為了看看什麼會不見，就直接拔真電腦的插頭或長按電源鍵。請用正常的方式關機。

safety.en: Save your work before you try anything in the second activity, and save often in general.
safety.zh: 做第二個活動之前，先把手上的東西存檔；平常也要常常存檔。

safety.en: In Activity Monitor or Task Manager, only look. Do not quit or end anything in the list.
safety.zh: 在「活動監視器」或「工作管理員」裡只要看就好，不要結束清單裡的任何東西。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission, and do not change its settings.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意，也不要更改設定。

materials.en: A table at the front of the room: the desk, with four spaces marked in tape
materials.zh: 教室前面的一張桌子當書桌，用膠帶標出四個位置

materials.en: A shelf or box at the back of the room: the bookcase
materials.zh: 教室後面的一個架子或箱子當書櫃

materials.en: Eight folders, each holding one sheet of paper, with two photocopies of each sheet
materials.zh: 八個資料夾，每個裡面放一張紙，每張紙另外影印兩份

materials.en: A pencil and a stopwatch
materials.zh: 一枝鉛筆和一個碼錶

steps.en: The folders stay in the bookcase at all times. One student is the processor and sits at the desk. Another is the runner. A third keeps time.
steps.zh: 資料夾永遠留在書櫃裡。一位同學當處理器，坐在書桌前；一位當跑腿的；一位負責計時。

steps.en: The teacher calls out a folder. If a copy is on the desk, the processor touches it and says “Got it!” If not, the runner walks to the bookcase and brings back a photocopy. Time both.
steps.zh: 老師喊一個資料夾的名字。桌上有它的影本，處理器就摸一下說「拿到了！」；沒有的話，跑腿的走到書櫃拿一份影本回來。兩種情況都計時。

steps.en: When the desk already has four copies and a fifth is called, the runner must first carry one copy back to the bookcase. Which one should go?
steps.zh: 桌上已經有四份影本、老師又喊第五樣的時候，跑腿的得先把一份影本送回書櫃。該送哪一份回去？

steps.en: Write on one of the copies with the pencil. Then the teacher says “Power off!” and sweeps everything off the desk. Look in the bookcase: is your writing there?
steps.zh: 用鉛筆在其中一份影本上寫字。接著老師說「停電！」，把桌上的東西全部掃掉。去書櫃看看：你寫的字在那裡嗎？

activities.tip_en: Compare the times: touching a copy on the desk against a walk across the room. Then play again, and this time carry the written copy back to the bookcase before the power goes off. That walk is saving. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson matches the topic “System platforms”: 資 S-IV-2, whose notes list memory.
activities.tip_zh: 比一比時間：摸一下桌上的影本，和走過整間教室。接著再玩一次，這次在停電之前，把寫了字的那一份送回書櫃。那一趟路就是存檔。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課對應「系統平台」主題：資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（附錄的說明列有記憶體）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A Windows or Mac computer
materials.zh: 一台 Windows 或 Mac 電腦

materials.en: The numbers you wrote down in Lesson 5, or the steps from that lesson
materials.zh: 第五課寫下來的那幾個數字，或照那一課的步驟再查一次

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Find how much memory your computer has and how much storage it has, both in gigabytes. Lesson 5 shows where to look.
steps.zh: 找出你的電腦有多少記憶體、多少儲存空間，單位都是 GB。在哪裡看，第五課有教。

steps.en: Divide the storage by the memory. How many times bigger is the bookcase than the desk?
steps.zh: 把儲存空間除以記憶體。書櫃是書桌的幾倍大？

steps.en: On a Mac, open Activity Monitor and click Memory. On Windows, open Task Manager, select the Performance tab, and look for Memory. How much memory is in use right now?
steps.zh: Mac：打開「活動監視器」，按「記憶體」（Memory）。Windows：打開「工作管理員」，選 Performance（效能）分頁，找到 Memory（記憶體）。現在用了多少記憶體？

steps.en: Open a few more apps, look again, then close them and look once more. On a Mac, watch the color of the Memory Pressure graph.
steps.zh: 多開幾個 App，再看一次；把它們關掉，再看一次。Mac 上可以注意「記憶體壓力」那張圖的顏色。

activities.tip_en: A computer with 16 GB of memory and 512 GB of storage has 32 times as much storage as memory. A computer with 8 GB and 1 TB has 125 times as much. Whatever your numbers are, the bookcase is far bigger than the desk. The names of menus differ a little between versions of Windows and macOS.
activities.tip_zh: 記憶體 16 GB、儲存空間 512 GB 的電腦，儲存空間是記憶體的 32 倍；8 GB 配 1 TB 的電腦是 125 倍。不管你的數字是多少，書櫃都比書桌大得多。不同版本的 Windows 和 macOS，選單的名稱會略有不同。

links_head.en: Inside the chips, the processor that waits, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 晶片的裡面、在等的處理器，以及下一課

links.en: What Does a Processor Do All Day?
links.note_en: The processor fetches from memory at every step. That is why memory has to be the fast one.
links.note_zh: 處理器每一步都要從記憶體拿東西，所以記憶體一定得是快的那一個。

links.en: How Does a Computer Remember Things?
links.note_en: Why does memory forget and storage remember? Look inside the chips: one kind of cell leaks its charge, and the other locks it in.
links.note_zh: 為什麼記憶體會忘、儲存裝置記得住？到晶片裡面看看：一種小格子的電荷會漏掉，另一種把電荷鎖在裡面。

links.en: What Is Inside a Computer?
links.note_en: Find the memory sticks and the solid-state drive in the 3D computer, and check how many gigabytes fit on a drive.
links.note_zh: 在 3D 主機裡找出那兩條記憶體和固態硬碟，再算算一顆硬碟裝得下多少東西。

links.en: What Happens When You Press a Key?
links.zh: 按下一個鍵，發生了什麼？
links.note_en: Now put the whole machine together. Next: follow one letter from the keyboard, through memory and the processor, to the screen.
links.note_zh: 現在把整台機器接起來。下一課要跟著一個字母，從鍵盤出發，經過記憶體和處理器，一路走到螢幕。

lessons.sources_note_en: Facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); the desk model is our own illustration, and its rules are tested
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；書桌模型是我們自己的示意，規則有測試

sources.en: Memory forms a hierarchy, from very small, fast, and expensive registers in the CPU, to cache, to larger DRAM, to very large hard disks, to slow and inexpensive nonvolatile backup storage; virtual memory gives each program a portion of main memory and stores the rest on a hard disk, copying blocks to and from main memory as needed
sources.zh: 記憶體形成一個階層：從 CPU 裡非常小、快而貴的暫存器，到快取、較大的 DRAM、非常大的硬碟，再到慢而便宜的非揮發性備份儲存；虛擬記憶體給每個程式一部分主記憶體，其餘放在硬碟，需要時自動在兩邊複製
sources.src: David Hemmendinger, “computer memory: Memory hierarchy,” Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.en: Main memory holds instructions and data when a program is executing; auxiliary memory holds programs and data for future use; nonvolatile memories, unlike SRAM and DRAM, do not lose their contents when power is turned off
sources.zh: 主記憶體放正在執行的程式的指令與資料；輔助記憶放以後要用的程式與資料；非揮發性記憶體和 SRAM、DRAM 不同，斷電後不會失去內容
sources.src: David Hemmendinger, “computer memory,” Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.en: “Application data is first loaded into RAM from permanent storage before the CPU processes it”
sources.zh: 應用程式的資料會先從永久的儲存裝置載入 RAM，處理器才去處理它
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “RAM”

sources.en: Opening a file transfers its data from storage to RAM for short-term use; storage remembers files even when the device is off
sources.zh: 打開檔案時，資料從儲存裝置傳到 RAM 供短期使用；儲存裝置在關機時也記得檔案
sources.src: Crucial (Micron), “What is an SSD?”

sources.en: The Memory pane shows how much memory a Mac is using and how often it is swapping memory between RAM and the startup disk; free or unused memory does not necessarily improve performance; Memory Pressure is green, yellow, or red
sources.zh: 「記憶體」面板顯示 Mac 用了多少記憶體、多常在 RAM 與開機磁碟之間交換記憶體；有空著沒用的記憶體，效能不見得比較好；「記憶體壓力」有綠、黃、紅三種顏色
sources.src: Apple Support, “Check if your Mac needs more RAM in Activity Monitor”

sources.en: Task Manager’s Performance tab shows how a Windows device’s hardware is being used
sources.zh: 工作管理員的 Performance 分頁顯示 Windows 裝置的硬體使用情形
sources.src: Microsoft Support, “Find out how many cores a processor on a Windows device has”

lessons.title: What Happens When You Press a Key?
lessons.title_zh: 按下一個鍵，發生了什麼？
lessons.blurb_en: Follow one key in 3D, from the keyboard, along the cable, through the processor and memory, to the screen. At every stop it is something different: a switch, a key number, a character number, eight bits, and at last a pattern of pixels. Then guess what it is at each stop, sort input from output, and test the keys on your own keyboard.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在 3D 裡跟著一個鍵走一趟：從鍵盤出發，沿著線，經過處理器和記憶體，走到螢幕。每一站它都是不一樣的東西：一個開關、一個鍵的編號、一個字元的編號、八個位元，最後是一片像素。接著猜猜它在每一站是什麼、分辨輸入和輸出，再測測自己鍵盤上的鍵。
lessons.big_idea_en: A computer takes something in, works on it, and sends something out: input, processing, output. A keyboard does not send a letter. It sends a number that says which key was pressed. The computer turns that into a character number, keeps it in memory as bits, and lights pixels on the screen. It is 0s and 1s the whole way.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 電腦把東西收進來、處理它、再送出去：輸入、處理、輸出。鍵盤送出的不是一個字母，而是一個「哪一個鍵被按了」的編號。電腦把它變成字元的編號，用位元放在記憶體裡，再讓螢幕上的像素亮起來。從頭到尾都是 0 和 1。

lab.how_en: On the left is a keyboard with four keys. In the middle is a circuit board with a processor and eight cells of memory. On the right is a screen with 35 pixels. Choose a key and press it, then follow the glowing dot. The list on the right fills in what the key has become at each stop. Then hold Shift and press the same key again, and see which stops change.
lab.how_zh: 左邊是一個只有四個鍵的鍵盤，中間是一塊電路板，上面有處理器和八格記憶體，右邊是一個 35 個像素的螢幕。選一個鍵按下去，跟著那顆光點走。右邊的清單會一站一站填上：這個鍵在那一站變成了什麼。接著按住 Shift，再按一次同一個鍵，看看哪幾站變了。

legend.en: Keys: each one is a switch
legend.zh: 按鍵：每一個都是開關

legend.en: Glowing dot: where the key press is now
legend.zh: 光點：這一次按鍵現在走到哪裡

legend.en: Processor: glows blue while it looks up the character
legend.zh: 處理器：查字元的時候發藍光

legend.en: Eight memory cells: a lit cell is a 1
legend.zh: 八格記憶體：亮的是 1

legend.en: Screen pixels: 5 across, 7 down
legend.zh: 螢幕的像素：橫 5 格、直 7 格

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The key numbers are the real ones from the USB keyboard standard (the A key is 4, the 1 key is 30, the space bar is 44); other kinds of keyboard connection use other numbers. In a real computer the lookup is done by the operating system, a program that the processor runs, and it uses whatever keyboard layout you have chosen. The model always uses the U.S. layout. A real keyboard also reports when the key comes back up. And a real letter is drawn with far more pixels than 35: the tiny letter shapes here are our own, drawn just for this model.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。鍵的編號是 USB 鍵盤標準裡真正的編號（A 鍵是 4、1 鍵是 30、空白鍵是 44）；其他接法的鍵盤用的是別的編號。真的電腦裡，查表這件事是作業系統做的（作業系統也是處理器在執行的程式），而且用的是你選的鍵盤配置；模型固定用美式配置。真的鍵盤在鍵彈回來的時候也會回報。還有，真的字用的像素遠遠多於 35 個：這裡小小的字形是我們為了這個模型自己畫的。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The steps are tested in tools/computers/test/keypath.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；每一站的規則有自動測試（tools/computers/test/keypath.test.mjs）。

paras: Press the key marked A, and the letter a appears on the screen. It seems to happen at once, and it seems simple. It is not simple. Between your finger and the screen, that key press changes form four times. Let us follow it.

Under each key there is a switch. When you press the key, the switch closes, and the keyboard sends the computer a number. The number does not mean a letter. It means a key: it says which key was pressed. On a USB keyboard, the A key is key number 4. The keyboard sends the same number whether you are holding Shift or not, and it reports again when you let the key go.

Now the computer has to decide what the key means. It looks at three things: the key number, whether Shift is down, and the keyboard layout you have chosen. From these it picks a character. Key 4 with no Shift gives a. Key 4 with Shift gives A. As you saw in Lesson 2, every character has its own number: a is 97, and A is 65.

The number 97 is stored in memory as eight bits: 01100001. The program you are typing in now has a new character to work with, and the processor carries out that program’s instructions, one small step at a time, just as in Lesson 6. If you save your work, the bits are copied to storage, as in Lesson 7.

You still cannot see anything. To show the character, the computer needs a shape for it, and the shapes come from a font. A font is a collection of shapes for characters. The computer uses the font to decide which pixels on the screen to light, and the letter appears. Choose a different font and other pixels light up, but the character in memory is still 97.

This is the pattern of every computer: input, processing, output. An input device, such as a keyboard, a mouse, or a microphone, turns something from the outside world into electrical signals in binary code. The computer works on them. An output device, such as a screen, a printer, or a speaker, turns the signals back into something a person can understand. Switches, bits, codes, a processor, memory: everything in the first eight lessons took part in that one key press.
paras_zh: 按下標著 A 的那個鍵，螢幕上就出現字母 a。這件事好像是一瞬間發生的，也好像很簡單。其實不簡單。從你的手指到螢幕之間，這一次按鍵換了四次樣子。我們跟著它走一趟。
每個鍵的下面都有一個開關。你按下鍵，開關接通，鍵盤就送一個數給電腦。這個數指的不是一個字母，而是一個鍵：它說的是「哪一個鍵被按了」。在 USB 鍵盤上，A 鍵是第 4 號鍵。不管你有沒有按住 Shift，鍵盤送出的都是同一個數；你放開鍵的時候，它還會再回報一次。
接下來，電腦要決定這個鍵是什麼意思。它看三樣東西：鍵的編號、Shift 有沒有按著、你選的鍵盤配置。從這三樣，它挑出一個字元。第 4 號鍵、沒按 Shift，是 a；第 4 號鍵、按著 Shift，是 A。第二課說過，每個字元都有自己的編號：a 是 97，A 是 65。
97 這個數，以八個位元放進記憶體：01100001。現在，你正在打字的那個程式多了一個字元可以用；處理器一小步一小步地執行那個程式的指令，就像第六課那樣。如果你存檔，這些位元會被抄到儲存裝置，就像第七課那樣。
到這裡，你還是什麼都看不到。要把這個字元顯示出來，電腦需要它的形狀，而形狀來自字型。字型就是一整套字元的形狀。電腦用字型決定螢幕上哪些像素要亮，字母就出現了。換一種字型，亮的像素就不一樣，可是記憶體裡的字元還是 97。
每一台電腦都照這個模式工作：輸入、處理、輸出。輸入裝置（像鍵盤、滑鼠、麥克風）把外面世界的東西變成二進位的電訊號；電腦處理這些訊號；輸出裝置（像螢幕、印表機、喇叭）再把訊號變回人看得懂、聽得懂的東西。開關、位元、編碼、處理器、記憶體——前八課講過的每一樣東西，都參與了這一次按鍵。
questions: What does a keyboard send to the computer when you press a key?
Why do a and A come from the same key but have different numbers in memory?
Name one input device and one output device, and say what each one does.
answers: It sends a number that says which key was pressed. It does not send a letter. The computer decides which character the key means.
The key sends the same key number both times. The computer looks at the key number, the Shift key, and the keyboard layout, and picks a different character: a is 97, and A is 65.
For example, a keyboard is an input device: it turns key presses into signals the computer can use. A screen is an output device: it turns the computer’s signals into pictures a person can see.

vocab.ex: A keyboard gives the computer its input.
vocab.exzh: 鍵盤把輸入交給電腦。

vocab.ex: The sound from the speakers is output.
vocab.exzh: 喇叭發出的聲音是輸出。

vocab.ex: A mouse is a small device that you move with your hand.
vocab.exzh: 滑鼠是一個用手移動的小裝置。

vocab.ex: Press the space bar to start the game.
vocab.exzh: 按空白鍵開始遊戲。

vocab.ex: Release the key when you hear the beep.
vocab.exzh: 聽到嗶一聲就放開按鍵。

vocab.ex: A French keyboard has a different layout.
vocab.exzh: 法文鍵盤的配置不一樣。

vocab.ex: She chose a larger font for the title.
vocab.exzh: 她幫標題選了比較大的字型。

vocab.ex: A microphone converts sound into electrical signals.
vocab.exzh: 麥克風把聲音轉換成電訊號。

Which of these is an output device?

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: Follow the dot all the way. At which stop does the key first become a letter?
parts.text_zh: 跟著光點走完全程。這個鍵是在哪一站才第一次變成一個字母？

parts.meta_zh: 鍵的編號一樣，字元不一樣
parts.text_en: Now Shift is held down. Which stop still shows the same number as before, and which ones change?
parts.text_zh: 這次按住 Shift。哪一站的數字和剛才一樣？哪幾站變了？

parts.text_en: The key says 1 on top, but an exclamation mark appears. Who decided that: the keyboard or the computer?
parts.text_zh: 鍵上面寫的是 1，出現的卻是驚嘆號。這是誰決定的：鍵盤，還是電腦？

parts.meta_en: No pixels, but still a character
parts.meta_zh: 一個像素都不亮，可是還是一個字元
parts.text_en: Watch the memory cells and the screen. Is a space nothing at all?
parts.text_zh: 注意看記憶體的格子和螢幕。空白真的什麼都沒有嗎？

lessons.parts_note_en: Then tap a row in the list of stops to jump straight to that stop, or tap a key in the 3D model.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 接著可以點右邊清單裡的任何一站直接跳過去，或直接點 3D 模型裡的鍵。

stages.lead_en: A key press takes three forms on its way: a key number, a character number, and lit pixels. Eight questions. For each one, choose the form that fits.
stages.lead_zh: 一次按鍵在路上有三種樣子：鍵的編號、字元的編號、亮起來的像素。一共八題，每一題選出符合的那一種。

tasks.en: What travels along the cable from the keyboard
tasks.zh: 從鍵盤沿著線送出來的東西
tasks.why_en: The keyboard only says which key was pressed.
tasks.why_zh: 鍵盤只說「哪一個鍵被按了」。

tasks.en: What is kept in memory for the letter you typed
tasks.zh: 你打的那個字母，放在記憶體裡的東西
tasks.why_en: Memory holds the character’s number, as bits.
tasks.why_zh: 記憶體裡放的是字元的編號，用位元表示。

tasks.en: What you finally see
tasks.zh: 你最後看到的東西
tasks.why_en: The screen shows the character by lighting pixels.
tasks.why_zh: 螢幕靠點亮像素把字元顯示出來。

tasks.en: The one that is the same for a and A
tasks.zh: a 和 A 一樣的那一種
tasks.why_en: Both come from the same key, so the key number is the same.
tasks.why_zh: 兩個都來自同一個鍵，所以鍵的編號一樣。

tasks.en: The one that is 97 for a and 65 for A
tasks.zh: a 是 97、A 是 65 的那一種
tasks.why_en: Each character has its own number.
tasks.why_zh: 每個字元都有自己的編號。

tasks.en: The one that changes when you choose a different font
tasks.zh: 換一種字型就會變的那一種
tasks.why_en: A font changes the shape, so other pixels light up. The character number stays the same.
tasks.why_zh: 字型改的是形狀，所以亮的像素不一樣；字元的編號不變。

tasks.en: The one a keyboard can produce all by itself
tasks.zh: 鍵盤自己就能產生的那一種
tasks.why_en: Turning it into a character is the computer’s job.
tasks.why_zh: 把它變成字元，是電腦的工作。

tasks.en: The one a space has none of
tasks.zh: 空白完全沒有的那一種
tasks.why_en: A space has a key number, 44, and a character number, 32, but it lights no pixels.
tasks.why_zh: 空白有鍵的編號（44），也有字元的編號（32），可是一個像素都不亮。

io.lead_en: Input devices bring things into the computer. Output devices bring things out to you. Some devices do both. Eight devices: decide which kind each one is.
io.lead_zh: 輸入裝置把東西送進電腦，輸出裝置把東西送出來給你，有些裝置兩樣都做。一共八種裝置，分辨每一種是哪一類。

tasks.en: Keyboard
tasks.zh: 鍵盤
tasks.why_en: Your key presses go into the computer.
tasks.why_zh: 你的按鍵送進電腦。

tasks.en: Printer
tasks.zh: 印表機
tasks.why_en: The computer’s work comes out on paper.
tasks.why_zh: 電腦做好的東西印在紙上送出來。

tasks.en: Microphone
tasks.zh: 麥克風
tasks.why_en: Sound goes into the computer.
tasks.why_zh: 聲音送進電腦。

tasks.en: Speakers
tasks.zh: 喇叭
tasks.why_en: Sound comes out to your ears.
tasks.why_zh: 聲音送出來給你的耳朵。

tasks.en: Mouse
tasks.zh: 滑鼠
tasks.why_en: Your hand movements and clicks go in.
tasks.why_zh: 手的移動和點按送進電腦。

tasks.en: Headphones
tasks.zh: 耳機
tasks.why_en: Like speakers, they bring sound out to you.
tasks.why_zh: 和喇叭一樣，把聲音送出來給你。

tasks.en: Webcam
tasks.zh: 網路攝影機
tasks.why_en: Pictures go into the computer.
tasks.why_zh: 影像送進電腦。

tasks.en: Touch screen
tasks.zh: 觸控螢幕
tasks.why_en: It shows you a picture, which is output, and it senses your finger, which is input.
tasks.why_zh: 它顯示畫面給你看（輸出），又感應你的手指（輸入）。

io.note_en: The first seven follow Britannica’s lists of input and output devices. The touch screen is our own example of what Britannica calls a device that provides both.
io.note_zh: 前七種依照大英百科列出的輸入與輸出裝置。觸控螢幕是我們自己舉的例子，說明大英百科所說「兩樣都提供」的裝置。

live.lead_en: Your web browser can tell a page two different things about a key press: which key it was, and what it typed. Click the box, then press a key. Press it again while holding Shift, and see which of the two answers changes.
live.lead_zh: 瀏覽器可以告訴網頁關於一次按鍵的兩件事：按的是哪一個鍵，以及打出了什麼。先點一下框框，再按一個鍵；按住 Shift 再按一次，看看這兩個答案是哪一個變了。
live.note_en: This box shows your key presses only on your own screen. Nothing is sent anywhere. The names such as KeyA are the browser’s own names for keys; they are not the USB key numbers used in the model above.
live.note_zh: 這個框框只把你按的鍵顯示在你自己的螢幕上，不會送到任何地方。KeyA 這類名稱是瀏覽器自己給鍵取的名字，不是上面模型用的 USB 鍵編號。

tips.en: “Which key” stays the same with Shift. “What it typed” changes.
tips.zh: 「哪一個鍵」按不按 Shift 都一樣；「打出什麼」會變。

tips.en: Try a key that types nothing, such as an arrow key. It still has a name.
tips.zh: 試試不會打出字的鍵，例如方向鍵。它還是有名字。

tips.en: If your computer has another keyboard layout, the same key may type a different character.
tips.zh: 如果你的電腦設了別的鍵盤配置，同一個鍵可能打出不一樣的字元。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Keys · 按鍵的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A key that reports twice, one keyboard for many languages, a typewriter without Shift, and letters without shapes
culture_cards.title_zh: 回報兩次的鍵、一個鍵盤打很多種語言、沒有 Shift 的打字機、沒有形狀的字母
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about what a key press really is.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於「一次按鍵到底是什麼」的四個小故事。

cards.k: Down and up · 按下與放開
cards.en: A key reports twice
cards.body_en: Microsoft’s guide for programmers explains that each key on a keyboard has a unique value called a scan code, and that a keyboard generates two scan codes when you type a key: one when you press it and another when you release it. That is how a game knows you are still holding a key down, and how the computer knows that Shift is still held while you press something else.
cards.body_zh: 微軟寫給程式設計師的說明提到：鍵盤上每個鍵都有一個獨一無二的值，叫做掃描碼（scan code）；你打一個鍵，鍵盤會產生兩個掃描碼，按下去一個，放開又一個。遊戲就是這樣知道你還按著某個鍵沒放，電腦也是這樣知道你按別的鍵時 Shift 還按著。

cards.k: Y and Z · Y 和 Z
cards.en: One keyboard, many languages
cards.body_en: The USB keyboard standard gives an example. On a North American keyboard there is a Y key; in Germany the key in that position is typically Z. The standard says the maker should not change the electronics. Both keyboards send the same key number, and only the letter printed on the key is different. The computer’s layout setting decides which letter it means.
cards.body_zh: USB 鍵盤標準裡舉了一個例子。北美的鍵盤上有一個 Y 鍵，在德國，同一個位置的鍵通常是 Z。標準說，製造商不必更動裡面的電子零件：兩種鍵盤送出同一個鍵的編號，不一樣的只有印在鍵帽上的字母。到底是哪個字母，由電腦的鍵盤配置設定決定。

cards.en: The first typewriter had no Shift
cards.zh: 第一台打字機沒有 Shift
cards.body_en: According to Britannica, the first practical typewriter was built by the American inventor Christopher Latham Sholes, patented in 1868, and sold from 1874 by the Remington company. It wrote capital letters only. The first shift-key typewriter, the Remington Model 2, appeared in 1878: each bar carried two letters, a capital and a small one, and the shift key chose between them. Britannica adds that the positions of the characters on that early keyboard conform almost exactly to the arrangement that is now universal.
cards.body_zh: 根據大英百科，第一台實用的打字機由美國發明家蕭爾斯（Christopher Latham Sholes）製造，1868 年取得專利，1874 年起由雷明頓公司販售。它只能打大寫字母。第一台有 Shift 鍵的打字機是 1878 年的雷明頓二號：每根字桿上有兩個字，一大寫一小寫，由 Shift 鍵決定用哪一個。大英百科還說，那台早期機器上各個字元的位置，和現在通用的排法幾乎完全一樣。

cards.k: Character and glyph · 字元與字形
cards.en: A character has no shape of its own
cards.body_en: The Unicode Standard’s glossary keeps two ideas apart. A character is what is stored: a number. A glyph is a shape used to show it. A font is “a collection of glyphs used for the visual depiction of character data,” and rendering is the process of choosing glyphs and making them visible on a display. So the 97 in memory is not round or tall or bold. It gets a shape only at the last stop.
cards.body_zh: Unicode 標準的詞彙表把兩個概念分得很清楚。字元（character）是存起來的東西：一個數。字形（glyph）是用來顯示它的形狀。字型（font）是「一整套用來把字元資料顯示出來的字形」，而算繪（rendering）就是挑選字形、讓它們在顯示器上看得見的過程。所以記憶體裡的 97 沒有圓不圓、高不高、粗不粗的問題。它到最後一站才有形狀。

myths.myth_en: The keyboard sends the letter A to the computer.
myths.myth_zh: 鍵盤把字母 A 送給電腦。
myths.fact_en: It sends a number that says which key was pressed. The computer decides which character that key means.
myths.fact_zh: 它送的是一個編號，說的是哪一個鍵被按了。這個鍵代表哪個字元，是電腦決定的。

myths.myth_en: Holding Shift makes the A key send something different.
myths.myth_zh: 按住 Shift，A 鍵送出的東西就不一樣。
myths.fact_en: The USB keyboard standard says a key does not send extra codes because of Shift. The A key sends the same number either way; Shift is reported separately.
myths.fact_zh: USB 鍵盤標準寫明，鍵不會因為 Shift 而多送別的碼。A 鍵送的編號都一樣，Shift 是另外回報的。

myths.myth_en: The letter printed on a key decides what it types.
myths.myth_zh: 鍵上印的字母，決定它打出什麼。
myths.fact_en: The printing is only a label for you. The computer’s keyboard layout setting decides, which is why one keyboard can type in many languages.
myths.fact_zh: 印在上面的字只是給你看的標籤。決定的是電腦的鍵盤配置設定，所以同一個鍵盤可以打很多種語言。

myths.myth_en: A space is nothing.
myths.myth_zh: 空白就是什麼都沒有。
myths.fact_en: A space is a character with its own number, 32, and it takes up room in memory like any letter. It just lights no pixels.
myths.fact_zh: 空白是一個字元，有自己的編號 32，和任何字母一樣要占記憶體。它只是不點亮任何像素。

tricks_head.en: One key press in a sentence

tricks.body_en: Input, processing, output.
tricks.body_zh: 輸入、處理、輸出。

tricks.body_en: The keyboard says which key. The computer says which character.
tricks.body_zh: 鍵盤說是哪個鍵；電腦說是哪個字元。

tricks.body_en: a is 97. A is 65. One key.
tricks.body_zh: a 是 97，A 是 65，同一個鍵。

tricks.body_en: Memory keeps the number. The font gives the shape.
tricks.body_zh: 記憶體放的是編號；形狀是字型給的。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: Do not pull the keys off a keyboard to look at the switches. On many keyboards they break or do not go back on.
safety.zh: 不要為了看開關而把鍵帽拔下來。很多鍵盤的鍵一拔就壞，或裝不回去。

safety.en: Never type a password into a page or program that is only showing you which keys you press.
safety.zh: 只是用來顯示你按了什麼鍵的網頁或程式，絕對不要在裡面打密碼。

safety.en: Do not change the keyboard layout on a school or family computer without asking. If you change it, change it back.
safety.zh: 沒有問過，不要改學校或家裡電腦的鍵盤配置。改了就要改回來。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意。

materials.en: Five desks in a row, labeled Keyboard, Cable, Processor, Memory, and Screen
materials.zh: 排成一排的五張桌子，分別標上：鍵盤、線、處理器、記憶體、螢幕

materials.en: Small cards and pencils
materials.zh: 小卡片和鉛筆

materials.en: A lookup sheet for the Processor desk: key 4 → a (97), key 4 with Shift → A (65), key 30 → 1 (49), key 30 with Shift → ! (33), key 44 → space (32)
materials.zh: 給「處理器」那一桌的對照表：第 4 號鍵 → a（97）、第 4 號鍵加 Shift → A（65）、第 30 號鍵 → 1（49）、第 30 號鍵加 Shift → !（33）、第 44 號鍵 → 空白（32）

materials.en: Squared paper for the Screen desk, with a grid 5 squares across and 7 down
materials.zh: 給「螢幕」那一桌的方格紙，畫好橫 5 格、直 7 格的格子

steps.en: The teacher whispers a key to the Keyboard student, for example “the A key, with Shift.” The Keyboard writes only a key number on a card, 4, and adds “Shift” if it is held. No letters allowed.
steps.zh: 老師小聲告訴「鍵盤」同學一個鍵，例如「A 鍵，加 Shift」。「鍵盤」只能在卡片上寫鍵的編號 4，有按 Shift 就加寫「Shift」。不可以寫字母。

steps.en: The Cable carries the card to the Processor, who uses the lookup sheet and writes the character number on a new card: 65.
steps.zh: 「線」把卡片送給「處理器」。「處理器」查對照表，在新的卡片上寫下字元的編號：65。

steps.en: Memory writes that number as eight bits, 01000001, and passes it on.
steps.zh: 「記憶體」把那個數寫成八個位元 01000001，再傳下去。

steps.en: The Screen turns the bits back into a number, finds the character, and colors in squares on the grid to draw it. The class reads the screen: is it the key the teacher whispered?
steps.zh: 「螢幕」把位元換回數字、找出是哪個字元，在方格上塗出它的樣子。全班看螢幕：是老師小聲說的那個鍵嗎？

activities.tip_en: Ask afterward: which student was the first to know it was a letter? Then let two Screen students draw the same character. Their drawings will differ a little, and that is what a font is. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson matches the topic “System platforms”: 資 S-IV-2, whose notes list input and output.
activities.tip_zh: 做完問大家：哪一位同學是第一個知道它是字母的人？再請兩位「螢幕」同學畫同一個字元，兩個人畫的會有一點不一樣，這就是字型。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課對應「系統平台」主題：資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（附錄的說明列有輸入輸出）。

activities.title_en: Check It on Your Own Computer

materials.en: A computer with a keyboard that has real keys
materials.zh: 一台有實體鍵盤的電腦

materials.en: The “Ask Your Own Keyboard” box on this page
materials.zh: 這一頁的「問問自己的鍵盤」那個框框

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Click the box and press the A key. Write down the two answers: which key, and what it typed.
steps.zh: 點一下框框，按 A 鍵。把兩個答案寫下來：哪一個鍵、打出什麼。

steps.en: Hold Shift and press A again. Which answer changed, and which stayed the same?
steps.zh: 按住 Shift 再按一次 A。哪一個答案變了？哪一個沒變？

steps.en: Do the same with the 1 key and with the space bar. Write the character number for each.
steps.zh: 用 1 鍵和空白鍵各做一次，把每個字元的編號寫下來。

steps.en: If your keyboard has a number pad, press the 1 there, and then the 1 above the letters. Both type 1. Do they have the same key name?
steps.zh: 如果你的鍵盤有數字鍵區，按那裡的 1，再按字母上方的 1。兩個都打出 1，它們的鍵名一樣嗎？

activities.tip_en: With the U.S. layout you should find: A key, a = 97 and A = 65; 1 key, 1 = 49 and ! = 33; space bar, 32. The two numbers for a and A differ by exactly 32, which is one bit. If your numbers are different, your computer is probably set to another keyboard layout, and that is the lesson too.
activities.tip_zh: 用美式配置應該會看到：A 鍵，a＝97、A＝65；1 鍵，1＝49、!＝33；空白鍵 32。a 和 A 這兩個數剛好差 32，也就是只差一個位元。如果你看到的數字不一樣，你的電腦大概設了別的鍵盤配置——這也正是這一課要說的事。

links_head.en: The stops along the way, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 路上的每一站，以及下一課

links.en: Why Does a Computer Need Two Kinds of Memory?
links.zh: 電腦為什麼要有兩種記憶？
links.note_en: The character you typed sits in memory. It reaches storage only when you save.
links.note_zh: 你打的字元待在記憶體裡，存檔的時候才會到儲存裝置。

links.en: How Do 0s and 1s Become Words, Pictures, and Sound?
links.zh: 0 和 1 怎麼變成文字、圖片和聲音？
links.note_en: Where the numbers 97 and 65 come from, and how a grid of pixels makes a picture.
links.note_zh: 97 和 65 這些編號是哪裡來的，以及一格一格的像素怎麼拼成圖。

links.en: What Does a Processor Do All Day?
links.note_en: The lookup in the middle of the trip is a program, carried out one small step at a time.
links.note_zh: 路程中間那一次查表，是一個程式，由處理器一小步一小步執行。

links.en: What Is a Program?
links.note_en: Unit 2 ends here: you have seen the whole machine. Unit 3 is about software, the instructions that tell the machine what to do.
links.note_zh: 單元二到這裡結束：整台機器你都看過了。單元三要講軟體，也就是告訴機器該做什麼的那些指令。

lessons.sources_note_en: Facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); the model and its small letter shapes are our own illustration, and its rules are tested
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；模型和裡面小小的字形是我們自己的示意，規則有測試

sources.en: Usage 0x04 is “Keyboard a and A,” 0x1E is “Keyboard 1 and !,” 0x2C is “Keyboard Spacebar”; a key “does not send extra codes to compensate for the state of any Control, Alt, Shift or Num Lock keys”; the Y key on a North American keyboard is typically Z in Germany, and the vendor should use the Y usage on both
sources.zh: 編號 0x04 是「Keyboard a and A」、0x1E 是「Keyboard 1 and !」、0x2C 是「Keyboard Spacebar」；鍵不會因為 Control、Alt、Shift、Num Lock 的狀態而多送別的碼；北美鍵盤的 Y 鍵在德國通常是 Z，製造商在兩種鍵盤上都應該用 Y 的編號
sources.src: USB Implementers Forum, HID Usage Tables for Universal Serial Bus (USB), Version 1.5, section 10, “Keyboard/Keypad Page (0x07)”

sources.en: “Assigned to each key on a keyboard is a unique value called a scan code, a device-dependent identifier for the key”; a keyboard generates two scan codes when the user types a key, one on press and one on release; the keyboard layout translates scan codes into messages for the application
sources.zh: 鍵盤上每個鍵都有一個獨一無二的值，叫掃描碼，是隨裝置而定的鍵識別碼；使用者打一個鍵，鍵盤產生兩個掃描碼（按下一個、放開一個）；鍵盤配置把掃描碼轉成給應用程式的訊息
sources.src: Microsoft Learn, “About Keyboard Input”

sources.en: KeyboardEvent.code “represents a physical key on the keyboard (as opposed to the character generated by pressing the key)” and is not altered by the keyboard layout or the modifier keys; KeyboardEvent.key returns the value of the key pressed, taking into consideration modifier keys such as Shift and the keyboard locale and layout
sources.zh: KeyboardEvent.code 代表鍵盤上實體的那個鍵（不是按下它產生的字元），不受鍵盤配置與修飾鍵影響；KeyboardEvent.key 回傳按下的鍵的值，會考慮 Shift 這類修飾鍵以及鍵盤的語系與配置
sources.src: MDN Web Docs, “KeyboardEvent: code property” and “KeyboardEvent: key property”

sources.en: An input device converts incoming data and instructions into a pattern of electrical signals in binary code; an output device reverses the process; input devices include keyboards, the mouse, microphones, and webcams; output equipment includes video displays, printers, loudspeakers, and headphones; some devices may provide both input and output
sources.zh: 輸入裝置把進來的資料與指令轉換成二進位碼的電訊號；輸出裝置把這個過程反過來；輸入裝置包括鍵盤、滑鼠、麥克風、網路攝影機；輸出設備包括顯示器、印表機、喇叭、耳機；有些裝置同時提供輸入和輸出
sources.src: The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica, “peripheral device” (revised by Erik Gregersen)

sources.en: Sholes built the first practical typewriter; patented June 23, 1868; on the market in 1874 and soon renamed the Remington; the first typewriter wrote capital letters only; the first shift-key typewriter, the Remington Model 2, appeared in 1878; the positions of the characters conform almost exactly to the arrangement that is now universal
sources.zh: 蕭爾斯造出第一台實用的打字機；1868 年 6 月 23 日取得專利；1874 年上市，不久改名雷明頓；第一台打字機只能打大寫；第一台有 Shift 鍵的打字機（雷明頓二號）1878 年問世；字元的位置和現在通用的排法幾乎完全一樣
sources.src: The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica, “typewriter”

sources.en: Font: “A collection of glyphs used for the visual depiction of character data”; rendering: the process of selecting and laying out glyphs to depict characters, and of making glyphs visible on a display device
sources.zh: 字型：一整套用來把字元資料顯示出來的字形；算繪：挑選並排列字形來呈現字元、讓字形在顯示裝置上看得見的過程
sources.src: Unicode Consortium, “Glossary of Unicode Terms”

sources.en: A = 65 and a = 97 in ASCII (see Lesson 2)
sources.zh: ASCII 裡 A＝65、a＝97（見第二課）
sources.src: Encyclopaedia Britannica, “ASCII”

sources.en: Taiwan terms: output device 輸出裝置, peripheral device 週邊裝置, scan code 掃描碼, font 字型. For keyboard layout the term bank gives 鍵盤布局; this page uses 鍵盤配置, the wording more common in Taiwan’s software
sources.zh: 台灣用語：output device 輸出裝置、peripheral device 週邊裝置、scan code 掃描碼、font 字型。keyboard layout 樂詞網作「鍵盤布局」；本頁用台灣軟體介面較常見的「鍵盤配置」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《樂詞網》

sources.en: 資 S-IV-2, how system platforms are built and basically work (p. 10); the notes list the operating system, CPU, memory, and input and output (p. 43)
sources.zh: 資 S-IV-2 系統平台之組成架構與基本運作原理（第 10 頁）；附錄三的說明：「系統軟硬體架構與運作原理：作業系統、CPU、記憶體、輸入輸出」（第 43 頁）
sources.src: 教育部《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校 科技領域》（2018）
sources.url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/816/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校-科技領域.pdf

sources.src: Our own illustration, checked by tools/computers/test/keypath.test.mjs

units.title_en: Software: Telling the Computer What to Do
units.blurb_en: What a program is, why one method can be far faster than another, how one processor serves many programs, and how a file can get smaller.
units.blurb_zh: 程式是什麼、為什麼同一件事換個方法會快很多、一個處理器怎麼同時服務很多程式，以及檔案為什麼可以變小。

lessons.title: What Is a Program?
lessons.blurb_en: A small robot on a floor of squares does exactly what its program says, one instruction at a time. Watch it walk a staircase in fifteen instructions, then in five. Leave one instruction out and see where it ends up. Then write your own programs for three levels: in order, with a repeat, and with a question.
lessons.blurb_zh: 格子地板上的一台小機器人，完全照程式說的做，一次一條指令。看它用十五條指令走一段階梯，再看它只用五條；漏掉一條，看它最後停在哪裡。接著自己寫程式闖三關：照順序、用重複、會問問題。
lessons.big_idea_en: A program is a list of instructions, in order, with nothing left unclear. The computer does exactly what the program says. It does not guess what you meant. Three ideas are enough to build one: do things in order, repeat things, and choose what to do by asking a question.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 程式是一串照順序排好、沒有任何含糊地方的指令。電腦完全照程式說的做，不會去猜你的意思。組出一個程式只需要三個觀念：照順序做、重複做、先問一個問題再決定做什麼。

lab.title_en: The Robot That Does Exactly What It Is Told
lab.title_zh: 說什麼就做什麼的機器人
lab.how_en: The robot understands only a few instructions: forward, turn left, turn right, repeat, and “if there is a wall ahead.” Choose one of the four programs on the right and press Run. The line the robot is carrying out lights up. Compare the first two programs: they do the same walk. Then run the third, which has one line missing, and the fourth, which works in two different rooms.
lab.how_zh: 機器人只聽得懂幾種指令：前進、左轉、右轉、重複，還有「如果前面是牆」。在右邊四個程式裡選一個，按「執行」，機器人正在做的那一行會亮起來。比一比前兩個程式：它們走的是同一段路。再跑第三個（漏了一行），和第四個（在兩個不同的房間都走得到）。

legend.en: The robot
legend.zh: 機器人

legend.en: Teal pointer: the way the robot is facing
legend.zh: 青色箭頭：機器人面向哪一邊

legend.en: Walls: the robot cannot pass
legend.zh: 牆：機器人過不去

legend.en: The flag: where the program should take the robot
legend.zh: 旗子：程式要把機器人帶到的地方

legend.en: Green squares: where the robot has been
legend.zh: 綠色的格子：機器人走過的地方

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The robot’s instructions are a tiny language we made up for this lesson; it is not a real programming language. Real programs are written in languages such as Python and are then translated, in several stages, into machine instructions like the ones in Lesson 6. In the model a mistake is easy to see, because the robot ends up in the wrong place. In a real program a mistake can be much harder to notice.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。機器人的指令是我們為這一課自己設計的小語言，不是真的程式語言。真的程式是用 Python 這類語言寫的，再分好幾個階段翻譯成第六課那種機器指令。在模型裡，錯誤很容易看出來，因為機器人停在不對的地方；真的程式裡，錯誤可能難發現得多。
lab.credit_html:
Model and code are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The robot’s rules and every program on this page are tested in tools/computers/test/robot.test.mjs.
模型與程式由人師教育協會自行繪製、撰寫；機器人的規則和這一頁每一個程式都有自動測試（tools/computers/test/robot.test.mjs）。

paras: In Lesson 6 you watched a processor fetch an instruction, carry it out, and fetch the next one. But where do the instructions come from? People write them. A list of instructions written for a computer is called a program. An encyclopedia describes a program as an unambiguous, ordered sequence of instructions. Two words there matter most: ordered, and unambiguous.

Think of a small robot on a floor of squares. It understands only three instructions: forward, turn left, and turn right. To send it to a flag, you write the instructions one under another, and the robot carries them out from top to bottom. The order matters. “Forward, then turn left” and “turn left, then forward” end on different squares.

The robot does exactly what is written. If you leave out one “turn right,” it does not notice. It carries on and finishes somewhere else. If you tell it to go forward when a wall is in the way, it walks into the wall. A mistake in a program is called a bug, and finding and fixing it is called debugging. When a program goes wrong, it is usually because the computer did just what it was told.

Often a program does the same thing again and again. To climb four stairs, the robot does “forward, turn left, forward, turn right” over and over. Written out one by one, that is a long list. It is better to write those four once and say “repeat 4 times.” This is called a loop. The program becomes shorter, and it is easier to read and to change.

Sometimes the right move depends on what the robot finds. So a program can ask a question: “If there is a wall ahead, turn left.” The robot checks, and it does the inside part only when the answer is yes. A program with a question in it can work in rooms its writer has never seen. In the same way, a real program can wait to see which key you press.

These are the three building blocks: doing things in order, repeating, and choosing. Real programs are written in programming languages such as Python, and then they are translated, in several stages, into the machine language of Lesson 6. A game or a web browser may have millions of lines. But line by line, it is still someone’s instructions, carried out exactly.
paras_zh: 在第六課，你看過處理器拿一條指令、照著做、再拿下一條。可是這些指令是哪裡來的？是人寫的。寫給電腦的一串指令，就叫做程式。百科全書對程式的描述是：一串沒有含糊之處、照順序排好的指令。這裡面最重要的是兩個詞：照順序，以及沒有含糊之處。
想像格子地板上有一台小機器人。它只聽得懂三種指令：前進、左轉、右轉。要讓它走到旗子，你把指令一條一條往下寫，機器人就從上到下照著做。順序很重要。「先前進再左轉」和「先左轉再前進」，最後停在不同的格子。
機器人完全照寫的做。你漏寫一條「右轉」，它不會發現，繼續做下去，最後停在別的地方。前面明明有牆，你還叫它前進，它就撞上去。程式裡的錯誤叫做 bug（程式錯誤），把它找出來、改掉叫做除錯（debugging）。程式出問題的時候，通常正是因為電腦完全照著指示做了。
程式常常要把同一件事做很多遍。要爬四級階梯，機器人得把「前進、左轉、前進、右轉」做了又做。一條一條寫出來，是很長的一串。比較好的寫法是：這四條只寫一次，然後說「重複 4 次」。這叫做迴圈（loop）。程式變短了，也比較好讀、好改。
有時候該怎麼走，要看機器人遇到什麼。所以程式可以問一個問題：「如果前面是牆，就左轉。」機器人會去檢查，答案是「是」才做裡面的事。帶著問題的程式，連寫的人從來沒看過的房間都走得通。同樣的道理，真正的程式可以等著看你按的是哪一個鍵。
這就是三種積木：照順序做、重複、選擇。真的程式是用 Python 這類程式語言寫的，再分好幾個階段翻譯成第六課的機器語言。一個遊戲或一個瀏覽器可能有幾百萬行。可是一行一行看，它仍然是某個人寫下的指令，被一絲不差地執行。
questions: What is a program, and which two words in the encyclopedia’s description matter most?
The robot ends up in the wrong place. Whose mistake is it, and why?
What are the three building blocks of a program? Give an example of each from the robot.
answers: A program is a list of instructions written for a computer. The two words are “ordered” (the instructions are carried out in order) and “unambiguous” (each one has only one meaning).
It is the mistake of the person who wrote the program. The robot did exactly what was written. It cannot guess what the writer meant.
Doing things in order: forward, then turn left. Repeating: “repeat 4 times” around four instructions. Choosing: “if there is a wall ahead, turn left.”

vocab.ex: She wrote a short program to draw a square.
vocab.exzh: 她寫了一個短短的程式來畫正方形。

vocab.ex: Read each instruction before you begin.
vocab.exzh: 開始之前，把每一條指示都讀一遍。

vocab.ex: Put the steps in the right order.
vocab.exzh: 把步驟照正確的順序排好。

vocab.ex: Repeat the last two steps three times.
vocab.exzh: 把最後兩個步驟重複三次。

vocab.ex: The door opens only on one condition: you must know the code.
vocab.exzh: 門只在一個條件下才會開：你得知道密碼。

vocab.ex: There is a bug in my program, so the robot hits the wall.
vocab.exzh: 我的程式有一個 bug，所以機器人撞到牆。

vocab.ex: The robot did exactly what I wrote.
vocab.exzh: 機器人完全照我寫的做了。

vocab.ex: A computer cannot guess what you mean.
vocab.exzh: 電腦沒辦法猜你的意思。

quiz.q: What is a program?
options: An ordered list of instructions for a computer

quiz.q: You leave out one instruction. What does the robot do?
options: It carries on and does exactly what is written.
It goes back to the start.

quiz.q: What is a loop for?
options: Doing the same instructions again and again without writing them many times

quiz.q: “If there is a wall ahead, turn left.” When does the robot turn left?
options: Only when there is a wall ahead

quiz.q: What is debugging?
options: Finding and fixing mistakes in a program

parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試
parts_head.zh: 四個值得跑一跑的程式

parts.text_en: Watch the lit line move down the program. Do you see a group of four instructions that keeps coming back?
parts.text_zh: 看亮起來的那一行一路往下走。你有沒有發現，有四條指令一直重複出現？

parts.meta_zh: 同一段路，只要 5 條指令
parts.text_en: The robot takes the same fifteen steps. How many instructions did someone have to write this time?
parts.text_zh: 機器人走的是一樣的十五步。這一次，寫的人要寫幾條指令？

parts.text_en: One “turn right” was left out. Where does the robot finish? Can you tell which line is missing?
parts.text_zh: 有一條「右轉」被漏掉了。機器人最後停在哪裡？你看得出漏的是哪一行嗎？

parts.text_en: Before each step the robot checks for a wall. After it reaches the flag, send the same program into the other room.
parts.text_zh: 機器人每走一步之前都先看看有沒有牆。它走到旗子之後，把同一個程式換到另一個房間再跑一次。

lessons.parts_note_en: Use “One step” to go through any program slowly, one instruction at a time.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 想慢慢看的話，用「一次一步」，一條指令一條指令地走。

maze.lead_en: Three levels, one for each building block. Tap the blocks to add instructions to your program. Tap an instruction in your program to take it out. Then press Run and watch the robot do exactly what you wrote.
maze.lead_zh: 一共三關，三種積木各一關。點積木，把指令加進你的程式；點程式裡的指令，可以把它拿掉。然後按「執行」，看機器人完全照你寫的做。

levels.hint_en: Level 1. Get the robot to the flag. The robot starts facing up.
levels.hint_zh: 第一關。把機器人帶到旗子。機器人一開始面向上方。

levels.hint_en: Level 2. A staircase. Your instructions go inside a repeat, and there is room for only four. Choose how many times to repeat. The robot starts facing right.
levels.hint_zh: 第二關。一段階梯。你的指令放在「重複」裡面，而且只放得下四條。自己決定要重複幾次。機器人一開始面向右邊。

levels.hint_en: Level 3. There is room for only two instructions inside the repeat. You will need a block that asks about the wall. The robot starts facing right.
levels.hint_zh: 第三關。「重複」裡面只放得下兩條指令。你會用到問「前面是不是牆」的積木。機器人一開始面向右邊。

maze.note_en: The robot stops as soon as it reaches the flag, so repeating a few more times than needed does no harm. If it walks into a wall, the whole program stops there.
maze.note_zh: 機器人一走到旗子就會停下來，所以重複的次數比需要的多幾次沒有關係。如果它撞到牆，整個程式就停在那裡。

tips.en: Stuck? Run a program that is not finished. Seeing where the robot goes wrong tells you what to fix.
tips.zh: 卡住了？把還沒寫完的程式先跑跑看。看到機器人在哪裡出錯，就知道要改什麼。

tips.en: In Level 2, look for the small group of moves that climbs one stair.
tips.zh: 第二關：找出「爬一級階梯」的那一小組動作。

tips.en: In Level 3, the question comes first and the step comes second.
tips.zh: 第三關：先問問題，再走一步。

facing.lead_en: Be the computer. Eight tiny programs made only of turns. Carry out each one in your head, exactly as written, and say which way the robot faces at the end.
facing.lead_zh: 換你當電腦。八個只有轉彎的小程式。在腦子裡一條一條照著做，說出機器人最後面向哪一邊。
facing.ask_en: Which way does it face at the end?

tasks.en: Facing north. Program: turn right.
tasks.zh: 面向北。程式：右轉。
tasks.why_en: One turn to the right from north is east.
tasks.why_zh: 從北邊右轉一次是東。

tasks.en: Facing north. Program: turn left, turn left.
tasks.zh: 面向北。程式：左轉、左轉。
tasks.why_en: Two turns the same way point it backward.
tasks.why_zh: 往同一邊轉兩次，就是向後轉。

tasks.en: Facing east. Program: turn right, turn left.
tasks.zh: 面向東。程式：右轉、左轉。
tasks.why_en: The second turn undoes the first.
tasks.why_zh: 第二次轉彎把第一次抵銷了。

tasks.en: Facing north. Program: repeat 4 times: turn right.
tasks.zh: 面向北。程式：重複 4 次：右轉。
tasks.why_en: Four turns the same way bring it all the way around.
tasks.why_zh: 往同一邊轉四次，剛好轉一整圈。

tasks.en: Facing north. Program: repeat 3 times: turn left.
tasks.zh: 面向北。程式：重複 3 次：左轉。
tasks.why_en: North, west, south, east. Three lefts are the same as one right.
tasks.why_zh: 北、西、南、東。左轉三次等於右轉一次。

tasks.en: Facing south. Program: turn right, turn right, turn right.
tasks.zh: 面向南。程式：右轉、右轉、右轉。
tasks.why_en: South, west, north, east.
tasks.why_zh: 南、西、北、東。

tasks.en: Facing west. Program: repeat 2 times: turn left, turn left.
tasks.zh: 面向西。程式：重複 2 次：左轉、左轉。
tasks.why_en: That is four left turns in all: a full circle.
tasks.why_zh: 一共左轉四次，轉了一整圈。

tasks.en: Facing east. Program: repeat 3 times: turn right, turn right.
tasks.zh: 面向東。程式：重複 3 次：右轉、右轉。
tasks.why_en: Six right turns. Four make a full circle, and the two left over point it backward.
tasks.why_zh: 一共右轉六次。四次是一整圈，剩下兩次就是向後轉。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind Programs · 程式的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A program before computers, a turtle, a moth, and a translator
culture_cards.title_zh: 電腦出現之前的程式、一隻海龜、一隻飛蛾、一位翻譯
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about writing instructions for machines.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於「寫指令給機器」的四個小故事。

cards.en: A program for a machine that was never finished
cards.zh: 寫給一台沒有造完的機器的程式
cards.body_en: In 1843 the English mathematician Ada Lovelace translated an article about Charles Babbage’s Analytical Engine and added long notes of her own. According to Britannica, they included a description of how the machine could be programmed to compute a series of numbers called Bernoulli numbers. Babbage built only a small part of the engine, but Lovelace has been called the first computer programmer, and a programming language, Ada, was named for her.
cards.body_zh: 1843 年，英國數學家愛達・勒芙蕾絲（Ada Lovelace）翻譯了一篇介紹巴貝奇「分析機」的文章，還加上自己寫的長篇註解。根據大英百科，註解裡描述了怎麼替這台機器寫程式，算出一串叫做白努利數的數。巴貝奇只造出分析機的一小部分，但勒芙蕾絲被稱為第一位電腦程式設計師，後來還有一種程式語言以她的名字命名，叫 Ada。

cards.en: Forward, left 90
cards.body_en: The robot in this lesson has a famous ancestor. Britannica explains that the language Logo began in the late 1960s, and that Seymour Papert and others used it at MIT to teach mathematical thinking to schoolchildren. It featured “turtle graphics”: an object was moved around the screen by commands such as “left 90” and “forward,” which describe moves from where the turtle is and the way it is facing. The name came from an early project to program a turtle-like robot.
cards.body_zh: 這一課的機器人有個有名的前輩。大英百科說，Logo 這種語言誕生於 1960 年代後期，派普特（Seymour Papert）等人在麻省理工學院用它教小學生數學思考。它的特色是「海龜繪圖」：用「left 90」「forward」這樣的指令讓一個東西在螢幕上移動，這些指令說的是從海龜現在的位置、面向的方向出發要怎麼動。這個名字來自早期一個替像海龜的機器人寫程式的計畫。

cards.en: A real bug
cards.body_en: The Computer History Museum tells this story. On September 9, 1947, a team working on the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth caught between the contacts of a relay. They taped it into the logbook, and someone wrote beside it: “First actual case of bug being found.” The programmer Grace Hopper was there and later made the story famous in her lectures. The word was not new: the museum notes that “bug” had been used for a fault in a machine since the 1800s.
cards.body_zh: 這個故事出自電腦歷史博物館。1947 年 9 月 9 日，操作哈佛馬克二號電腦的團隊發現一隻飛蛾卡在繼電器的接點之間。他們把牠用膠帶貼進工作日誌，旁邊有人寫了一句：「第一次真的找到蟲（bug）。」程式設計師葛麗絲・霍普（Grace Hopper）當時在場，後來在演講裡把這個故事講得家喻戶曉。這個詞並不是那時才有的：博物館指出，用 bug 來稱呼機器的毛病，從 1800 年代就開始了。

cards.en: From your words to the machine’s
cards.body_en: A processor understands only machine language, the kind of simple instructions you met in Lesson 6. Britannica explains that a program is first written in a language suited to the task, and is then translated, commonly in several stages, into a coded program the computer can carry out directly. The translating is done by other programs. There are even programs called debuggers, which run a program a little at a time so that the programmer can check whether it is working correctly.
cards.body_zh: 處理器只懂機器語言，也就是第六課那種簡單的指令。大英百科說，程式會先用適合那件工作的語言寫出來，再翻譯（通常分好幾個階段）成電腦可以直接執行的編碼程式。做翻譯的，是別的程式。甚至還有一種叫除錯器（debugger）的程式，可以把一個程式一小段一小段地執行，讓程式設計師檢查它運作得對不對。

myths.myth_en: A computer understands what you mean.
myths.myth_zh: 電腦懂你的意思。
myths.fact_en: It carries out the instructions it is given, exactly. That is why a program has to be unambiguous: every instruction must have only one meaning.
myths.fact_zh: 它只是一絲不差地執行拿到的指令。所以程式不能有含糊的地方：每一條指令都只能有一個意思。

myths.myth_en: When a program gives the wrong result, the computer made a mistake.
myths.myth_zh: 程式的結果不對，是電腦弄錯了。
myths.fact_en: Usually the computer did just what it was told, and the mistake is in the instructions. That is what a bug is.
myths.fact_zh: 通常是電腦完全照指示做了，錯在指令本身。這就是 bug。

myths.myth_en: A longer program is a better program.
myths.myth_zh: 程式越長越厲害。
myths.fact_en: The robot’s staircase takes fifteen instructions written out one by one, and five with a repeat. The short one is easier to read, to check, and to change.
myths.fact_zh: 機器人走階梯，一條一條寫要十五條指令，用「重複」只要五條。短的那個比較好讀、好檢查、也好改。

myths.myth_en: Programs began with electronic computers.
myths.myth_zh: 有了電子電腦，才有程式。
myths.fact_en: Ada Lovelace described how to program a machine in 1843, about a hundred years before electronic computers. A program is an idea: ordered, unambiguous instructions.
myths.fact_zh: 愛達・勒芙蕾絲在 1843 年就描述了怎麼替一台機器寫程式，比電子電腦早了大約一百年。程式是一個觀念：照順序、不含糊的指令。

tricks.body_en: The computer does what you wrote, not what you meant.
tricks.body_zh: 電腦做的是你寫的，不是你想的。

tricks.body_en: Three building blocks.
tricks.body_zh: 三種積木。

tricks.body_en: A loop saves writing the same lines again.
tricks.body_zh: 迴圈讓你不必把同樣的幾行再寫一遍。

tricks.body_en: A bug is in the instructions, not in the machine.
tricks.body_zh: bug 在指令裡，不在機器裡。

safety_head.eyebrow: Before You Start · 動手之前

safety.en: For the human robot game, clear the floor first. Mark walls with tape or paper, not with chairs or desks.
safety.zh: 玩真人機器人之前，先把地板清空。牆用膠帶或紙來標示，不要用椅子或桌子。

safety.en: The human robot keeps their eyes open and walks slowly. “Walking into a wall” means stopping at the tape and saying “Bump!”
safety.zh: 當機器人的同學眼睛要張開、慢慢走。「撞牆」的意思是：走到膠帶前停下來，喊一聲「碰！」

safety.en: When a program goes wrong, laugh at the program, not at the person who wrote it or the person who walked it. Every programmer writes bugs.
safety.zh: 程式出錯的時候，笑的是程式，不是寫的人，也不是走的人。每個寫程式的人都會寫出 bug。

safety.en: Use a school or family computer only with permission.
safety.zh: 用學校或家裡的電腦要先得到同意。

materials.en: Tape to mark a grid of 5 by 5 squares on the floor, each big enough to stand in
materials.zh: 膠帶，在地板上貼出 5 × 5 的格子，每格要站得下一個人

materials.en: Sheets of paper for walls, and one for the flag
materials.zh: 幾張紙當作牆，一張當作旗子

materials.en: Cards that say FORWARD, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, REPEAT __ TIMES, and IF WALL AHEAD
materials.zh: 指令卡：FORWARD（前進）、TURN LEFT（左轉）、TURN RIGHT（右轉）、REPEAT __ TIMES（重複 __ 次）、IF WALL AHEAD（如果前面是牆）

steps.en: One student is the robot and waits outside the room. The others lay out walls and a flag, and lay the cards in a row as a program.
steps.zh: 一位同學當機器人，先到教室外面等。其他人擺好牆和旗子，再把指令卡排成一列，當作程式。

steps.en: The robot comes in. A reader reads the cards aloud, one at a time, in English. The robot does exactly what each card says, and nothing else. No one may help or change a card.
steps.zh: 機器人進來。一位同學用英文把卡片一張一張唸出來，機器人完全照卡片做，別的都不做。誰都不可以幫忙，也不可以改卡片。

steps.en: If the robot bumps or misses the flag, find the bug together. Change one card and run the whole program again from the start.
steps.zh: 如果機器人撞牆或沒走到旗子，大家一起找 bug。改一張卡片，再從頭把整個程式跑一次。

steps.en: Now make the program shorter with a REPEAT card. Then move one wall and see whether an IF WALL AHEAD card can make one program work for both rooms.
steps.zh: 接著用 REPEAT 卡把程式變短。然後移動一面牆，看看加上 IF WALL AHEAD 卡，能不能讓同一個程式在兩種房間都走得到。

activities.tip_en: The rule that makes this work is that the robot may not think. Students quickly find how much they leave unsaid when they give instructions. In Taiwan’s junior high Information Technology curriculum, this lesson matches “Program design”: 資 P-IV-1, basic concepts of programming languages, and 資 P-IV-2, structured programming, whose notes list sequence, selection, and repetition.
activities.tip_zh: 這個活動成立的關鍵，是機器人「不可以動腦」。學生很快會發現，自己下指令的時候有多少話沒說出口。對照十二年國教國中「資訊科技」的學習內容，這一課對應「程式設計」主題：資 P-IV-1 程式語言基本概念、功能及應用，以及資 P-IV-2 結構化程式設計（說明列有循序、選擇結構與重複結構）。

materials.en: Squared paper and a pencil for each student
materials.zh: 每人一張方格紙和一枝鉛筆

materials.en: A coin or small counter to be the robot
materials.zh: 一枚硬幣或小棋子，當作機器人

materials.en: The “Write the Program” game on this page, for checking
materials.zh: 這一頁的「換你寫程式」小遊戲，用來對照

steps.en: Draw a 5 by 5 room. Shade three or four squares as walls, mark a start with an arrow, and mark a flag.
steps.zh: 畫一個 5 × 5 的房間。把三、四格塗黑當牆，用箭頭標出起點和面向，再標一面旗子。

steps.en: On another sheet, write a program for your room: one instruction on each line.
steps.zh: 在另一張紙上替你的房間寫一個程式：一行一條指令。

steps.en: Swap rooms and programs with a friend. Move the coin exactly as your friend’s program says. Does it reach the flag?
steps.zh: 和朋友交換房間和程式。完全照朋友的程式移動硬幣。走得到旗子嗎？

steps.en: Count the instructions. Can either of you make your program shorter with a repeat?
steps.zh: 數一數有幾條指令。你們誰能用「重複」把程式變短？

activities.tip_en: If the coin goes wrong, do not explain what you meant. Fix the program on the paper and let your friend run it again. That is debugging. Then play Level 2 on this page and compare: a staircase takes 5 instructions with a repeat.
activities.tip_zh: 硬幣走錯的時候，不要用嘴巴解釋你的意思。把紙上的程式改好，請朋友再跑一次——這就是除錯。接著玩這一頁的第二關比一比：階梯用「重複」只要 5 條指令。

links_head.en: The instructions underneath, a machine that chooses, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 底下的指令、會選擇的機器，以及下一課

links.en: What Happens When You Press a Key?
links.zh: 按下一個鍵，發生了什麼？
links.note_en: The lookup that turned a key into a character was done by a program.
links.note_zh: 把一個鍵查成一個字元的那一步，就是程式做的。

links.en: What Does a Processor Do All Day?
links.note_en: Machine language: the five simple instructions that a program is finally translated into. JUMP is how a loop is made.
links.note_zh: 機器語言：程式最後被翻譯成的那五種簡單指令。迴圈就是用 JUMP 做出來的。

links.en: How Does a Computer Make a Decision?
links.note_en: A question like “is there a wall ahead?” has a yes-or-no answer: one bit. Logic gates are how the machine acts on it.
links.note_zh: 「前面是牆嗎？」這種問題的答案只有是或不是，也就是一個位元。機器靠邏輯閘來根據它行動。

links.en: What Is an Algorithm?
links.note_en: Two programs can do the same job, and one can be far faster. Next: why the method matters.
links.note_zh: 兩個程式可以做同一件事，其中一個卻快得多。下一課：為什麼方法很重要。

lessons.sources_note_en: Facts on this page were checked against these sources (October 2026); the robot and its small language are our own, and every program on the page is tested
lessons.sources_note_zh: 本頁的事實依下列資料查證（2026 年 10 月）；機器人和它的小語言是我們自己設計的，頁面上每一個程式都有測試

sources.en: A computer program is a “detailed plan or procedure for solving a problem with a computer; more specifically, an unambiguous, ordered sequence of computational instructions”; a program is expressed in a computer language and translated, commonly in several stages, into machine language; principal languages include C, Python, and C++; debuggers execute a program piecemeal so the programmer can check whether it is correct
sources.zh: 電腦程式是「用電腦解決問題的詳細計畫或步驟；更明確地說，是一串不含糊、有順序的運算指令」；程式用某種電腦語言寫出，再（通常分幾個階段）翻譯成機器語言；主要的語言有 C、Python、C++；除錯器把程式一小段一小段執行，讓程式設計師檢查對不對
sources.src: The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica, “computer program” (revised by Erik Gregersen)

sources.en: Ada Lovelace translated and annotated Menabrea’s article in 1843; her notes described how the Analytical Engine could be programmed to compute Bernoulli numbers; she has been called the first computer programmer; Babbage built only a small part of the engine; the language Ada was named for her
sources.zh: 愛達・勒芙蕾絲 1843 年翻譯並註解梅納布雷亞的文章；註解描述怎麼替分析機寫程式計算白努利數；她被稱為第一位電腦程式設計師；巴貝奇只造出分析機的一小部分；Ada 語言以她命名
sources.src: The Editors of Encyclopaedia Britannica, “Ada Lovelace”

sources.en: Logo originated in the late 1960s; Seymour Papert and others used it at MIT to teach mathematical thinking to schoolchildren; turtle graphics moved an object with commands such as “left 90” and “forward”; the name came from an early project to program a turtlelike robot
sources.zh: Logo 誕生於 1960 年代後期；派普特等人在麻省理工學院用它教小學生數學思考；海龜繪圖用「left 90」「forward」這類指令移動物件；名字來自早期一個替像海龜的機器人寫程式的計畫
sources.src: David Hemmendinger, “computer programming language,” Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.en: On September 9, 1947, a team reported a moth caught between the relay contacts of the Harvard Mark II; they taped it into the logbook with the words “First actual case of bug being found”; Grace Hopper was present and made the incident famous in her lectures; the term “bug” originated in the 1800s
sources.zh: 1947 年 9 月 9 日，團隊回報一隻飛蛾卡在哈佛馬克二號的繼電器接點之間；他們把牠貼進日誌，寫上「First actual case of bug being found」；葛麗絲・霍普在場，後來在演講中讓這件事出名；bug 這個說法起於 1800 年代
sources.src: Computer History Museum, “This Day in History: September 9”

sources.en: The operators “put out the word that they had debugged the machine”
sources.zh: 操作人員對外說他們替機器「除了蟲」（debugged）
sources.src: U.S. Naval History and Heritage Command, photograph NH 96566-KN, “The First ‘Computer Bug’”

sources.en: 資 P-IV-1, basic concepts, functions, and uses of programming languages; 資 P-IV-2, structured programming: sequence and selection structures, repetition structures (p. 10; notes on p. 42)
sources.zh: 資 P-IV-1 程式語言基本概念、功能及應用；資 P-IV-2 結構化程式設計：循序與選擇結構、重複結構（第 10 頁；附錄三的說明在第 42 頁）
sources.src: 教育部《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校 科技領域》（2018）
sources.url: https://www.naer.edu.tw/upload/1/16/doc/816/十二年國民基本教育課程綱要國民中學暨普通型高級中等學校-科技領域.pdf

sources.en: Taiwan terms: debug 除錯, machine language 機器語言, program 程式, instruction 指令. For loop, this page uses 迴圈, the word in Taiwan’s curriculum (p. 42)
sources.zh: 台灣用語：debug 除錯、machine language 機器語言、program 程式、instruction 指令。loop 本頁用課綱的用詞「迴圈」（第 42 頁）
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《樂詞網》

sources.en: The robot: the staircase takes 15 instructions in order and 5 with a repeat, and both take 15 steps; with one “turn right” missing the robot finishes on another square; the question program reaches the flag in both rooms; all three game levels can be solved, in 5, 5, and 4 instructions; the eight facing answers
sources.zh: 機器人：階梯照順序寫要 15 條指令、用重複要 5 條，兩種都走 15 步；漏掉一條「右轉」機器人停在別的格子；會問問題的程式在兩個房間都走得到旗子；小遊戲三關都解得出來（5、5、4 條指令）；八題面向的答案
sources.src: Our own illustration, checked by tools/computers/test/robot.test.mjs
